News.title: I’ll never speak to him unless it’s to give evidence, Thomas Markle’s son vows after unearthing child sex abuse images
News.content:
Next

THOMAS Markle Snr’s son has vowed never to speak to his father again after claiming to have discovered a grim stash of child sex abuse images.

Horrified Thomas Jnr, 60, told cops he found the sickening pictures in four large boxes at his father’s home in Cebu, the Philippines.



After submitting his sworn statement to child abuse police, Thomas Jnr told The Sun: “When I found this material I was horrified and I had no option but to report my dad.

“I have supported, cared for him and helped him for years — but that stops now.



“I won’t speak to my father ever again unless I’m called to give evidence against him.”

Thomas Jnr, Meghan’s half-brother, reported their father to detectives in the Philippines after making the horrifying find.



Cops investigating the Duchess of Sussex’s estranged dad, 82, were last night preparing to seize the evidence.

Thomas Jnr – the retired TV lighting director’s carer after he suffered a life-threatening stroke in 2022 – had been searching for a phone for his Filipino girlfriend’s father in boxes of Thomas Snr’s belongings.



He told friends he was left a “shaking wreck” when a 15-minute video of naked little girls flashed up on the abandoned LG mobile.

He confided to one: “What I saw made me sick to the stomach — all this stuff was just dumped on me and I didn’t know what to do.

“I knew right away it was highly illegal and would land me in jail for a long time if I didn’t get rid of it. I felt betrayed, angry and disgusted — and realised I had to report him.”

Victims appearing to be aged no older than ten or 11 appeared in sex acts captured on video along with three still pictures of naked and scantily clad girls of about the same age.

Thomas Jnr alleges one of the sick images on the phone was a photo taken of the screen of a Lenovo ThinkPad laptop that was in a room he recognised in his father’s former home in Rosarito, Mexico.



Markle Snr had been forced to leave the house in May and return to the US after suffering a stroke and a blood clot which led to the amputation of his left leg.

But he is alleged to have abandoned the enormous stash of vile content packed into storage boxes.

Thomas Jnr told his pal: “There was an unbelievable amount of stuff — old family home movies on VHS cassettes, books, nine mobile phones, along with the Emmy Awards he won for his TV work.



“But there were also many more worrying items which I’d never seen before — old books that turned out to be full of naked little girls.

“Then the technician helped me turn on the first hard drive and I gasped when all of the icons suddenly appeared.

“His desktop was full of row- upon-row of thumbnail pictures linking to the most sickening child abuse imaginable. The worst of the worst.”

On July 10, Thomas Jnr reported his discovery to the FBI Hotline, the US-based National Centre for Exploited and Missing Children and the state police in Pennsylvania where his father was living.

But his anxiety grew in the weeks that followed as he received no calls or follow-up inquiries — and he decided to steel himself to check the remaining contents.



He retrieved the four large brown cardboard boxes from storage and enlisted the help of a local IT expert to help him access three computer hard drives.

Preschool kids including toddlers either captured nude or engaged in horrifying sex acts were among the files stored on the hard drive.

More images of a man engaged in a sex act with a very young Asian girl appeared to have been stored in the pages of an antique book called “Lewis Carroll Photographs Of Children: Four Nude Studies.”

Another developed film negative showed two more naked schoolgirls.

Other books found in the boxes included lifelong photography enthusiast Thomas Snr’s most treasured family keepsakes and arty picture books.



But innocuous covers featuring tasteful nude pictures of adult women led to page after page of naked little girls in sexual poses on the pages inside.

Further analysis found there were also vile images on the same hard drive as some of the former Hollywood film technician’s work files, including his professional CV.

The document headed “Thomas W Markle” listed his old Hollywood address and phone numbers together with his “Executive Profile, Skill Highlights and Professional Experience”.



Another column of the CV listed his “Core Accomplishments” including three Emmy Awards won for lighting excellence.

The résumé appeared next to another download of daughter Meghan addressing a women’s event at the United Nations on the same hard drive as the child abuse images.

Thomas Snr remains estranged from American former actress Meghan, 45, and has never met her husband Prince Harry, 42.

He claimed he suffered a heart attack shortly before her Windsor Castle wedding in 2018 and did not attend the ceremony.

And he was supported by his son as he begged for years to be allowed to reunite with her after a string of public spats.



Window fitter Thomas Jnr, who moved to a new home a few doors from his father in Cebu in January 2025, even mocked and lampooned Meghan on social media.

But he spectacularly turned on his father yesterday as court papers filed in Cebu City sparked a high-profile police inquiry.

Investigators from the Inter-Agency Council Against Trafficking yesterday appointed a task force run by the specialist Women and Children’s Protection Centre.

The FBI also confirmed receipt of the contents of Thomas Jnr’s affidavit and look certain to conduct their own probe.



A source close to the case in Cebu said last night: “An FBI agent has already requested the contact details of investigators leading the case in the Philippines.

“Thomas Markle Snr is a US citizen, he is currently living in the US and may be linked to alleged offences committed on US soil.

“There is a strong precedent for cases in circumstances like this to be investigated by the FBI.”

Thomas Snr is currently living in a nursing and rehabilitation centre in Florida, where he has been supported by daughter Samantha, 60.



Samantha and Thomas Jnr were the children of his first marriage to secretary Roslyn Loveless, whose 11-year marriage to him ended in 1975. She died in 2024 aged 79.

Meghan was born in 1981 to Thomas Snr’s second wife Doria Ragland, 70, whose eight-year marriage to him ended in 1987.

Cebu City legal sources confirmed yesterday that Thomas Jnr had agreed to surrender the four cardboard boxes of assorted items for detailed forensic examination.

He was due to formally hand over the material while accompanied by a team of lawyers acting on the instruction of the task force of investigators.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The boxes will be taken to Cebu City Department of Justice, where Thomas Jnr was due to sign documents consenting to their detailed forensic examination.



Officers from the specialist Women and Children’s Protection Centre Task Force declined to comment last night.

News.title: Multi-millionaire ex-Starbucks boss ordered to BULLDOZE illegal tennis court & luxury gym after losing planning war
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

BUCKS OFF Multi-millionaire ex-Starbucks boss ordered to BULLDOZE illegal tennis court & luxury gym after losing planning war







Next

A MULTI-MILLIONAIRE ex-Starbucks boss has been ordered to tear-up an illegal tennis court and luxury garden complex after losing a three-year planning battle.

Mark Hepburn, 53, faced a bitter backlash after building the bright blue tennis court, children’s playground, a gym, bar and TV room on the grounds to his six-bedroom pad in Durley, near Southampton.



The garden makeover sparked fury among neighbours, who complained of late-night parties, outdoor discos and glaring lights.

Mr Hepburn bought the property, called Cupressus, for £740,000 in December 2017.



The business mogul then installed artificial grass, timber buildings and a gravel car park, as well as a pen for the family’s pet micro-pigs and flock of alpacas.

But boffins at Winchester City Council ruled the land was agricultural and could not lawfully be used as an extended residential garden.



Mr Hepburn argued previous owners had used it as a garden for years.

However, the dad-of-three was twice refused retrospective planning permission before being served with an enforcement notice.

Neighbours claimed the development had turned their peaceful stretch of countryside into a noisy leisure complex.

Richard Callaway said the work had caused a sharp decline in local wildlife.

Neighbour Rebecca Forest said the household had suffered from “various extremely noisy evening events”.



Suzanne Farr claimed badgers, deer and foxes had been displaced by solid six-foot fences and wire fencing.

She also accused Mr Hepburn of chopping down mature trees and leaving lights on overnight, shining into neighbours’ homes.

Janet Burcombe-Filer said the development had caused a “dramatic reduction in wildlife sightings”.



Mark and Susan Day said their once-picturesque view was now dominated by a “hideous bright blue tennis court”, playground and outbuildings.

They also complained that lights around the swimming pool, court and alpaca shed were often left on all night.

Winchester Council chiefs argued the complex had brought suburban-style leisure facilities into open countryside, damaging its rural character.



Mr Hepburn’s planning agents insisted large gardens were common nearby and claimed the development had no adverse impact on the area.

But planning inspector Morgan Howell rejected their arguments and upheld the council’s enforcement notice.

Mr Hepburn must now remove the tennis court and garden buildings and restore the land to its previous condition within six months.

Mr Hepburn co-founded 23.5 Degrees, the UK’s first independent Starbucks franchise, which controlled 115 outlets before it was sold in October 2014.

The deal was reportedly worth around £140million.



Cllr Jackie Porter, of Winchester City Council, said the ruling confirmed its enforcement action had been “right and justified”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

She added: “Planning enforcement plays an important role in protecting our district to ensure that development is appropriate for Winchester and follows proper planning process.”

The council said it would continue working with Mr Hepburn to ensure the work was completed within the six-month deadline.

PRISON bosses have magicked up a part-time pagan adviser role — just in time for Halloween.

The successful candidate must be of “good standing” in the pre-Christian faith and will oversee the rehabilitation of wicca, druid, and other pagan lags after jail.



Up to 90 per cent of those claiming to follow the old spiritual paths are recently converted, says the Pagan Federation.

Now the Prison and Probation Service is searching for an adviser to help them adapt after jail — and to oversee prisons’ pagan chaplains.

Or, for witches and wizards living in the capital, a pro-rata salary of between £60,518 and £68,357 if offered.

News.title: Urgent warning over common passwords exposed millions of times in data leaks – is yours on the list?
News.content:
Next

SOME 210million people use the foolishly simple password 123456, analysis has revealed.

More than 52million have “password” as their login and 2.5million opt for “computer”, analysis shows.



Football teams are popular — 1,218,040 choosing Chelsea — and bands, with Metallica used by more than a million, a list of exposed passwords shows.

The problem was revealed by insurance firm Alan Boswell Group. It uses data from Have I Been Pwned, a website that tracks passwords worldwide exposed in data breaches.



Spokesman Heath Alexander-Bew said: “Weak passwords can feel like a small issue, but can cause problems very quickly.

“For individuals, it could mean someone accessing shopping accounts, banking apps or social media.



“For a business, it could open the door to invoices, customer details, internal files or password reset links for other platforms.”

He added: “What is worrying is that many passwords are not being guessed.



“They’re sitting in leaked password lists. Criminals can use automated tools to try them across different sites.

“That is why passwords such as ‘123456’, ‘admin’, a football team, a name or a birth year can still be risky, especially when reused across work and personal accounts.”

It comes as UK government departments and companies scramble to patch up a cyber-security flaw in a programming language discovered on Wednesday and said to affect 70 per cent of the internet.

Some government services were taken offline yesterday and gym David Lloyd took its app down to make emergency fixes.

News.title: Healey’s Budget MUST back business and reverse Starmer’s tsunami of tax rises – not inflict more pain
News.content:
Heal economy







Next

BUSINESSES are the job-producing, wealth-creating lifeblood of the economy.

But many on the Left see the private sector as the enemy — grasping exploiters of working people.



This is nonsense. And it’s reassuring John Healey seems to know so.

As he puts the finishing touches to the Budget, the Chancellor says he wants to encourage “bloody-minded” business to boost the UK.



If he’s sincere, it would not be difficult.

He could reverse the tsunami of tax rises imposed by Keir Starmer which have suffocated the economy.

What he must avoid is a repeat of that punishment beating. But business chiefs are sceptical. Half fear the Budget will leave their firms worse off.

Even if Mr Healey genuinely wants to help, the final decision rests with his boss, Andy Burnham.

Who on all the available evidence is a socialist throwback with little love or understanding of the private sector.

Ghost police

LAW and order in Britain has become a sick joke.



The public is fed up with the epidemic of shoplifting, phone snatches, violence and anti-social behaviour.

Labour appears to have surrendered control of the streets to criminals, with cops often nowhere to be seen.

So Kemi Badenoch is right to warn that people now see the police as a “ghost service”.

Her plan, if elected, to put 10,000 extra officers on the beat, looks sound.

On Shabana Mahmood’s watch numbers have actually FALLEN by nearly 2,000. But a hiring spree will achieve little unless more police start deploying common sense.



While many brave bobbies willingly risk their lives in the line of duty, others act with inexplicable callousness – handcuffing 18-year-old student Henry Nowak as he lay dying, for instance.

Officers need reminding their role is catching crooks — not pandering to pernicious wokery.

Woofragettes

EVERYBODY can see Andy Burnham’s Government is going to the dogs…but yesterday the dogs went to the Government.

A pack of greyhounds — wearing Save Our Bets coats — and their owners descended on Parliament to warn against another hike in betting taxes.

If the Budget doubles levies on gaming machines, it will hammer greyhound racing, which depends on the gambling industry for funding.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Local tracks, jobs and opportunities for young people would go. So too would an affordable night out for the working-class communities Labour says it cares so passionately about.

Burnham should ditch this idea — it’s barking mad.

News.title: Who is Thomas Markle? Everything you need to know about Meghan’s father
News.content:
Next

THOMAS Markle is the father of Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex.

Here we take a look at his life, family and controversial relationship with the Royals.

It comes as a Sun world exclusive has revealed Markle’s son told police he has discovered “hundreds, if not thousands” of child sex abuse images at his father’s home.

Markle Snr is now being probed by cops after Markle Jnr claimed he unearthed the horrific pictures and video with family mementos at home in the Philippines.

Who is Thomas Markle?

Thomas Markle is the father of Meghan Markle, the Duchess of Sussex.

He was born on July 18, 1944, in Newport, Pennsylvania, US.

Before becoming related to the Royal Family, he made a name for himself as a lighting director and director of photography on a number of US TV shows.

His resume includes working as a lighting director at WTTW-TV Channel 11 on their programme, Made In Chicago, which won him a Chicago/Midwest Emmy Award for Outstanding Achievement.

Thomas went on to work on the TV series General Hospital and the sitcom Married… With Children.

For his work on General Hospital in 1982 and 2011, Thomas won two Daytime Emmy Awards.

I’m a really loving father and she [Meghan] knows that, and there’s no excuse for treating me this way — no excuse to treat grandparents that way Thomas Markle ,

Thomas’ relationship with his daughter has been difficult for years — the pair have been estranged since her 2018 wedding to Prince Harry.

In September 2023, Thomas renewed pleas to see his grandkids Archie, 4, and Lilibet, 2, on Good Morning Britain.

Speaking live from his California home, Thomas said: “I’m heartbroken. I am very upset.

“This is a cruel thing to do to a grandparent — to deny the right to see a grandchild.”

He added: “In California, I can actually sue to see them but I don’t want to do that.”

Thomas went on to say: “The other thing is I’ve done nothing wrong.

“There’s nothing that points to say I’m a bad guy.

“I’m a really loving father and she knows that, and there’s no excuse for treating me this way — no excuse to treat grandparents that way.”

Was Thomas Markle rushed to the hospital?

Thomas has faced a series of health issues in recent years.

In 2018 he had heart surgery following a heart attack in the run-up to his daughter’s royal wedding, and missed her big day.

Then-Prince Charles took over from Thomas’ duties and walked Meghan down the aisle.

In May 2022, Thomas was rushed to the hospital after suffering from a stroke.

In December 2025, Thomas suffered another medical emergency when a blood clot in his left leg cut off circulation to his foot.

He underwent a life-saving, three-hour operation in the Philippines to amputate his leg below the knee.

In May 2026, Thomas returned to the United States to continue physical therapy and be fitted for a prosthetic limb.

Is Thomas Markle married?

Thomas has been married twice, but following a divorce from his second wife in 1987, he never remarried.

His first marriage, to Roslyn Markle, lasted from 1964 to 1975.

Thomas went on to marry Doria Ragland — Meghan’s mum — in 1979, before an amicable divorce in 1987.

Who are Thomas Markle’s children?

Thomas has three children and seven grandchildren.

Together with his first wife Roslyn, Thomas had two children — Samantha Markle and Thomas Markle Jr.

Samantha was born on November 24, 1964, and is 17 years older than her duchess half-sister.

Samantha is a former actress and model, who lives in Florida.

She has two children from her first marriage to Earl Hale — Ashleigh and Christopher.

Samantha had her third child, daughter Noelle, with her second husband Scott Rasmussen.

Thomas Markle Jr was born on September 17, 1966.

He has reportedly led a quieter life than his sister, living in Oregon and working as a window fitter.

Thomas Jr has two children — Tyler and Thomas Dooley.

With his second wife Doria, Thomas Senior welcomed Meghan on August 4, 1981.

Meghan also has two children with her second husband Prince Harry.

Son Archie was born in the UK on May 6, 2019.

Lilibet Diana arrived two years later after the couple relocated to the US.

Her date of birth is June 4, 2021.

Meghan was previously married to Trevor Engelson, from 2011 until 2014.

News.title: Prepare for supply chain disruption from cyber or climate emergencies, Streeting warns public
News.content:
Members of the public and businesses need to think more about how they would cope with natural disasters, cyber-attacks or state-sponsored terrorism, the defence secretary has said.

Wes Streeting warned people needed to be more aware of emerging risks facing the UK and make plans to deal with them.

He added that the government was launching a "national resilience conversation" to raise awareness, including advice for households like stocking up on food, bottled water and first aid supplies.

Streeting also said that cyber incidents - like the recently discovered critical security flaw in the programming language which powers much of the internet - will happen "more and more".

Streeting told BBC One's Question Time that the UK is facing a greater threat to the country, "than we have certainly for most, if not all, of my lifetime".

Speaking to an audience at the UK Gun Hall Plant in Telford earlier on Thursday, where it was announced production of tank gun barrels would return to the UK, he spoke of "everyday challenges" facing households.

He pointed to wildfires burning this summer and the flooding that is expected this winter.

Streeting said the public need to be prepared for "increasingly sophisticated cyber-attacks" on businesses, or supply chain disruption caused by "hostile state actors or terrorists".

The defence secretary referenced the critical security flaw in the PHP programming language which has left organisations around the world scrambling to update their systems.

In the UK, 32 government services were offline while the potential cyber-security issues were addressed.

"It's not just from foreign states engaged in espionage or sabotage; it's also organised criminals," Streeting told Question Time.

"In this world of AI that we live in... it does also present threats if people are innovating and pushing against conventional [cyber] defences."

News.title: Raye wins the Mercury Prize with This Music May Contain Hope
News.content:
Raye has won the 2026 Mercury Prize for her show-stopping second album This Music May Contain Hope.

A pop record sprinkled with golden age Hollywood glamour, it beat the likes of Sir Paul McCartney, Olivia Dean and Jade to scoop the Â£25,000 prize.

"I couldn't tell you how grateful I am to be holding this," said Raye, clutching her trophy at Newcastle's Utilita Arena. "I'm shaking, I'm jet-lagged, I'm tired. It's all blurry."

It is the first time a pop album has won the coveted prize - which recognises the best British or Irish album of the last 12 months - since M People's Elegant Slumming in 1994.

Speaking to the BBC afterwards, Raye said she'd "poured everything I had" into the record, which features the global hit song Where Is My Husband?

"I made this album not focusing on commercial [success], not focusing on making things cookie-cutter," said the 28-year-old.

"Some of these songs are seven minutes. They're indulgent. They're maximalist."

Across 17 tracks and 73 minutes, the record tells a cinematic story about a relationship that ends in tears on the rainy streets of Paris, then follows our plucky heroine as she dusts off the debris and emerges stronger and more resilient.

Along the way, it features both of her grandparents, the soul legend Al Green, four separate orchestras and more than 100 musicians.

News.title: Celebrity Traitors - paranoia deepens as traitor behaviour splits opinion
News.content:
Once the croissant crumbs had been cleared, it was time for a mission that threw the cat among the pigeons - not least because the traitor's lair it took place in "smelled like a litter tray", according to Jerry.

Miranda felt there were more complex olfactory notes at play: "A mix of salmon, cheap cologne and crotch." Delightful.

The mission involved each player having to build a shield on a plinth in front of them out of 3D jigsaw-type pieces which were buried in troughs in sawdust. Think Krypton Factor meets lucky dip.

At three intervals, a bell would ring, and the players all had to stop and put on blindfolds for a few minutes. The traitors could then remove theirs and go about sabotaging the handiwork of anyone they fancied.

And while James A revealed he was "starting to have more fun" after murdering poor Ross, if there was a prize for the worst traitor of all time, he would still smash it.

He was too scared to take off his blindfold and remove any shield pieces from the faithfuls, leaving the dirty work - and all the risk - to fellow traitors Maya Jama and King Kenny. Suffice to say, they were not impressed.

"He didn't even lift the blindfold off - I'm speechless," said Maya.

James A knew he was in trouble: "I'm aware I'll get a dressing down in the turret but I am the one who killed Grant Mitchell."

He wasn't wrong about the telling off. And the fact he completed his own puzzle, earning himself a shield, must have really riled his co-conspirators.

To be fair, you could argue he's playing a blinder - there's been very little suspicion of him so far.

Three other celebrities also managed to complete their shield puzzles - James B, Joanne McNall and Michael Sheen - but no money was banked after Maya and Kenny panicked and didn't remove any pieces at their last opportunity.

But the task at least threw up another bunch of mad theories for the faithfuls to chew over, as they tried to unsuccessfully guess where the floorboard creaking was coming from as two of the traitors tried to creep around the room.

It was good news for Romesh at least, whose hay fever saved the day - Sharon Rooney could hear him sniffing constantly next to her so knew he couldn't have been a traitor.

Maybe the tickly moustache isn't helping his allergies - and combing it won't make much difference.

News.title: Russell Brand accuser said alleged rape 'really hurt', court hears

The friend of a woman claiming to have been raped by Russell Brand told a jury the complainant had told her after the alleged attack that it had "really, really hurt".

The witness who spoke via video link at his trial said she had attended the Hammersmith Apollo theatre in London with the alleged victim in 2009, where they had been invited to the defendant's dressing room after his comedy show.

Statements from the woman's parents were also heard in court, saying their daughter had told them about the alleged attack, and that she had been "very worried about HIV".

Brand, 51, has pleaded not guilty to all seven charges in the trial - three counts of rape, three charges of sexual assault and one of indecent assault.

The allegations span a 10-year period from 1999 to 2009 and involve six female complainants.

The witness said the woman had told her she had visited Brand's house in London soon after meeting at the theatre, and that he then sent a car to collect the woman, which took her to his place in Hampstead.

She said when they spoke about it "quite soon after", she said she "was just crying - really upset".

The witness said Brand had forced her into having anal sex at the end of an encounter that started off consensually.

"He was quite aggressive," she said her friend had told her.

"He forcibly put it in my bum and "it really really hurt".

The witness says she remembers specifically asking the complainant if she had said no to Brand when the alleged attack started.

News.title: Prince William makes surprise appearance on Graham Norton Show
News.content:
The Prince of Wales has made a surprise appearance on the Graham Norton Show, as part of a special edition to mark the Earthshot Prize.

During the episode, which airs on Friday, he joined Cate Blanchett, Robert Irwin and Hannah Waddingham, who are all involved with the prize.

As Norton spoke about the initiative with the trio he surprised the audience by then inviting the prince out to join them on the sofa.

They discussed the need to pair optimism and urgency when tackling climate change. The prize was founded by William to "celebrate and scale the solutions that will repair our planet".

The guests also chatted about William's long-time support for Aston Villa, and his love of Christopher Nolan films.

William set up the Earthshot Prize in 2020, drawing inspiration from US President John F Kennedy's Moonshot project, which challenged scientists to get astronauts to the Moon and back safely.

There are five Earthshots, or goals, for which an award is given: Protect and Restore Nature, Clean Our Air, Revive Our Oceans, Build a Waste-Free World and Fix Our Climate. Each winner receives Â£1m.

The future king has committed himself to the prize until 2030. This year's winners will be announced at a ceremony in Mumbai in November.

Last year, the ceremony for the prizes drew famous faces such as former Formula 1 driver Sebastian Vettel and then-UK prime minister Keir Starmer. Pop stars Kylie Minogue and Shawn Mendes performed at the ceremony in Rio de Janeiro.

The 2025 winners included Lagos Fashion Week, for "transforming one of the world's most wasteful industries" by requiring designers to demonstrate their commitment to sustainability.

At last year's ceremony, William said the winners were "proof that progress is possible".

The Graham Norton Show is on BBC One at 22.40 Friday.

News.title: Items recovered in search for missing fishing boat and crew
News.content:
Items belonging to a fishing boat that vanished off the north coast of the Isle of Lewis last week have been recovered as the search for the vessel and two missing crew members continues.

Norman "Tam" Murray, 40 and Murdo Morrison, 23, were on board the Kilda when it disappeared on 13 October.

The body of crewmate Douglas Craigie, 49, was recovered from the sea in the early hours of the following morning by rescuers.

On Thursday, police confirmed that items belonging to the vessel had been recovered from what was described as "an area of interest" off the coast near Port of Ness.

The search was carried out by Police Scotland's marine and dive unit and partners.

A Marine Accident Investigation Branch (MAIB) exclusion zone has been in place for divers and vessels in an area between the Butt of Lewis and Port of Ness, but this will be lifted from 23:59 on Thursday.

Insp Neil Taylor, local area inspector for the Western Isles, said the search was a "complex operation" and asked for officers to be given "time and space" to carry out inquiries.

He said: "Efforts are continuing to work with partners and we are doing everything we can to get answers.

"While the Marine Accident Investigation Branch (MAIB) exclusion zone will be lifted tonight, we would urge people not to put themselves at any risk.

"Please do not attempt to carry out searches in areas which put you at risk of harm."

A GoFundMe for the families affected by the event has raised more than Â£148,000, against a target of Â£110,000.

News.title: Woman charged after police officer injured in shooting
News.content:
A 27-year-old woman has been charged after a police officer was shot in Nottingham city centre.

Nottinghamshire Police said the officer was shot in the foot after he approached a man and a woman at a bus stop in Angel Row shortly before 04:50 BST on Sunday.

The male officer remains in hospital receiving treatment, the force added.

Aisha Zaman, of Collison Street, Hyson Green, has been charged with possession of a prohibited firearm and possession of that firearm with intent to commit an indictable offence.

Police said the charge came after "consultation with the Crown Prosecution Service".

Zaman has been remanded into custody and will appear before Nottingham Magistrates' Court on Friday, police added.

Several other people have been arrested in connection with the incident, including two men, 24 and 30, and two women, 25 and 21, who have been arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender.

A 35-year-old man and a 33-year-old woman have also been arrested on suspicion of possession of a firearm with intent to endanger life and assisting an offender. Both remain in police custody.

Det Ch Supt Rich Bull, who is leading the investigation, said the "outpouring of support" for the officer had been "greatly appreciated".

"We would just like to take this moment to thank the public", he added.

"We continue to support him as he undergoes further treatment in hospital and keeping him and his family fully informed of the developments in this investigation."

He said officers were "still following a number of lines of inquiry", and anyone with information has been asked to contact the force.

News.title: Two storms in two days as Austen and Boelo head for UK
News.content:
Gusts of wind will widely reach 60-70mph, and perhaps 80mph in exposed locations.

Winds of this strength will blow some trees over, bringing a significant risk of transport disruption and there may also be some power cuts.

Some buildings could potentially be damaged by the strongest winds, leading to a risk of flying debris at the height of the storm.

Yellow wind warnings cover most of England and Wales with gusts of wind on Friday forecast to reach 45-60mph, with 70mph gusts likely in some places.

As strong as these winds are, the most damaging winds will run to the south of the low pressure centre.

That puts north-west France firmly in the firing line and parts of Brittany could see gusts close to 90mph.

The Channel Islands are also expecting severe gales with gusts up to 80mph.

All schools have been told to close on Friday because of the high winds predicted to be caused by Storm Austen, the Government of Jersey has said.

Heavy rain in Scotland may cause some localised flooding with a Met Office yellow warning for 20-40mm of rain forecast with up to 80mm accumulating in a few areas through Friday.

News.title: Barclays cutting 5,000 jobs as it increases reliance on AI
News.content:
Barclays is cutting around 5,000 staff as it introduces more artificial intelligence (AI) into its work processes.

The banking group said 1,000 posts had already been closed and it expects a further reduction of 4,000 to be complete by the end of this year, amounting to around 5% of its global workforce.

The bank's cost reductions are focused on its UK retail bank, but some back office functions for the UK are done in India, where a significant proportion of the job cuts are expected to fall.

Barclays said the changes were the result of an ongoing modernisation plan, with the use of AI being the "icing on the cake" of its strategy.

Although not all of the cuts are due to AI, their scale will prompt further concern over the impact of the new technology.

Company spending on AI is increasing along with claims new tools can replace some of the basic tasks currently done by staff such as administrative and programming work.

HSBC, Standard Chartered and Danske Bank have also flagged AI-related job cuts this year.

"It is a hot button topic," said AJ Bell investment analyst, Russ Mould.

However, banks had not yet made big moves towards the widespread introduction of AI and they would be considering the implications for security and customer service before implementing AI technology to make financial savings, he said.

"Any company at any time needs to keep on top of its cost base," he said.

"It will be intriguing to see what other banks say in their results in the coming weeks.

Sharon Graham, general secretary of the Unite union that represents banking sector workers said the company was "using AI as an excuse to discard its loyal and long-suffering workforce".

"Employers should be focussed on upgrading employees' skills so that they remain employed as new technology changes the workplace. Instead, Barclays is guilty of taking a short-term, kneejerk approach," she said.

Barclays is reaching the end of a three year cost-cutting programme focused primarily on its UK retail banking arm, although the investment banking division is also affected.

AJ Bell's Russ Mould said despite "reaching for the AI lever" Barclays had failed to match expectations with its financial results.

Barclays also revealed it made Â£2.3bn profit in the three months to September, higher than the same period a year ago, but slightly less than forecast.

Barclays Group chief executive CS Venkatakrishnan said the job cuts were the result of significant investment it is making in technology to simplify and improve its business.

"AI has an important role to play and may have a more important role to play in the future.

"We will employ the AI at scale," he said. "But AI is the icing on the cake not the cake.

"Because you need to do the infrastructure build to get the benefits of AI."

Barclays said around 60% of the job cuts will fall within its support functions, including among developers.

Will Howlett, financials analyst at Quilter Cheviot said the cuts illustrated "how significantly AI and automation could reshape the banking industry over the next few years".

"Banks have spent heavily on technology for years, but we are increasingly reaching the point where that investment translates into fewer people being required to run the business," he said.

Barclays said it expects its efficiency measures to deliver a further Â£1.1bn of savings in 2027.

News.title: Tommy Robinson hired detectives to find journalists, court told
News.content:
Political activist Tommy Robinson has told a court he hired private detectives to track down and photograph two reporters to "put pressure" on them.

The 43-year-old from Bedfordshire, real name Stephen Yaxley-Lennon, told Southwark Crown Court he was "shocked and scared" when the Daily Mail published a story accusing him of "stoking race riots from his sunbed".

He has denied two charges of harassment causing fear of violence to reporters Andrew Young and Jacob Dirnhuber after the 2024 Southport attacks.

Robinson is accused of writing posts on X, sending direct messages and making phone calls that made the two journalists fear the risk of vigilante attacks.

He denied wanting to expose the journalists to threats of violence, and said he felt his actions were "totally reasonable... under the circumstances".

News.title: Lockerbie bombing accused loses bid to have case thrown out
News.content:
She referred to a longstanding American legal doctrine, which stipulates that a court's right to hold a trial is not impaired if the suspect has been the subject of a forceful abduction.

"This rule rests on the principle that due process of law is satisfied when one present in court is convicted of a crime after a fair trial and in accordance with constitutional procedural safeguards," said the judge.

"Put differently, there's nothing in the Constitution that requires a court to permit a guilty person rightfully convicted to escape justice because he was brought to trial against his will."

In her ruling, the judge said there were two exceptions to that doctrine.

One would apply if Marimi had been brought before the court through the US government's "deliberate, unnecessary and unreasonable invasion" of his constitutional rights.

For that exception to be triggered, the challenged conduct had to be carried out by, or at the direction of, US officials.

The judge said Marimi's allegations "at best suggest that US government officials exerted pressure on Libyan officials to facilitate a rendition, not that US government officials directed or controlled the challenged conduct."

The second exception to the doctrine would apply if the US government had violated an extradition agreement which was the only way a suspect could be transferred between the two countries.

The judge said the US government had invoked two conventions to secure Marimi's appearance in a US court.

News.title: Map thief leads 'merry dance' with return promises
News.content:
Defence barrister Jessica Flain said West had partly paid a man to restore the map, but he would not hand it back until the full fee was settled. She asked for sentencing to be adjourned for seven days so a friend could pay the balance and West could take the map to Charing Cross Police Station.

Judge Charlotte Welsh refused, saying she did "not believe a word of it".

She said West had told the court in June that he could return the map within seven days, and in August that it was with a friend and he would retrieve it once he had recovered from heart surgery.

"Again, that appears to have been a lie," she said. "You were charged in February. You have had eight months to return the map."

The judge said she believed West had a buyer in mind and had stolen the map "to order".

The court heard he had 27 convictions for 107 offences in the UK and abroad, mostly for dishonesty and including 41 thefts. They included a burglary conviction in Hungary in 2011 and a theft conviction in France in 2013, and he had also been convicted under various identities.

Flain said West, a father of two, was "ashamed and embarrassed" and had been in debt and unable to meet basic living costs. She described the offence as "a short-term, pressured decision by an elderly man living in difficult circumstances".

Judge Welsh said the map was of "international cultural significance" and the damage had "permanently diminished what can be learned from it". The court was told the two digital copies of the atlas are incomplete.

West was jailed for three years for criminal damage, with concurrent sentences of 16 months for theft and six months for possessing a bladed article. The judge refused to suspend the sentence, saying immediate custody was needed "to deter other people from doing precisely what you have".
