ALEJANDRO GARNACHO froze during Aston Villa’s warm-up and was caught on camera watching former club Manchester United getting battered by Como from the big screen at Villa Park.

Garnacho, 22, left United for Chelsea in 2025 after five years at Old Trafford that led to a hapless ending, marred by a dramatic dip in form.



However, the winger hasn’t forgotten about his former club it seems as he kept tabs on them while he was in action with his new team Villa, where he moved on loan from the Blues last summer.

The Argentina international was on Unai Emery‘s bench during the Villans’ Champions League clash with Viking on Wednesday.



And a camera caught Garnacho pausing his half-time warm-up as the big screen showed highlights of Man Utd’s heavy 4-1 defeat at Como earlier that night.

Fans were left in stitches with that sight and immediately stormed social media.



One supporter tweeted: “Anyone else see Garnacho pause at HT to watch United get battered?”

Another commented: “Now he’s at Villa Park…”

A third wrote: “It’s all good.”

This fan said: “Bruv, the way Garnacho froze mid-warm-up after seeing Como vs Man Utd scoreline…”



That one added: “Hilarious.”

And a comment read: “LMAO.”

Garnacho came on for Villa in the second half and helped the hosts pick up a 3-1 victory.

That was the Premier League giants’ third Champions League win in a row that places them joint-top of the League Phase table.

Sports.title: Shocking state of seven abandoned stadiums left as derelict ghost grounds including 100,000-capacity building site
Sports.content:
Next

FOOTBALL STADIUMS are a thing of beauty for us at SunSport.

In Great Britain we are blessed with some of the best stadia in the world – and they keep getting better across the land.



However, sometimes when it’s out with the old and in with the new, or clubs run into financial ruin, the homes of many teams get left abandoned.

So, we’ve rounded up those that are now derelict and left to ruins that are still standing.



They really are a sight for sore eyes…

Milmoor, Rotherham, England

Rotherham left Millmoor in 2008 after then-new owner Tony Stewart failed to agree a deal with controversial previous custodian Ken Booth.

As the Millers moved to Sheffield’s Don Valley Stadium, and then the swanky New York Stadium four years later, Millmoor was largely allowed to rot.

The club had been halfway through a redevelopment of the ground’s main stand before running into significant financial issues – work that would never finish.

In 2024, following a cash injection by Ken Booth Jr, Millmoor was partially restored and opened its doors to junior teams.

A year later, the historic ground, which once housed 25,170 fans, became the new home of former WSL side Doncaster Belles – marking the return of regular senior football to Millmoor for the first time since 2008.



It wasn’t to last, however, as the Booth family business went into administration earlier this year.

Millmoor was subsequently bought by the Ron Hull Group, who opted to demolish the ground.



One proposal is for a 2000-seater women’s stadium to be constructed in the location where Millmoor once stood.

Donbass Arena, Donetsk, Ukraine

Recent viral videos have shown how shocking the once beautiful home of Shakhtar Donetsk is now.

The club was forced to flee the region due to the initial outbreak of conflict in 2014.

They have never returned to their £300million home, which is sadly war-damaged, and overgrown with weeds.

The outer glass facade has suffered extensive damage from multiple shelling incidents over the years.



Without groundskeepers or maintenance, the structural surroundings and the pitch itself have been completely overtaken by wild vegetation.

Shakhtar have been operating in exile, playing their domestic home matches at the Arena Lviv in Ukraine and European matches at Stamford Bridge.

Stadio Sant’Elia, Sardinia, Italy

Italia ‘90 still holds a place in the hearts of football fans across the world – but one of the iconic tournament’s former stadiums now lies in ruins.



The Stadio Sant’Elia once seated 60,000 and played host to all three of England’s group matches 36 years ago.

Today, it’s been left to rot after Cagliari abandoned it in 2017 due to a risk staff could be electrocuted.

The derelict stands are still in place, although they are now covered in dust and debris.



Outside, there are piles of seats littered everywhere along with scaffolding poles.

A set of goal posts still remain where the pitch once stood, but instead of the grass, huge weeds now stand where the turf used to be.

Stadio Flaminio, Rome, Italy

Designed by the legendary architect Pier Luigi Nervi and his son Antonio for the 1960 Rome Olympics, the Flaminio hosted Roma and Lazio matches, and was a base for Italy rugby team’s Six Nations matches.

It also featured concerts by the likes of U2 and Michael Jackson.

However, it was gradually abandoned after the Italian Rugby Federation relocated its Six Nations matches to the larger Stadio Olimpico in 2012, compounded by failed redevelopment plans and chronic municipal neglect.



Promised modernisation and maintenance projects repeatedly stalled due to bureaucratic delays and funding issues.

However, there is light at the end of the tunnel.

This week, it was claimed in the Italian press that Lazio president Claudio Lotito has reached an agreement with a state committee entrusted with preserving the country’s cultural heritage to redevelop the stadium.



Lazio are planning to have the stadium ready for 2030.

Guangzhou Football Park, Guangzhou, China

Thankfully, this brilliant arena’s development is back on track too.

But, in 2021 the Evergrande Group defaulted on its massive debts and the development of their 100,000 capacity stadium was halted.

The site sat half-finished and empty, as the original tenant, Guangzhou FC, completely collapsed and were banned from competition by the Chinese FA.

However, the local government stepped in and seized the facility to prevent it from becoming a permanent “ghost stadium”.



The plan is to downgrade the capacity to a more manageable 74,000.

Workers are aiming to complete the stadium by 2028.

Stadion Za Lužánkami, Brno, Czechia

One of Europe’s most famous abandoned stadiums, the 50,000 capacity Stadion Za Lužánkami became completely derelict after being shuttered in 2001.



Soon, nature aggressively reclaimed the concrete bowls, transforming the former terraces into a dense forest of trees and bushes.

Opened in 1953, it served as the iconic home of FC Zbrojovka Brno. It still holds the record for the highest attendance in Czech top-flight football history, drawing over 44,000 fans to a match in 1996.

However, it was closed because it failed to meet modern FIFA and Czech FA structural safety criteria, forcing the club to move out.

Last month, Brno city councillors cancelled the concession proceedings for the sale of the land at Za Lužánkami.



This decision followed disagreements over property valuation and complications regarding zoning plans and maximum height limits for a new stadium.

Cathkin Park, Glasgow, Scotland

Another famous “ghost stadium”, Cathkin Park was home to Third Lanark A.C., one of the founding members of the Scottish Football League, who went bankrupt in 1967.

Today, the park is unique because the original terracing and concrete stands from the stadium still remain on three sides of the pitch, slowly being reclaimed by trees and nature.

The ground holds a deeply significant place in Scottish football history, having hosted major clubs, cup finals, and international fixtures between Scotland and England.



Maintained by the Glasgow City Council’s parks department, Cathkin Park functions as a public green space.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Visitors can still walk along the concrete steps where tens of thousands of fans once stood.

It is a popular pilgrimage site for football purists, groundhoppers, and historians looking to experience the haunting atmosphere of a lost era.

Sports.title: Man Utd decide on Bruno Fernandes punishment after 'disgraceful' TV interview
Sports.content:
Man Utd decide on Bruno Fernandes punishment after 'disgraceful' TV interview

Manchester United have made a decision on whether to discipline Bruno Fernandes for his public criticism of Michael Carrick after being battered 4-1 by Como in the Champions League

View 2 Images Bruno Fernandes will continue to captain Manchester United (Image: Ash Donelon, Manchester United via Getty Images)

Bruno Fernandes will stay as Manchester United captain and is unlikely to be disciplined despite publicly criticising Michael Carrick following their Champions League defeat to Como. United's skipper challenged the United head coach and his backroom team over their tactical decisions in his post-match interview.

‌



‌



Fernandes claimed that the players were instructed against pressing their opponents man-to-man, rather than not carrying out orders. He called on the coaches to show greater courage under pressure by adopting a higher pressing game.

‌



The captain believes United allowed Como to build momentum. Fernandes said they had too much room to exploit the flanks.

‌



Mirror Football understands Fernandes is unlikely to face any sanctions whatsoever. However, there is internal disappointment with the Portugal international's remarks.

Michael Carrick given Man Utd sack verdict as Red Devils confirm decision READ MORE :

That is balanced, though, by a broader acknowledgement that the anger and frustration he voiced were understandable given the nature of the defeat. United found themselves trailing 1-0 inside two minutes.

‌



Speaking to TNT Sports following the 4-1 loss on Wednesday evening, Fernandes delivered an interview described as 'disgraceful' by pundit Jamie Carragher. He said: "It's not the first time, we started on the wrong foot, and they scored very early. Not much pressure on the ball, not many good movements with the ball, not many things going our way.

"Conceding early makes us go into game with a mood of defeat, it's difficult to get out of that, trying to be brave, to have the ball and make something happen. If we are not able to do that, it is going to be very difficult to get out of this situation."

‌

View 2 Images Bruno Fernandes gave a bombshell interview (Image: HBO Max)

‌



Fernandes then chose to shift his attention towards the dugout, saying: "It's a decision from the staff to not press man to man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence."

When questioned whether Carrick had got his tactics wrong, Fernandes didn't hold back, replying: "That's on the manager and staff to see, not me. Sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of pressing high and making them uncomfortable.

‌



"As you saw with them [Como], the centre-back was coming to mark me in my own half. We need to do that as a team, but we were unable to.

‌



"A team that plays through the middle with small connections, if you give them too much time and space then they can hurt you out wide."

Responding to those comments, Carrick said: "We actually half-pressed man-to-man the second half and then conceded a goal from that. And there's a little bit on whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don't run, and you don't run forward, and you don't run back, you ain't going to win."

Sports.title: Bruno Guimaraes hails 'unbelievable' Arsenal team-mate who starred in Bayern Munich clash
Sports.content:
Bruno Guimaraes hails 'unbelievable' Arsenal team-mate who starred in Bayern Munich clash

Bruno Guimaraes got his first taste of a high-profile Champions League match since joining Arsenal as the Gunners played out an exciting 2-2 draw away to Bayern Munich

View 2 Images Bruno Guimaraes is enjoying life at Arsenal (Image: Harry Langer/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images)

Bruno Guimaraes heaped praise on 'unbelievable' Declan Rice after he inspired Arsenal's late comeback against Bayern Munich. Gunners midfielder Rice scored an 82nd-minute equaliser at the Allianz Arena to snatch a 2-2 draw and maintain Arsenal's unbeaten start in the Champions League.

‌



‌



The England international has formed a solid partnership with Guimaraes since the latter joined Arsenal from Newcastle in a £75million move, and the Brazilian is loving playing alongside him. "He's so good, he's an unbelievable player, unbelievable guy," Guimaraes said post-match.

‌



"He's trying to help me a lot since my first day in the club. I think he can play like me as a six, as an eight, as a 10, everywhere in the midfield. I think the manager is still trying to get the best version of ourselves.

‌



"Today, I played more as a six, he plays more as an 8. I enjoy a lot playing with him, with Martin [Odegaard] as well, a top player, so good with the ball. The pass from him here today for [Eberechi] Eze was an unbelievable pass. I think we've had a good run so far, we've been enjoying playing with each other."

Sports.title: 'I knew Man Utd were sacking me at half-time before I apologised like Michael Carrick'
Sports.content:
'I knew Man Utd were sacking me at half-time before I apologised like Michael Carrick'

Former Manchester United manager Ole Gunnar Solskjaer reflected on when he knew his reign was coming to an end

View 2 Images Former Manchester United manager Ole Gunnar Solskjaer reflected on the end of his reign at the club (Image: Glyn KIRK / AFP via Getty Images)

Ole Gunnar Solskjaer knew his time as Manchester United manager was over at half-time during his final match as boss. While Michael Carrick is expected to remain in charge for United’s next game after their dismal defeat by Como, Solskjaer was aware that his reign was over as the club headed to a 4-1 loss against Watford in November 2021.

‌



‌



The former United striker was in charge of the Red Devils for almost three years. Similar to Carrick, the 53-year-old was initially a temporary fix before being appointed manager permanently.

‌



Last season, Carrick enjoyed success as he guided United to third in the table, but his tenure hit a low on Wednesday with a humbling 4-1 defeat by Como in the Champions League. The United boss has won just two of 11 games so far this term and his side are winless in seven.

‌



The 45-year-old apologetically raised his hands to travelling United supporters after full-time in Como. Despite the defeat, Carrick is set to take charge against Bournemouth on Sunday. However, Solskjaer knew he would not be given a similar reprieve after seeing his side fall short for the first 45 minutes against Watford in 2021, with United 2-0 down at the interval.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



“Nobody told me, but I knew at half-time against Watford,” United icon Solskjaer recalled to The Athletic in 2023. “We didn’t look like a Man United team; the players weren’t running for each other.

“At half-time, I told the players it was probably going to be the last time we worked together and to play with pride. We almost turned it around, until Harry Maguire got sent off.”

‌



In the immediate aftermath, Solskjaer was quick to apologise to United supporters for his team’s display. "I feel for the fans. I feel the same as the fans,” he said at the time. “We’re embarrassed losing the way we do. We are in a very bad run and bad situation. But that is part of football.

“I know they will support the team and the players on the pitch every single day. Sometimes you have to say sorry and that was a sorry for the performance.”

‌



View 2 Images United boss Michael Carrick worked alongside Solskjaer during his tenure (Image: Clive Brunskill/Getty Images)

Solskjaer was sacked by United the day after his team’s 4-1 defeat at Vicarage Road. Carrick, who was part of the Norwegian’s coaching staff throughout his reign, sent a similar message to supporters as he reeled from the loss to Como.

‌



“I have to apologise to the supporters,” Carrick said. “I went over to the end and I care about this football club as much as anyone, if not more, with the position that I'm in and what I value this football club. For us to play in that way, it's not acceptable. It wasn't a good performance at all.”

The United boss added: “We might win, we might lose, but the way we went about it tonight, I wouldn't say everyone, but the way we went about it in some ways tonight wasn't acceptable. And I just wanted to let the fans know that I feel for them, for sure.”

Article continues below

Carrick will hope his side can produce a positive response against Bournemouth as his job comes under increasing scrutiny. United will aim to end their winless run on Sunday, with the club preparing to host the Cherries at Old Trafford.

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes urges Man Utd to 'stop living in the past' in fresh damning interview
Sports.content:
Bruno Fernandes urges Man Utd to 'stop living in the past' in fresh damning interview

Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes broke ranks to send a clear message to his team-mates and the club hierarchy after the shambolic 4-1 defeat by Como in the Champions League

View 3 Images Bruno Fernandes had some alarming words post-match (Image: Getty Images)

Bruno Fernandes has accused others at Manchester United of living in the past in a second eye-catching interview after the dismal defeat by Como.

‌



‌



Fernandes' words added fuel to the fire after United were thrashed 4-1 in northern Italy on Wednesday night. Speaking to TNT Sports, the United captain openly questioned Michael Carrick's tactics, piling pressure onto the manager just 11 games into the season.

‌



While the United hierarchy are not about to pull the trigger on Carrick just months after handing him the job on a permanent basis, his position is far from safe. Director of recruitment Christopher Vivell is understood to be pushing for the appointment of Julian Nagelsmann if United sack Carrick, who desperately needs a win against Bournemouth on Sunday.

‌



And the bullish words of Fernandes won't help the perception that not everyone at the club are pulling in the same direction. Speaking to Sky Sports Italy, the midfielder spoke his mind.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Michael Carrick given Man Utd sack verdict as Red Devils confirm decision READ MORE :

Julian Nagelsmann gives Man Utd green light as Michael Carrick replacement identified READ MORE :

“Everyone at the club must understand that it’s no longer the same,” Fernandes said. “We’re no longer in the past and we must look to the future. We must create something different in the present.

‌



“At this club, we focus too much on what was achieved in the past, but we are no longer the same. The club and the players must understand this.

“Unfortunately for us, especially the players, those who come think about winning trophies, matches, and reaching the highest level, but unfortunately it’s been very difficult at this club in recent years. That’s the situation.”

‌



View 3 Images Michael Carrick is clinging onto his job (Image: Stefano Guidi/Getty Images)

Intriguingly, Sky Sports Italy reporter Pierluigi Bagnulo said that Fernandes was not allowed by the club to conduct the fiery interview in Italian, despite speaking the language fluently following time spent in his early career at Novara, Sampdoria and Udinese.

‌



“It’s a very difficult moment for us, we’re not getting the points and results we want," Fernandes added. “The most important thing is that we’re not performing as we expect.

"Unfortunately, it’s one of those moments where it seems like we can’t get out of it. We have to do something to change this situation and start winning because it’s important.”

‌



View 3 Images Bruno Fernandes spoke openly about his frustrations post-match (Image: PIERO CRUCIATTI, AFP via Getty Images)

Carrick raised eyebrows by replacing Fernandes with Joshua Zirkzee in the second half in Como. “Nobody likes to leave the pitch, especially with a result like that," the United captain said when asked about the decision.

‌



“It was a very difficult match for us, it was almost impossible to play with the ball, we weren’t close enough to maintain possession and play in their half.

“Como were very brave in their man-to-man pressing, we never did that and we gave them too many opportunities to play between our lines, thus managing to create chances to score.”

‌



United have won just two matches this season, against newly promoted Ipswich and Champions League minnows Sabah. They host Bournemouth in the Premier League on Sunday before travelling to Chelsea the following weekend.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick given Man Utd sack verdict as Red Devils confirm decision
Sports.content:
A majority of fans have decided that Manchester United should sack Michael Carrick - but they won't get their wish for now. Carrick, 45, hit a new low on Wednesday as he watched his side produce an abject display and lose 4-1 away to Champions League debutants Como.

It's now seven games without a win for United, who've already been knocked out of the Carabao Cup and are languishing 13th in the Premier League table after a dreadful start to the season. Their woeful form is a stark contrast to the winning run that they enjoyed during Carrick's spell as interim manager last term.

Wednesday's result plunged his future into doubt and it was unknown whether he'd be in charge for Sunday's home match against Bournemouth. It's now been confirmed that Carrick will hold his pre-match press conference as usual on Friday, with the message from Old Trafford being that it's 'business as usual'.

But just 11 games into his first full season, the majority of readers who voted on Mirror Football's poll have seen enough. Fifty-four per cent voted to sack Carrick, with the remainder believing that he deserves more time.

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

In contrast, the United hierarchy are showing faith in Carrick after handing him a two-year contract in May. That's despite reports that former Germany manager Julian Nagelsmann would be a leading candidate and would be open to the job in the event that Carrick is sacked, while Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler has admirers at Old Trafford.

Carrick was reluctant to discuss his future in Como, as his typical controlled demeanour slipped away and his anger showed. When asked if thought that his players were still behind him, the former United midfielder replied: "I'd like to think so. I didn't like what I saw tonight, though.

‌



"It's not about playing for me, it's about playing for this football club. It's the responsibility that comes with being in the position; I'm responsible for the football club and the supporters.

View 2 Images The vote was narrowly against Michael Carrick

"I'm giving my best, absolute best all the time, I care about it. My whole life's wrapped around it. I genuinely give everything that I possibly can."

‌



Carrick apologised to United's 700 travelling fans, although most had left by the full-time whistle, and said: "I care an unbelievable amount about the supporters. They are the heartbeat of this football club and they always will be.

"For them to travel, I had to apologise for the performance. To have to watch a performance like that, I totally feel for them. There are no excuses at all. It is not acceptable."

Sports.title: Everything Julian Nagelsmann has said about Man Utd as he makes stance clear
Sports.content:
Everything Julian Nagelsmann has said about Man Utd as he makes stance clear

Julian Nagelsmann would be a leading candidate if Manchester United decide to sack Michael Carrick, and the ex-Germany manager is reportedly open to an approach

View 3 Images Manchester United have sounded out Julian Nagelsmann (Image: Ezra Shaw - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

Julian Nagelsmann already has a special connection with Manchester United amid reports that he'd be keen to replace Michael Carrick. Nagelsmann, 39, is out of work after stepping down as Germany boss following his country's humiliating World Cup exit.

‌



‌



Should United dispense with Carrick's services, the former Bayern Munich, RB Leipzig and Hoffenheim manager would be a leading candidate to replace him. The Red Devils have decided to stick with Carrick for now, despite Wednesday's abject 4-1 loss away to Como in the Champions League which extended their winless run to seven games.

‌



Nagelsmann's name has surfaced amid the fallout, as have his past comments. The German faced Ole Gunnar Solskjaer's United in the 2020-21 Champions League group stage when he was in charge of Leipzig.

‌



The first match took place at Old Trafford and Nagelsmann was wide-eyed as he visited the Theatre of Dreams, telling the Mail: "I've never played in Old Trafford or been there. It will be a great experience.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"I watched a lot of games in the Theatre of Dreams and of Manchester United on television. Now to be part of the stadium will be perfect. Bayern Munich v Manchester United, for example, the final when Ole Gunnar Solskjaer scored.

"Ryan Giggs did a lot of big games for Manchester United, Paul Scholes, Ruud Van Nistelrooy… a lot of players. I watched nearly every game of Manchester United 10 years ago, when I was a younger guy and a player.

‌



"I watched not only English football but also Serie A, Primera Division. I wanted to become a professional so it was important to watch games and look at what the best players in Europe do.

"Sir Alex Ferguson had a long and very successful time for Manchester United so it was also interesting to watch him, what he changed from one season to the next.

‌



"I know there will be no fans so that's hard. When there will be fans it will be more of a bigger experience. But if we win the game in the Theatre of Dreams it will be perfect."

View 3 Images Julian Nagelsmann 'watched nearly every game' involving Manchester United in his youth (Image: Vincent Mignott/DeFodi Images via Getty Images)

‌



Sadly for Nagelsmann, his side suffered a 5-0 loss. But his impressive work at Leizpig didn't stop him from being poached by Bayern, who paid €25million (£20.9m) to prise him away from Red Bull's football operation.

Nagelsmann lasted just shy of two seasons in Bavaria, winning the Bundesliga title in his first campaign. His next job was with Germany, leading them to the quarter-finals of a home European Championship in 2024.

‌



That was before the four-time winners were dumped out of this year's World Cup by Paraguay in the round of 32 on penalties. Nagelsmann quit shortly after the defeat, making way for Jurgen Klopp.

View 3 Images Julian Nagelsmann demands that his teams press high (Image: Image Photo Agency/Getty Images)

‌



United fans may also be interested in some of his tactical comments after Bruno Fernandes criticised how Carrick set the Red Devils up against Como. "It's a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little space in behind and try to get the ball in the first moment, to wait for them, to give them the ball," Fernandes told TNT Sports.

"But sometimes when you give too much the ball to these teams they get confident, they have so many bodies behind the ball that make you run a lot, make people get frustrated, and then obviously when you recover the ball the legs are, and the brain, much more difficult to make it work."

‌



Pressing is central to Nagelsmann's philosophy, as he explained in an interview with the Guardian in 2025: "I am not too keen on tackles. I much prefer us to win the ball by pressuring the opponent into a mistake, that we cut off his angles so that he makes a mistake when he tries to find a team-mate with a difficult pass.

‌



"And then, when we get the ball, we need to be quick in order to be able to create a chance and then it's better and the player is fresher when he hasn't had to make five tackles before starting an attack."

Once the hottest prospect in management, Nagelsmann's stock is arguably lower than ever. But at just 39 and with experience of high-pressure roles under his belt, he'll fancy he chances of being the answer to United's problems.

Sports.title: Julian Nagelsmann gives Man Utd green light as Michael Carrick replacement identified
Sports.content:
Julian Nagelsmann gives Man Utd green light as Michael Carrick replacement identified

Michael Carrick's job is hanging by a thread after Manchester United suffered a 4-1 hammering against Como in the Champions League, leaving them winless in seven games

View 2 Images Michael Carrick will remain in his post - for now (Image: Stefano Guidi/Getty Images)

Manchester United are set to consider Julian Nagelsmann if they decide to sack Michael Carrick - and the German is open to talks. United chiefs are sifting through the wreckage of Wednesday's woeful 4-1 defeat away to Como in the Champions League which thrust Carrick's future back into the spotlight.

‌



‌



The hammering extended the Red Devils' winless run to seven games, having only claimed victory in two of their 11 matches this season - against newly prompted Ipswich and European minnows Sabah. Carrick apologised to United's travelling supporters at the rainy Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium in scenes reminiscent of Ole Gunnar Solskjaer's final act before he was sacked in 2021.

‌



While it's been decided that Carrick will stay in charge for Sunday's game against Bournemouth, the Telegraph report that United will consider appointing Nagelsmann if things don't improve. It's added that the ex-Bayern Munich boss would listen to an approach.

‌



The 39-year-old has been out of work since being resigning as manager of Germany in July. Nagelsmann - who made his name managing Bundesliga side Hoffenheim in his late 20s - has links with Christopher Vivell, United's director of recruitment, having worked together at RB Leipzig.

Another manager on United's shortlist is Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler, whose side are flying high in the Premier League. Like Nagelsmann, Hurzeler began his managerial career at a young age and he's been tracked for some time by the Old Trafford hierarchy as a future option.

‌



View 2 Images Julian Nagelsmann stepped down as Germany's manager in July (Image: Joe Prior/Visionhaus via Getty Images)

Antonio Conte has also been offered to the Red Devils, although the ex-Chelsea and Tottenham manager isn't likely to be considered. Nor will Eddie Howe, who's also a free agent after he left Newcastle.

‌



As for Carrick, he was handed a two-year deal by United following an outstanding spell as their interim manager last season. But things have already unravelled, with captain Bruno Fernandes calling out his tactics in a post-match interview.

"It's the responsibility that comes with being in the position; I'm responsible for the football club and the supporters. I'm giving my best, absolute best all the time, I care about it. My whole life's wrapped around it. I genuinely give everything that I possibly can."

Sports.title: Celtic stunned by quick double in Europa League defeat to Celta Vigo
Sports.content:
Celtic's Europa League hopes took another blow as Celta Vigo came from behind to inflict their third straight defeat in the competition.

After an emphatic 7-1 win against Hearts, the Hoops once again showed their struggle to take their domestic dominance into European competition. The defeat leaves them as one of four clubs in the 36-team table yet to register any points.

The Celtic fans were screaming for a penalty midway through the first half when Callum Osmond went down from a push from Javi Rueda. It was just outside the box, with the referee deciding not to award a free-kick.

Image: Mika Baur gave Celtic the lead just after the break

Mika Baur did give them the lead just after the break as he swept home a deflected cross from Haissem Hassan.

After Liam Scales hit the crossbar, Celta hit back with a quick double.

Javi Rodriguez scored twice in three minutes - a header then an unstoppable drive - to stun the home side who could not find a way back as they suffered another damaging Euro night.

Celtic, four points clear of Old Firm rivals Rangers at the top of the Scottish Premiership, face Hibernian at Easter Road on Sunday (kick-off 12pm) - live on Sky Sports.

Key moments from Celtic Park....

12: BLOCK! Colby Donovan is well placed to clear Javi Rueda's cross as Celta Vigo look to open the scoring.

15: BLOCK! Mika Baur is in the right place this time to stop Iago Aspas' effort.

23: PENALTY APPEALS! Callum Osmand is pushed as he ran into the box, but the referee is having none of it. Camilo Duran is booked for his protests.

43: CHANCE! The ball falls to Osmand outside the box after Duran failed to get his shot away. He sends it well over the bar.

44: SAVE! Ferran Jutgla is denied by Sam Johnstone with half time approaching.

47: GOAL CELTIC! Haissem Hassan sends in a dangerous cross, it takes a deflection and breaks to Mika Baur to fire in.

52: CHANCE! Aleix Febas meets Sergio Carreira's low cross only to send it past the post.

63: OFF THE BAR! Liam Scales inches from doubling Celtic's lead. The defender gets his head to Hassan's cross, but it hits the woodwork.

68: GOAL CELTA! Javi Rodriguez meets the free-kick and his header can't be saved by Johnstone.

72: GOAL CELTA! A brilliant strike from Rodriguez, a nightmare for Celtic.They fail to clear the danger and he fires in from outside the box.

85: SAVE! Forrest sets up Donovan, but his effort lacks power and it's easily saved.

The stats don't lie

Image: Celtic have lost their last four games in Europe

Sky Sports' Luke Shanley was watching at Celtic Park:

Celta were worth their win. The stats don't lie and they had many more chances than Celtic.

The home side were ahead though and what will annoy them is not being able to see it out. Losing two goals in the space of three minutes was a hammer blow.

Martin O'Neill might not be happy with the award of the free-kick that led to the equaliser, but ultimately they needed to defend it better.

Celtic have now lost four European games in a row. The frustration or the worry is that Celtic are not competing enough at this level and can't bridge the gap after winning 7-1 at the weekend in the Scottish Premiership against Hearts.

Their Europa League campaign is all but over but their misery in Europe might not be.

'Still a lot of points to play for'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Celtic manager Martin O'Neill believes they can still progress in the Europa League despite Celta Vigo inflicting their third straight defeat in this season's tournament

Celtic manager Martin O'Neill:

"Where did it all go wrong? Well, we hit the bar with the header, we could have gone 2-0 in front. I think if we had done that we'd probably have won, but forget ifs, buts and maybes, we conceded a goal from a set piece.

"We just lost a bit of momentum, but conceded the second goal, which was a blinding shot by the player outside the penalty area.

"It was a tough evening, but I can't ask for any more from the players.

"Tonight is disappointing because I thought that we could win the game, I felt that beforehand, and while it was a tight match throughout, I still thought we could win.

"I haven't looked at the table, but I was told roughly that there's still a lot of points to play for.

"We have to obviously win a game at Celtic Park, and we have to win away from home, and I think we're capable of doing that."

What the result means and next fixtures...

Sports.title: Bournemouth seal historic win over Amorim's 10-man Milan
Sports.content:
Amine Adli scored a fine free-kick to cap Bournemouth's historic 3-0 win over 10-man AC Milan, which continues their brilliant start to their first-ever European campaign.

Ruben Amorim's side are far from the standard of the great Milan teams of the past but this is nonetheless a treasured scalp for Bournemouth who, for the majority of their history, could not have imagined they'd play this fixture. The seven-time European champions, humbled by the Cherries.

It was a wet and wild night on the south coast, with the weather fitting for the chaotic first half, which included Milan captain Mike Maignan being sent off for brutally pushing both hands into Tyler Adams' face at a corner.

Image: AC Milan goalkeeper Mike Maignan looks at Tyler Adams as he is sent off for a push to the face of the Bournemouth player

That recklessness from the goalkeeper brought Bournemouth their second penalty, which was expertly dispatched by Marcus Tavernier after Justin Kluivert had slotted in the first spot-kick following a Koni De Winter handball.

Another dead-ball moment brought Bournemouth's third. It was a wonderful whip from sub Adli - but Amorim would not have been happy with the Milan wall which broke apart to sum up their sloppiness.

Image: 'How did we end up here?' - Bournemouth's tifo before facing AC Milan in the Europa League

'How did we end up here' was the sign on the Bournemouth banner before kick-off. Their supporters would have been in even further disbelief with their side two-up against 10 men before half-time. By full-time they were gleefully taunting Amorim, who has now failed to beat Bournemouth in five attempts. It was a miserable return to England for the former Manchester United boss.

But it's lift-off at Bournemouth now, after they recorded their first Premier League win of the season over 10-man Sunderland at the weekend and go third in the Europa League table with a perfect record of three from three.

Rose proud of 'brilliant' Bournemouth performance

Bournemouth boss Marco Rose:

"A big night for us. I'm happy for the club, our fans especially and really proud of my lads. The way they did it was brilliant from the first minute until the last minute, we played a really good game.

"Even with 11 against 11 we started well, we put pressure on them, we got one penalty. Then the red card makes something of the game. Sometimes you get in trouble in these situations but, like on Sunday, we did it really well. We didn't give anything to them.

"It suits us to stay humble. We know we are good. We know if we have the whole squad we can compete with everyone everywhere but the season is long."

Amorim: There was no game after 20 minutes

AC Milan boss Ruben Amorim:

"It's hard to talk about our performance. There was no game after 20 minutes. We need to avoid our mistakes. We need to have 11 players on the pitch all the time.

"We tried to defend in the way they are comfortable and try to push the game forward like we did until the last minutes and then the free-kick killed the game.

"It was a hard night for us, a difficult night in every aspect."

Key moments from the Vitality Stadium...

5: PENALTY! After a VAR check, the officials spot a handball from De Winter, who had his arm up and connected with the ball when Evanilson headed wide.

8: GOAL! Kluivert coolly sends Maignan the wrong way to side-foot into the other corner for a historic early opener for Bournemouth.

Like father, like son Bournemouth’s Justin Kluivert scored against Milan 31 years & 151 days after his father Patrick netted the winner against them in the Champions League final in May 1995.

Image: Justin Kluivert celebrates giving Bournemouth the lead vs AC Milan

28: RED CARD & PENALTY! Maignan is shown a straight red for shoving Adams in the face as Bournemouth send a corner into the Milan box. After a VAR check and plenty of confusion, Bournemouth are awarded another penalty as well!

Maignan's unwanted record Mike Maignan became the first ever Milan goalkeeper to be sent off in a major European game.

32: GOAL! Tavernier steps up this time but it's the same result - he sends replacement goalkeeper Lorenzo Torriani the wrong way to put Bournemouth into dreamland.

57: CLOSE! Moments after De Winter is forced to clear the ball over his own bar from close range, Kluivert whips the follow-up short corner narrowly wide of the far post.

67: OVER! Sub Rayan rises high but sends his header from Ben Gannon-Doak's cross over the bar.

84: GOAL! Adli whips a free-kick through the Milan wall and into the net to cap a brilliant night for Bournemouth.

87: SAVE! Rayan takes a crossfield pass into the box with his chest - and then is denied a goal by Torriani's fingertips.

Upcoming Bournemouth fixtures...

Sports.title: Mateta on target as Palace draw with Besiktas in Istanbul
Sports.content:
Jean-Philippe Mateta scored his first goal since last season's UEFA Conference League final but Crystal Palace had to settle for a 2-2 draw away at 10-man Besiktas.

Mateta thought he had opened the scoring with the first chance of the match when he swept home in the fifth minute, only for VAR to intervene and rule the striker had strayed marginally offside.

Besiktas took the lead against the run of play when Wilfred Ndidi rifled in on the stroke of half-time with Besiktas' first shot on target.

But Palace equalised six minutes after the restart when Pino got on the end of Anan Khalaili's cutback to sweep in. The flag went up for offside, but this time VAR intervened in Palace's favour with the visitors drawing level.

Image: Crystal Palace's players celebrate their side first goal during the Europa League opening phase soccer match between Besiktas and Crystal Palace in Istanbul, Turkey, Thursday, Oct. 22, 2026. (AP Photo/Emrah Gurel)

And four minutes later they went ahead after Mateta intercepted a loose back pass before striding into the area and smashing home into the roof of the net.

But Besiktas were back level in the 73rd minute when substitute Junior Olaitan shot low and hard and into the corner.

Umit Akdag was sent off for a two-footed lunge on Jorgen Strand Larsen, before the striker went off injured late on, as Besiktas held on for the draw.

Sage: We deserved better

Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage to TNT:

"It's really intense, it's crazy to play here, but I would have preferred to say it's crazy to win here.

"I am pleased (with the performance) but with the result a little bit frustrated for the lads

"They gave a lot this evening and I think they deserve better, but we have a lack of concentration during one minute in the first half at the end, and it was the same thing when it was 2-1 for us.

"In this period, this kind of situation, you pay quickly for little mistakes, and we have to remember that the situation was worse before the game.

"The performance was worse on Sunday, and it's a good step to go forward to win against Newcastle."

Sports.title: 'That's not enough for me' - Hamilton explains why he went against Ferrari strategy
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton has explained the reasons why he overrode Ferrari's call to pit in the Singapore Grand Prix, a mistake he says he "owned up to" and will work not to repeat - but which would not prevent him from continuing "challenging the norms".

Hamilton dropped out of the podium positions to sixth on worn tyres in the closing stages of the last race at Marina Bay after what proved the costly decision not to pit under the Virtual Safety Car, as the Ferrari pit wall had requested.

Feeling unwell after the gruelling night race, and being excused from his post-race media obligations by the FIA, Hamilton's only comments about his race came via a statement issued by the team and then a post on his Instagram, in which he said he took responsibility for the strategy going wrong.

He spoke in person about what had happened for the first time in Thursday's press conference in Austin ahead of this weekend's United States Grand Prix.

In a detailed answer, Hamilton initially explained why he first chose to start the race on different tyres, the mediums, to team-mate Charles Leclerc who was one place ahead of him on the grid behind Red Bull's polesitting Max Verstappen, the eventual race winner.

"Well, firstly, you learn from these experiences," said Hamilton.

"It's rare that I find myself in that position. Of course, the next couple of days didn't feel so great but you live and you learn.

"I think when I was lining up on grid, when I knew I was going to be third, I'm always looking at ways to win. I'm always looking at doing potentially something different.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton drops to P6 as Lando Norris, Kimi Antonelli and Oscar Piastri ease past him in Singapore.

"And I wanted to be on a different strategy, not just the same strategy as Charles, where we just follow each other. We assumed Max would be potentially quicker and the strategy kind of showed just us finishing second and third and that's not enough for me.

"I wanted to have options and see what could be possible. If the medium tyre could last longer, maybe you could go deeper into the race, but it wasn't the case when I got going and it didn't feel great in the first stint.

"Then obviously coming out behind Charles and losing a lot of time, ultimately, with him on the slower tyre, which I was on at the beginning I had the pace on the soft was a bit of a similar scenario to maybe to Zandvoort."

On the decision to not heed Ferrari's call to pit under the Virtual Safety Car and continue on to take over what stood as second place, Hamilton said: "I was coming towards the pit lane entry, and I didn't know Charles was coming in, because I think just recently he had stopped and in a split-second decision I decided to stay out.

"And as soon as I was alongside the pit lane, I realised it's probably the wrong decision, but I owned up to it, took responsibility for it and you move on."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player On the F1 Show podcast, Bernie Collins considers whether Lewis Hamilton has lost trust in Ferrari after overriding a team strategy call in Singapore.

'I will not shy away from that' - Hamilton to keep 'challenging the norms'

Hamilton said there had been productive discussions in the team since Singapore and that he believed it was important that he continued to "continuously challenge the team, and myself" in the search for better results.

"We've had good conversations in the background of how we can do better together, how we can collaborate better, but I think that nothing's changed in terms of how well we work together in the background," he added.

"I truly believe my job is rather than to follow suit always, it's to continuously challenge the team, and myself including, and just constantly challenging the norms. And that's ultimately how I've got to where I am and I will not shy away from that.

"Sometimes it doesn't go well and that was one of those but you live to fight another day, you win or lose as a team. So we carry the weight and the costs together.

"It definitely hurts when I lose points for the team, it's not something I do very often, but I'll work, I'll double the efforts to make sure that doesn't happen again."

Sports.title: What cost England in epic as 'box office' Brook's 'genius' goes to waste?
Sports.content:
At the halfway stage, most people would have given Sri Lanka no chance.

The ask was a herculean 430, second only to the 438-9 South Africa peeled off versus Australia in Johannesburg in 2006 when it came to successful ODI run chases.

But on a day when South Africa beat Australia once again - this time in a one-sided Test match in Gqeberha - Sri Lanka stunned England in a Rawalpindi run-fest.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch how Harry Brook rewrote the record books with England's highest individual ODI score

Image: The records broken by Brook during his stunning ODI double hundred for England

That meant Harry Brook's astonishing 202 from 116 balls, during which he reached 200 from 114 deliveries to set a new record for the fastest ODI double ton, came in vain.

So where exactly did things go wrong for England?

How did England lose that game?

Not with the batting, obviously, as Brook's sizzling knock - the highest for England in a men's ODI, eclipsing the 182 Ben Stokes scored against New Zealand in 2023 - was backed up by half-centuries from Tom Banton, Joe Root and Will Jacks.

The bowling was the issue with Sri Lanka rallying from 24-2 once Kamindu Mendis had been bowled by a beauty from Josh Tongue and captain Kusal Mendis was run out backing up without facing a ball after Gus Atkinson tipped on to the non-striker's stumps.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sri Lanka captain Kusal Mendis was run out backing up without having faced a single ball as Gus Atkinson tipped onto the non-striker's stumps

Sky Sports' Nasser Hussain noted how England overcompensated from bowling too full during their 87-run defeat to Pakistan at the same venue on Tuesday by dropping too short, particularly to Pavan Rathnayake, who top-scored with 130 from 106 balls.

The former England captain also lamented his country's long-standing issue of middle-overs wickets, with only one taken between Kusal's run out in the fifth over and Rathnayake holing out off the expensive Sam Curran at long-on in the 41st.

Rathnayake put on 166 with Avishka Fernando for the third wicket and then 133 with the wisely-promoted Dasun Shanaka for the fourth - both of his team-mates made 97.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the last over of Thursday's ODI as Josh Tongue claimed back-to-back wickets before Janith Liyanage struck the winning six

Hussain: Lack of middle-order wickets a concern for England

Hussain said of the wicketless woes: "It comes from that middle period where England, historically, over the last two or three years, have struggled to take wickets.

"That is even with Adil Rashid, who did not play in this game, at his best, so that is something they need to solve, a box they need to tick. Getting back Jofra Archer, rested for this series, will help and add a bit of firepower.

"Maybe Adil has come off his best but today showed the need for Archer, and Rashid being back to his best. We all big up Adil but he has just dropped off, maybe because of injuries."

Former Sri Lanka batter and Hussain's fellow Sky Sports pundit Kumar Sangakkara said: "England needed an all-out push to take wickets when they had Sri Lanka 24-2. You have 429 on the board.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Sky Sports pundits reflect on Sri Lanka's staggering run chase in Pindi

"Have set plays, try to bowl the bumpers, fielders set for catches - of if you want to restrict because conditions are not suitable for wickets, then go to death bowling early, try to cut off the boundaries.

"The only way they were going to lose the game was by the boundary count rising. If you are a fast bowler, you stop the fours with fields set and the sixes by executing the best deliveries.

"Still, England need to give credit to an incredible batting performance from Sri Lanka."

Brook: Sri Lanka 'played a blinder' England captain Harry Brook: “We can take a lot of learnings from that game. We definitely didn't execute what we were trying to do for long enough. "We were trying to keep the stumps in play as much as we possibly could. We were probably erring on the short side which played into their hands. "But to be involved in a game like that is incredible and hats off to Sri Lanka. They've played an absolute blinder there."

Sri Lanka get over the line after 'marathon'

That point about Sri Lanka is an important one from Sangakkara.

For as loose as England were with the ball - Curran, in just his second game since The Hundred in August due to a groin injury, struggled to land his moon balls and yorkers and was flogged for 103 runs from his nine overs - Sri Lanka were superb.

They showed grit after slipping two down early, then the ability to adapt by pushing Shanaka up the order - he smoked eight sixes in his 50-ball 97 - and when late wickets had seen Sri Lanka wobble a bit, Janith Liyanage fired under pressure with an unbeaten 61.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Check out the best of Liyanage's crucial 61 not out for Sri Lanka

Liyanage crunched two fours and a six across three balls off Curran to trim the ask to 29 from 21 deliveries and then spanked the winning six with one ball to spare after Tongue has taken two wickets in two deliveries earlier in the final over.

Hussain added: "Sri Lanka had to be pretty much perfect for 50 overs and they were. There were lads in there who played pretty much the perfect innings.

"It was like running a marathon for Sri Lanka - they saw that last bit and started to stumble when they needed to be calm.

"So Liyanage in the end - that was incredibly special. You looked at his body language, it was like, 'leave it to me, lads' - he was calm, composed and belted it down the ground.

"It was a perfect, historic chase and brilliant for Sri Lanka. They are such a talented, passionate cricketing nation. They needed a day like today and they got one."

Why Brook said his double hundred 'does not matter'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England captain Brook said his double ton had 'no value whatsoever' as it came in a losing cause

Brook had spoken earlier in the week about wishing there was a match-winning column in players' stats.

If that was part of cricket, then for a long time in Rawalpindi on Thursday it looked like Brook's would have a big fat tick in it.

In the end, though, the Yorkshireman insisted that his individual heroics "didn't matter."

Brook, whose innings featured 21 fours and 10 sixes said: "I always say I want to make match-winning contributions, have a match-winning impact. Unfortunately I've got 200 and it's not been match-winning. In my eyes, it doesn't matter. It had no value whatsoever."

Still, Hussain and Sky Sports colleague Mark Butcher enthused over the England captain, with Hussain calling him the best male multi-format batter in the world and saying his presence makes the team contenders at next year's 50-over World Cup in Africa.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Nasser Hussain and Mark Butcher laud 'genius' Brook's 114-ball double century against Sri Lanka

The pundit added: "Every shot selection he made was spot on - it had to be to score 200 that quickly. He has been touched by genius ever since we have seen him.

"The biggest area of growth for this ODI team is if Brook can convert his Test and T20 form into this format. He did that, it was magical.

Butcher said: "Sometimes your breath is taken away with Brook and you don't quite have the words to describe what you are watching.

"Such is his precision and the way he can uses the pace on the ball, he can pretty much manoeuvre it wherever he likes. Then he will fly out of the crease and hit you for six.

"He has such balance, his hands are so good, the control of the bat face is as good as anybody I have seen. He can play a shot for pretty much every delivery. He is absolutely box office."

Now, if England could just get the bowling sorted…
