Sports.title: Nottingham Forest’s false start places early focus on Glasner and Delap
Sports.content:
Sitting 19th in the Premier League was not the plan for Nottingham Forest after the arrival of a highly acclaimed manager and a £45m striker to fuel their ambitions. The fates of Oliver Glasner and Liam Delap are intertwined and with the stark stats of zero home goals and a solitary point at the City Ground it is not the dream start they were aiming for.

As Delap prepares to return to Ipswich, where his career ignited, on Friday night, Forest are remaining calm. There is a desperation to get away from the short-termism that caused so many problems; 12 months ago, they were on their third head coach of a disappointing season. This summer they were ruthless with the removal of Vítor Pereira, who had done a fine job to escape the drop, because they saw an opportunity to upgrade with Glasner, hoping he could transform Forest like he did Crystal Palace.

It cost plenty to acquire Glasner and Delap, which many fans believe should lead to instant results, but that is rarely the case in an industry as complicated as football. For the coach, it is a case of learning the club inside out while influencing performance through his carefully choreographed methods. For the striker, he needs to rebuild confidence and that comes via goals.

In Glasner’s first full season at Palace, they won one of their first 13 league matches but ended comfortably in mid-table and FA Cup winners. It was similar at Eintracht Frankfurt, getting one victory in 10, but going on to win the Europa League.

Learning the Glasner way is not straightforward. Playing three at the back is rarely the norm and nor is having two No 10s, all with the background of Forest losing their best player in Elliot Anderson.

The recruitment was measured, targeting positions that required strengthening and avoiding needless purchases that dogged the club after promotion. Replacing Anderson became a priority, but Glasner felt James McAtee could adapt to a deeper role in midfield alongside the shrewd free signing Xaver Schlager. Ousmane Diomande was a coup in defence and Glasner convinced Daniel Muñoz to follow him from Selhurst Park.

Behind the obvious figures, there is plenty of underlying encouragement for Forest. Based on chances created and conceded, Glasner has had the best start of any Forest manager in the Premier League era. His team rank seventh, according to Opta, for expected goals (xG), but have scored the fewest – five – and are the biggest xG underperformers at -6.2. It is a huge discrepancy, missing out on almost a goal a game. It includes 62 shots at home that have come to nothing and if Glasner wants buy-in from the fans, that needs to change quickly. If every team had scored and conceded the goals measured by xG, Forest would be fourth.

View image in fullscreen Nottingham Forest, and Liam Delap, are yet to score at the City Ground this season. Photograph: Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty Images

It is understandable that Delap is yet to find his feet after a disappointing year at Chelsea and the lack of pre-season set him back. Forest tried to sign him before he went to Stamford Bridge and have great faith in him, but he needs to improve his record of one goal every five league appearances. He is the ideal No 9, possessing pace, power and sharp finishing, but unless he is on peak form, turning that into guaranteed output is not straightforward.

Delap has scored once for Forest, but is putting in the effort through being the front line of defence, relentlessly pressing opposition centre-backs. He has shown plenty of quick thinking, demonstrated by his quick throw-in to set up a goal at Anfield, something almost replicated against Arsenal only for Chris Wood to miss the chance.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Forest allowed Arsenal a single shot on target last Sunday – it just happened to be deflected in for a winner. Glasner can also point in that match to the absence of his captain, Morgan Gibbs-White, the team’s attacking fulcrum. “It feels very unfair,” Glasner said of the result. “We have to accept we are missing some bits. But the performance in many parts was very good.”

In two full seasons at Selhurst Park, Glasner won two major trophies for a club that had gone almost 120 years without one. He has two European titles and his own distinctive formation and execution, something he has harnessed over 12 years in coaching, so he knows how long it takes to develop the complexities.

The picture looks clearer after almost four months together. The hope at Forest is that the endeavour is rewarded with greater luck, the missing ingredient among well thought-out recruitment led by the chief football officer, George Syrianos, and his team and clever coaching. Syrianos is Glasner’s biggest advocate and told fans the manager would be given time.

Friday will be Glasner’s eighth Premier League match at Forest, three more than Ange Postecoglou was permitted before being sacked this time last year by the owner, Evangelos Marinakis. Glasner, unlike the Australian, can show progress and will be justifiably confident points will come.

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca says honest talks have revitalised Foden’s Manchester City form
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca has revealed he held heart-to-heart conversations with Phil Foden to help the midfielder back to his best. Foden has struggled over the past two years but has scored four goals in his past two games to give hope he can recapture the form that won him the Professional Footballers’ Association player of the year award in 2023-24.

City travel to Aston Villa on Saturday lunchtime aiming to continue their perfect Premier League start under Maresca, with Erling Haaland fit after sitting on the bench for Wednesday’s Champions League win over AEK Athens.

“Since we started I sat down with Phil two or three times, especially at the beginning,” said Maresca, who knew Foden from a spell as Pep Guardiola’s assistant. “Maybe love is not the right word to use but just to show him how important he is.

“I said many times that I know Phil from years ago so I know how good he is. For different reasons the last few years he was not good enough, but again I think when you have more players like Phil available you are a better team because at the end it’s a matter of improving players. If you improve the players you improve the team, so for me it’s my duty to try to help Phil to be again one of the best players in England. But it’s not just about one game – the season is very long.”

Foden, 26, needs to remain consistent to keep his place in the team, with plenty of competition for the attacking roles, including from Rayan Cherki, who Maresca has described as “one of the best players in Europe”.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

City’s only competitive defeat under Maresca came against Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League, and they have seven straight wins in the Premier League to sit three points clear at the top. Maresca is waiting to find out whether Matheus Nunes, Mateo Kovacic and Nico O’Reilly are available after missing the AEK game. “The mood is good, we are happy with our start but we are still hungry for more wins,” Maresca said.

Sports.title: ‘No messing about’ – Ex-Premier League manager is the perfect successor to Michael Carrick at Manchester United
Sports.content:
‘No messing about’ – Ex-Premier League manager is the perfect successor to Michael Carrick at Manchester United

Manchester United can do a 'lot worse' than appointing Eddie Howe as their next manager.

That is the view of Howe's former Bournemouth winger Marc Pugh.

3 Howe has been urged to take on the United job if offered the chance Credit: Getty

The ex-Cherries boss has been put forward as a potential candidate to succeed Michael Carrick at Old Trafford.

It comes amid mounting pressure on Carrick after his side's winless run extended to seven matches in all competitions.

United were soundly beaten by Como in the Champions League on Wednesday, suffering a 4-1 defeat in Italy.

Whilst Carrick is set to remain in charge for Sunday's clash with Bournemouth, Howe has emerged as the favourite to succeed him.

talkSPORT understands technical director Jason Wilcox is leaning towards appointing the 48-year-old if Carrick is sacked.

Other candidates in the running include former Germany boss Julian Nagelsmann, who has already been sounded out by the Red Devils.

Howe backed for United job

Pugh has admitted United need a manager of Howe's profile to turn around their fortunes.

The 39-year-old was signed by Howe for the Cherries back in 2010 before winning promotion from League One and the Championship.

In total, Pugh made 232 appearances under Howe during a nine-year spell at the Vitality Stadium.

Speaking to Hawksbee and Baker on Thursday, Pugh was asked if he believes the United job would interest his former manager.

3 Pugh believes his former Bournemouth boss could transform United's fortunes Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Pugh explained: "If I was Eddie, I’d jump at the chance, but to be honest, I think United need someone like Eddie.

"The intensity level in training will go up a notch. He won’t stand for people sacking training off.

"I’m not saying Michael does. I don’t know what goes on behind the scenes at Old Trafford, at United, but he will make sure people that are playing on a Saturday and Tuesday, whenever it may be, that they are going to run and he plays high-press, high-intensity football.

"There will be no messing about, that’s for sure, but he’s fantastic tactically, technically, he cares about his players and I think they can do a lot worse than Eddie, that’s for sure."

When pressed as to whether Howe would take on the job, he added: "I think jobs like that don’t come around often and it’s one of the best clubs in the world. You’ve got to jump at the chance in my eyes."

Howe's managerial career so far

Howe is currently without a club having left Newcastle in July.

3 Howe has enjoyed historic success at both Bournemouth and Newcastle Credit: Getty

During almost five years in charge at St. James' Park, he twice guided the Magpies to Champions League qualification.

Meanwhile, the club's Carabao Cup triumph under Howe in 2025 ended a 70-year wait for major domestic silverware.

His time as Newcastle boss followed two spells in charge of Bournemouth either side of a nine-month stint at Burnley.

Having won promotion from League Two two years earlier, Howe returned to the Cherries in 2012 to guide them from League One to the Premier League.

Sports.title: Eddie Howe emerges as new favourite for Man United job as Michael Carrick’s authority diminishes
Sports.content:
Eddie Howe emerges as new favourite for Man United job as Michael Carrick’s authority diminishes

Manchester United technical director Jason Wilcox is leaning towards appointing Eddie Howe if Michael Carrick is sacked, talkSPORT understands.

Carrick faces an uphill battle to save his job in the wake of Wednesday's humiliating 4-1 defeat at Como after which captain Bruno Fernandes rounded on his manager.



2 Fernandes publicly questioned Carrick's tactics against Como Credit: AFP

Carrick is set to be in charge for Sunday's Premier League home clash with Bournemouth as the United hierarchy contemplate their options moving forward.

Who are the contenders to replace Michael Carrick if he's sacked?

As exclusively revealed by talkSPORT, former Germany and Bayern Munich chief Julian Nagelsmann has already been sounded out over his interest in taking charge at Old Trafford.

Nagelsmann is the standout option in the eyes of head of recruitment Christopher Vivell.



But Wilcox's opinion is likely to hold more weight in the eyes of Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazer family.

Wilcox is believed to prefer Howe due to his experience in the Premier League even though he rallied against appointing him when Dan Ashworth put him forward prior to Ruben Amorim's arrival.



Aston Villa boss Unai Emery also fits Wilcox's criteria but would be expensive to prise away even if he wanted the job.

talkSPORT understands Fabian Hurzeler, another admired by Wilcox, would not leave Brighton for United at this time.



Antonio Conte has put himself forward to replace Carrick but that looks unlikely having been previously overlooked due to his fiery nature.

Bruno Fernandes set to avoid punishment for post-match outburst

In another ominous sign for Carrick, United do not plan to punish captain Fernandes for his incredible outburst.

There is a fear in the boardroom that the 2008 Champions League winner is losing the faith of the dressing room after overseeing United's worst start to a season in 40 years.

2 Carrick has endured a torrid time since becoming United's permanent manager Credit: Getty



Howe has been out of work since leaving Newcastle by mutual consent in the summer.

While he is not desperate to return to the dugout quickly the feeling is he would be interested if the United vacancy came his way.

At Newcastle, Howe ended the club's 70-year wait for a domestic trophy when he led them to EFL Cup glory in 2025.

Howe also oversaw Newcastle's return to the Champions League in 2023, 20 years after they were last in the competition.



The Magpies repeated the feat at the end of the 2024/25 campaign.

Howe's final season at the helm ended with Newcastle finishing 12th, their lowest placing throughout his tenure at the club.

Sports.title: Troy Deeney: Michael Carrick allowed Bruno Fernandes to disrespect him with this costly mistake
Sports.content:
Troy Deeney: Michael Carrick allowed Bruno Fernandes to disrespect him with this costly mistake

Michael Carrick gave Lisandro Martinez an inch, only for Bruno Fernandes to take a mile.

Fernandes publicly questioned Carrick's tactics following the 4-1 humbling against Como on Wednesday, claiming the team had to be 'more brave under pressure' and 'take the risk of pressing high'.



3 Fernandes was not happy with how Carrick set his team up against Como Credit: Getty

Carrick countered his skipper's claim by stating he had his players do exactly what he'd asked for, only to concede a goal. Carrick also argued that a lack of running will contribute more to a defeat than any perceived tactical flaws.

Curiously, Fernandes' verdict came a week after Lisandro Martinez called out United technical director Jason Wilcox for not appropriately strengthening the squad in the summer.

Martinez later apologised for his comments but was not suspended by Carrick, as the centre-back started the 1-1 draw against Leeds last Sunday.



Troy Deeney's verdict on the Bruno Fernandes saga

But Troy Deeney believed not suspending Martinez was a major misstep from Carrick and ultimately paved the way for Fernandes to speak his mind.

“Last week when Martinez said what he said, you can't let him play," Deeney said on Premier League All Access.



"You've got to nip that in the bud and just be like, 'I get you apologising and all of that, but, you're out of the team this week.'

“And I know he probably looked around and went, 'I haven't got much here, I haven't got much in the way of help, we're at Elland Road.' You need to nip it in the bud.



“The second he didn't and Martinez played, he inadvertently allows for Bruno Fernandes to talk.

“Bruno Fernandes feeds it to the open season, 'I can say what I want.'

“But Bruno Fernandes, I've been saying this for three years, when he hasn't got the goals or assists, he's not a captain. We've had this discussion so many times, he's not a leader.”

3 Martinez's comments put Wilcox immediately under the microscope Credit: Getty



Carrick and Fernandes will now need to smoke the peace pipe if they are to help reverse United's fortunes, especially amid a run of seven games without a win.

But that will not be an easy feat as the Red Devils host Bournemouth on Sunday.

The Cherries go into the fixture on the back of their first league win this season, having beaten Sunderland 2-0.

A 'quite toxic' atmosphere awaits at Old Trafford

And should Bournemouth strike early on Sunday, talkSPORT chief football correspondent Alex Crook fears Old Trafford could 'turn quite toxic'.



"I think there were a lot of angry Manchester United fans, both inside the stands and watching at home in midweek," Crook said.

"They'll have seen what Bruno Fernandes has said.

3 Outside of his hat-trick and assist against Ipswich, Fernandes has one goal contribution this season Credit: Getty

"They'll feel for Michael Carrick. I think they do feel empathy for Michael Carrick. He's a club legend, someone who won the European Cup as a player. Someone who stepped in in their hour of need last season.

"They are very angry with those above Carrick, the likes of Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada.



"If this game starts to go against them, as you fear it will with Bournemouth picking up their first Premier League win last weekend, I think it could turn very badly, very quickly.

"Bournemouth have the capability to run all over Manchester United."

Sports.title: Lisandro Martinez and £50m player get brutal 2/10 ratings as Man United squad slated for nightmare start
Sports.content:
Lisandro Martinez and £50m player get brutal 2/10 ratings as Man United squad slated for nightmare start

The gloomy skies above Old Trafford don't look like dispersing any time soon.

A humiliating 4-1 defeat to Como on Wednesday evening marked Manchester United's seventh game without a win and heaped further doubt on Michael Carrick's future at the club.

7 Carrick is at risk of the sack at United just five months after being given the permanent job on the touchline Credit: AFP

The uncertainty was not aided by a controversial post-match interview where captain Bruno Fernandes publicly questioned Carrick's tactics.

Fernandes' outburst came a week after Lisandro Martinez called out United technical director Jason Wilcox following a 2-0 loss to Atletico Madrid.

In essence, all is far from well at United.

Amid the Red Devils' disastrous start to the campaign, talkSPORT's Alex Crook rates how every United player has performed thus far.

Goalkeeper

Belgian ace Senne Lammens has been the main man between the sticks for United this season.

After presenting himself as a relatively steady pair of hands last term, Lammens' confidence appears to have been dented on the back of an error at the World Cup.

Lammens only has one clean sheet to his name this season.

Defenders

It's largely been a start to forget for United's defenders, having shipped ten league goals so far.

Although it typically takes a team effort to be defensively poor, a number of players who have stood out for all the wrong reasons.

One of those is Martinez, who scored a comical own goal against Fulham and was then at fault for Dominic Solanke's late equaliser that rescued a 1-1 draw for Spurs.

7 Martinez is out of contract at the end of the season Credit: Getty

Noussair Mazraoui has also failed to prove himself worthy, having been brought in to suit Ruben Amorim's ill-fated 3-4-3 formation.

Harry Maguire may have ended last season in resurgent form but he, like several of his teammates, has dropped off and been unable to stop United leaking goals, although he continues to give his all.

It is a similar story for Diogo Dalot, who has created more chances than any other defender despite having to play out of position.

For Luke Shaw, his inability to stay fit has left Carrick with a serious selection headache and exposed United's failings in the transfer market as they did not add in another left-back.

Question marks remain regarding Ayden Heaven, who still does not look ready to play week-in, week-out in the Premier League.

Heaven also had the difficult task of playing as a left-back against Atleti, with the 20-year-old a centre-back by trade.

7 Maguire has been at United since July 2019, making him one of the club's most experienced heads Credit: Getty

Another centre-back who had to moonlight elsewhere across the back four is Leny Yoro.

Yoro played at right-back against Atleti and did okay, even if he was controversially sent off, but hasn't exactly pulled up trees in his usual position.

Midfielders

United underwent a costly reconstruction of their midfield this summer, but it hasn't panned out as hoped so far.

Andrey Santos looks a million miles off being a £50m player, with the Brazilian sloppy in possession and offering little protection for the defence.

Youri Tielemans has also struggled to fit in, with his mobility a serious issue.

The Belgian, who joined from Aston Villa, has logged more minutes than any other United midfielder, with the exception of skipper Bruno Fernandes.

7 Outside of his hat-trick and assist against Ipswich, Fernandes has one goal contribution this season Credit: Getty

As for Fernandes, he has seriously struggled to recreate the form that won him last season's Premier League Player of the Year award.

Serious concerns remain about Mason Mount, who is into his third season with the Red Devils but has just 25 league starts under his belt.

One player who could help turn United's midfield woes around is £70m man Carlos Baleba.

The 22-year-old made an instant impact off the bench in the Spurs draw and had a good game against Leeds, but is clearly still not fully match fit.

Once Baleba is back up to speed, Carrick may look to pair him with Kobbie Mainoo, who has been the standout performer in an abject team.

Shea Lacey is another who has showed promise, including a goal on his full United debut against Brighton in the Carabao Cup, but has been strangely under-used since.

7 Mainoo enjoyed a return to form under Carrick having previously been frozen out under Amorim Credit: Getty

Forwards

The one group somewhat sparing United from further misery is their attacking unit.

Only six Premier League sides have scored more goals than the Red Devils (ten) this term, with a large portion of those coming from Bryan Mbeumo.

The Cameroonian has four league goals to his name but could have scored more had he not spurned some big opportunities at important moments in games.

Matheus Cunha has been another source for goals, although he has largely flattered to deceive thus far.

Unfortunately the rest of United's attack have barely delivered many bright moments.

Marcus Rashford has zero goal involvements since returning from his Barcelona loan and his presence has upset the balance of the attack.

7 Rashford was reintegrated back into the United squad after Barcelona chose not to sign him permanently Credit: Getty

A pre-season disrupted by injury has not helped Amad Diallo, with his minutes still being managed.

Diallo will hope an assist in the Como debacle can provide some much-needed momentum to properly get his season up and running.

Fans are still hoping to see Patrick Dorgu recreate the form that earned him the nickname of 'Ballon D'orgu' early on under Carrick last season.

The left-sided ace has sadly regressed in the handful of games he's played this season and an injury sustained while on international duty hasn't helped.

Joshua Zirkzee has been game in coming off the bench and was particularly impactful in the 1-1 draw with Spurs, but has scored just one goal for United in the last ten months.

Continued injury issues for Benjamin Sesko has also hampered United's attack, with his prolonged absence proving to be a killer blow for Carrick.

7 It's been bad across the board at Man United

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes’ £4m home robbed by masked gang while he was away at Man United Champions League clash
Sports.content:
Bruno Fernandes’ £4m home robbed by masked gang while he was away at Man United Champions League clash

Bruno Fernandes' home was targeted by a masked gang during Manchester United's match against Como on Wednesday.

The midfielder's £4million mansion was broken into by three masked intruders whilst he was in Italy.

3 The burglary is understood to have taken place shortly after Man United's defeat to Como Credit: Getty

Police were pictured outside the Cheshire property on Thursday following the previous night's attack.

Fernandes' home raided

Thieves broke into the six-bedroom property at around 8:30pm on Wednesday night, The Sun reports.

It is understood luxury items including designer jewellery was stolen in the raid.

According to the Daily Mail, Fernandes' family were not at home when the incident occurred.

United are now supporting the player and are asking for privacy at what is a difficult time for both Fernandes and his family.

He had been in Italy at the time of the incident following United's 4-1 defeat to Como in the Champions League.

The Red Devils skipper played 67 minutes for Michael Carrick's side before being replaced by Joshua Zirkzee.

His home in Nether Alderley is located within the affluent 'Golden Triangle' area, home to several Premier League footballers.

The report adds neighbours spotted three 'unknown men' in the garden before alerting police.

Once officers arrived 10 minutes later, though, the suspects had gone.

3 Fernandes was in Italy at the time of the incident following United's clash with Como Credit: Getty

Cheshire Police statement

Cheshire Police have since launched a full investigation into the attack.

In a statement, a force spokesperson said: "At around 8.30pm on Wednesday 21 October, police were called to reports of suspicious activity at an address in the Alderley Park area of Nether Alderley.

"The caller reported three unknown men in the rear garden of a neighbouring property.

"Officers attended the scene and on arrival there was no trace of the suspects.

"However, officers discovered that there had been a burglary at the address and a number of items had been stolen."

Detective Inspector David Jarvis added: "This investigation is in its early stages at this time, and we’re committed to doing all we can to trace the people responsible.

3 Fernandes is the latest footballer to have his home targeted Credit: Getty

"As part of our enquiries, we’re keen to hear from anyone who was in the local area at the time and believes they may have witnessed anything suspicious."

The incident follows a similar raid on the home of Manchester City defender Ruben Dias in Alderley Edge back in January.

Jack Grealish, Raheem Sterling and Riyad Mahrez have also had their properties targeted in the past.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo becomes multi-billionaire as staggering net worth revealed
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo has topped a list of the world's highest-paid footballers for the third year in a row.

The Al Nassr forward's earning in 2026 have seen him become a multi-billionaire.

3 Ronaldo will reportedly earn £224million in 2026 Credit: instagram @alnassr

Ronaldo has already ranked as the best paid athlete in the world every year since 2023.

He has now extended his run as the highest-paid footballer on the planet in Forbes' latest money list.

According to the business magazine, Ronaldo will earn £224million this year across his Al Nassr salary, endorsements and business ventures.

It sees him rank ahead of World Cup winners Lionel Messi and Kylian Mbappe, who will take home £108million and £75million, respectively.

Meanwhile, Manchester City striker Erling Haaland (£64million) and Vinicius Jr of Real Madrid (£57million) complete the top five.

Ronaldo becomes multi-billionaire

Ronaldo's staggering earnings have seen the 41-year-old make a unique piece of financial history.

The Portugal international has become the first footballer to have a net worth of more than $2billion (£1.5billion).

He is also the first active athlete in sports history to surpass the figure in career earnings before taxes and agent fees.

Across the 2026/27 season, Ronaldo will earn £187million from his Al Nassr deal after his contract extension in June 2025.

His sponsorships and business ventures equate to a further £37million in earnings for the five-time Ballon d'Or winner.

3 Ronaldo is the first footballer to become a multi-billionaire Credit: Instagram / @cristiano

Ronaldo has endorsement deals with global brands including Lego, Nike, Panini and Whoop.

This year looks set to be his last at the top of Forbes' list of the highest-paid footballers, though.

He revealed in August that he expects the current season to be his last, with his Al Nassr contract expiring next summer.

Ronaldo will turn 42 in February, having made his senior debut as a 17-year-old in August 2002.

At present, he has scored 975 goals in 1,335 appearances for club and country as he closes in on his goal of 1,000 senior career goals.

Could Messi surpass Ronaldo's net worth?

As for Messi, the former Argentina captain's net worth is estimated to surpass the £1.5billion mark next year.

3 Messi's net worth is set to reach £1.5billion in 2025 Credit: Getty

This is in part thanks to his £52million-a-year Inter Miami salary following his contract extension in October 2025.

The 39-year-old is set to remain with the MLS side until the end of 2028, by which point he will have turned 41.

His off-field endeavours also see the forward earn a further £56million annually.

Messi has twice been named the world's highest-paid athlete in 2019 and 2022, with this year's list placing him third behind Ronaldo and legendary Mexican boxer Canelo Alvarez.

Sports.title: Neil Warnock outlines how Michael Carrick should deal with Bruno Fernandes at Man United
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick must hold a meeting with Bruno Fernandes and start him for Manchester United against Bournemouth on Sunday.

That's the view of legendary manager Neil Warnock, who knows the pair at not currently aligned with each other amid their worrying run of seven winless matches.



4 Fernandes vented his frustrations with Carrick's tactics after they were dispatched 4-1 by Como Credit: Getty

After a bleak 4-1 Champions League defeat to Como, United captain Fernandes took issue with their tactical approach to the match, particularly their decision to not play with man-to-man pressing.

His comments did not reflect well on under-fire head coach Carrick, who explained that when they half-pressed man-to-man during the second half, they conceded.

Carrick also appeared to dig out Fernandes and his commitment on the pitch as he added: "If you don't run, you don't run forward, you don't run back, you aren’t going to win."



Reacting to Fernandes' comments on talkSPORT Breakfast, Gabby Agbonlahor called for the 32-year-old to be dropped when they face Bournemouth at home in the Premier League this weekend.

However, despite having a reputation of being a fierce, no-nonsense manager, former Sheffield United and Crystal Palace boss Warnock thinks Carrick should take a more measured approach to the match.



Carrick must start Fernandes vs Bournemouth

"When things go wrong in a dressing room, players never look in the mirror, they always blame something else," he explained. "Whether it's the pitch, the ball, it used to be the boots and everything else, now it's the manager.

"I just thought it was a disgrace. Fernandes, about a year ago when he started waving his arms, I hated him from a manager's point of view. In fairness, he started playing and looked their best player, I thought, 'He's their best chance'.



"I understand what Gabby's saying about playing the kids, but you can't play the kids on Sunday, and you can't leave Fernandes out.

"He's going to have to have a chat with him and, however much he hates doing it, he'll play Fernandes on Sunday.

"He'll say, 'Come on, we're at home, get back to your way'."

4 Carrick, who currently faces the sack at United, has been told to drop his captain from his starting XI this weekend Credit: Getty

4 However, Warnock has stressed that he cannot drop Fernandes from the team despite his comments Credit: talkSPORT



Warnock then recalled last week's post-match rant from Lisandro Martinez after defeat to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League, during which he called out the United board.

"Martinez coming out like that, they're not bothered!" Warnock said. "They've got a club lined up, or they're going to go somewhere else. They're not bothered about the manager, I felt sorry for him (Carrick) last night."

Agbonlahor asked Warnock if he would be able to contain his anger if he was the United manager and heard what Fernandes said in his post-match interview.

"You're going to speak to him but, I'm not being funny, I think if you're captain is onside with you, he wouldn't even think about saying what he said," Warnock responded.



What next for Carrick?

talkSPORT understands that Carrick is still set to hold his pre-match press conference on Friday before the visit of Bournemouth and should be in charge of the team for Sunday's game.

However, United have taken steps to plan for a possible replacement, with former Germany and Bayern Munich boss Julian Nagelsmann being sounded out.

4 Warnock is also worried for Carrick and his future at United, and believes he would be better off with more experience around him Credit: AFP

Meanwhile, Brighton head coach Fabian Hurzeler has admirers at Old Trafford but would not be interested in taking the job, with Antonio Conte, Eddie Howe, Simone Inzaghi and Cesc Fabregas other options.



"I can't see a way out now for Michael," Warnock said. "I wish I could have worked with Michael.

"He's a lovely lad and he knows what he's doing. I think he just needs a bit of experience there with him as well."

Warnock added: "He's not going to walk away, but the guys at the top... it's almost like he wants to be relieved of his duties, really, he'll be pulling his hair out now.

"When people like Martinez and Fernandes have a go at the tactics, then he knows his time is limited.



"Unfortunately for managers, it's the easy way out, you're not going to get rid of the players."

Sports.title: Jason Cundy makes Man City comparison in explosive rant at Man United
Sports.content:
Jason Cundy has labelled Manchester United a 'car crash of a club', claiming they've swapped places with Manchester City.

His explosive outburst came after Man United fell to a chastening 4-1 Champions League defeat to competition newcomers Como on Wednesday.



2 Man United have lost their last two Champions League games and four of their last seven matches in all competitions Credit: Getty

What did Cundy say about Man United?

Alongside Jamie O'Hara on talkSPORT's Sports Bar, Cundy didn't hold back in his assessment of the current state of United.

"Honestly, watching Man United earlier: wowzers," exclaimed the former Chelsea and Tottenham defender. "What a car crash that club is.

"The thing is with Man United, they're going down the motorway, there's no brakes, and they keep hitting cars.



"Somehow, they're trundling on, and we know how this is going to end: they're going to hit a truck.

"And Carrick is still at the wheel. No brakes.

"For me, this is definitive: Manchester City have swapped places with Man United."



Cundy went on to accuse United of embarrassing English football.

"Man United are disgracing the Premier League in Europe and they're disgracing Manchester," he continued "They are an absolute disgrace."

Discussing Michael Carrick's future amid mounting pressure on the head coach, Cundy said: "He's not the solution, but he's not the problem. I don't know what the solution is.



"You go back to the 90s when Manchester United were the club - not just in England but in Europe, they were one of the best clubs if not the best club for years.

2 Appointed mid-season, Carrick steadied the ship and steered United to third in the Premier League last term, but they've managed a solitary league win so far this time around Credit: Getty

"Manchester City were hanging around, dwindling around mid-table.

"Now, Manchester United have turned into City and City have turned into Man United. That's what's happened. They have literally swapped seats."

Yet another setback for Carrick's United

United fell into further turmoil on Wednesday night as captain Bruno Fernandes hit out at Carrick's tactics post-match.



Fernandes had been hauled off after 66 minutes with United 3-0 down in Italy.

His rant came barely a week after teammate Lisandro Martinez had taken aim at the board for not assembling a squad good enough for the Champions League.

Carrick's days certainly appear to be numbered at Old Trafford, with United winless in seven games heading into Sunday's home Premier League clash against Bournemouth.

talkSPORT understands that former Bayern Munich and Germany boss Julian Nagelsmann is in the frame to take over should Carrick be sacked but that Fabian Hurzeler, currently doing a stellar job at Brighton, would not be interested in the job.

Sports.title: West Ham star Edson Alvarez accused of selling fake Covid-19 certificates in 'illicit' scheme during the pandemic along with his former father-in-law... just weeks after kidnapping allegation
Sports.content:
West Ham midfielder Edson Alvarez and his former father-in-law have been accused of selling false Covid-19 vaccination certificates during the pandemic.

The allegation has been made by the same film producer who accused the footballer of being linked to a kidnapping in Mexico just weeks ago.

Filmmaker Juan Jose Lopez Ordonez told Mexican outlet TV Notas in September that the family of Alvarez's former father-in-law Jonathan Toache Bedolla forced him into a vehicle at gunpoint in Mexico City in 2024. He claimed the West Ham star was aware of the kidnapping, although not directly involved.

Alvarez, who strenuously denied the accusation, has now been accused of falsifying Covid-19 certificates along with Bedolla and a doctor.

As reported by Mexican outlet El Financiero, Ordonez claimed in a press conference on Thursday that the trio allegedly sold fake Covid-19 vaccination certificates that included stamps, signatures and even a QR code.

The producer, who claims to have witnessed how the illicit forgery network operated, said: 'The moral burden is very heavy, and here I am facing the music. If I bear any responsibility, the authorities will determine that, but I can no longer hide this.'

West Ham's Edson Alvarez has been accused of selling false Covid-19 vaccination certificates

According to Ordonez and various Mexican publications, the fake Covid-19 certificates were sold for upwards of $500 (£370) each.

The alleged operation is said to have enabled several high-profile figures to travel abroad while bypassing Covid-19 restrictions during the pandemic.

Alvarez's alleged links to the counterfeit document scheme have come under scrutiny recently after a list of public figures who reportedly obtained the certificates was leaked.

Fashion model Montserrat Oliver, actress Yolanda Andrade, musician Jay de la Cueva and actor Alfredo Adame are among the Mexican celebrities named in the leaked document, according to the report. It is claimed they, among others, sought false certificates from Alvarez and his former father-in-law to avoid vaccination.

As falsifying public health documents is a federal crime in Mexico, authorities may launch an official investigation. Daily Mail Sport has approached Alvarez for comment on the latest allegation.

Addressing the kidnapping accusation made by film producer Ordonez last month, Alvarez said: 'I categorically reject any allegation or attempt to associate my name with events, conflicts, or conduct that are entirely unrelated to me.'

West Ham, who sit second in the Championship, are gearing up to face Southampton at the London Stadium on Saturday.

The Mexican has not been included in a single Championship matchday squad so far this season, having failed to secure a move away from the Hammers this summer.

Sports.title: Harry Brook's eye-watering double century against Sri Lanka proved he is now the best all-format batsman in the world - this is how he got there, writes LAWRENCE BOOTH
Sports.content:
If there were any doubt before this morning’s events in Rawalpindi, there can be none now. Harry Brook is the best all-format batsman in the world, and few bowlers appear to know how to handle him. On Tuesday, it’s true, he was outfoxed by Pakistan left-arm spinner Arafat Minhas, bowled for five by a delivery that gripped and turned, before defeating him on the back foot. There have been moments this year when Brook has felt like his own worst enemy, apparently heading for a century before doing something daft. But it’s getting to the stage where – like Minhas – the bowler has to produce something special to keep him quiet. If not, he’s going to cause you a world of pain. The raw numbers of today’s demolition of Sri Lanka are eye-watering in their own right. A double-century off 114 balls was the quickest in ODI history, beating by three balls Shubman Gill’s blitz for India against West Indies in Guwahati as recently as three weeks ago. His eventual 202 was the highest ODI score in an England shirt, surpassing Ben Stokes’s 182 against New Zealand at The Oval in 2023. And he helped his side to the highest total in Pakistan, beating Pakistan’s own 375 for three against Zimbabwe at Lahore in 2015. Brook also became only the second player, after West Indies’ Chris Gayle, to possess a triple-century in Tests, a double-century in ODIs, and a single century in T20s. Harry Brook walks off after his electrifying 202 against Sri Lanka - the first Englishman ever to score a double century in ODI cricket What took the innings to another level was its 360-degree nonchalance, the idea that no ball was safe, no area of the ground out of reach

Your browser does not support iframes.

But what took the innings to another level was its 360-degree nonchalance, the idea that no ball was safe, no area of the ground out of reach. When Sri Lanka’s bowlers dropped short, he pulled. When they pitched it up, he either scooped, reverse-scooped or went over extra cover. The eighth of his 10 sixes, an open-faced slice over backward point off Eshan Malinga, was simply ridiculous. Only the pinpoint yorker had any chance of slowing the carnage, and even then you couldn’t be sure. As Nasser Hussain put it on Sky Sports: ‘That was an innings touched by genius.’ Kumar Sangakkara spoke of ‘batting Nirvana’. The superlatives are drying up. Brook is making a case that is hard to answer. In Tests, he averages 53, with a strike rate – 86 – that would once have been considered a triumph in one-day cricket. In T20, he averages a very good 36 with a pulsating strike rate of 164; in February, his 50-ball century against Pakistan in Pallekele was arguably the innings of the World Cup. And now, in ODIs, he is averaging 41 with a strike rate of almost 110. The sense in all three formats, and especially the longer two, is that there is room for improvement. Who else can challenge him as the world’s best all-format player? Gill himself is in the argument, though he hasn’t played a T20 for India since last December. Then there’s Australia’s Travis Head, who – while Brook was destroying Sri Lanka – fell for 121 as his side failed to save the second Test against South Africa in Gqeberha, losing by an innings and 31 runs to set up a series decider in Cape Town next week. Head has played some seismic innings on the biggest stages, including 163 to help beat India in the World Test Championship final at the Oval in 2023, followed by a match-winning 137 to break Indian hearts in the World Cup final at Ahmedabad a few months later. Last winter, he tore England apart in the Ashes. But not even he can boast Brook’s range of strokes and imagination; nor can he quite convey the same sense that, at any given moment, a perfectly respectable delivery is about to disappear to kingdom come. Head is 33 in December, and may have reached his ceiling. Brook is 27, and seems to be getting better. Shubman Gill is one of the few players who gets close to Brook, but he hasn’t played a T20 for India since last December Travis Head has played some phenomenal innings in the last few years (pictured at Perth in the recent Ashes) but he does not have Brook's range of strokes or imagination So dominant was he this morning that other innings, which might usually have grabbed the headlines, ranked only as sideshows. Tom Banton made a powerful run-a-ball 50 before picking out long-off, Joe Root moved past 8,000 ODI runs during his typically unobtrusive 69 off 66, before Will Jacks – the only England player other than Brook to clear the ropes – chipped in with a superb 66 not out off 30 balls. None, though, could live with Brook, who didn’t allow himself a proper celebration until he lapped Janith Liyanage fine for four in the last over of the innings to bring up his 200. At the other end, Jacks seemed even more excited. England’s 50-over cricket has been mainly in the doldrums ever since Eoin Morgan’s side lifted the 2019 World Cup. But, under Brook and Brendon McCullum, they are finding their feet. Tuesday’s defeat by Pakistan showed they are not there yet. Yet if Brook keeps batting like this, no team will relish facing England in next year’s World Cup.

Sports.title: Widow of Middlesbrough icon Willie Maddren calls for greater protection for footballers over link between headers and fatal MND - which caused Rob Burrow's premature death
Sports.content:
Widow of Middlesbrough icon Willie Maddren calls for greater protection for footballers over link between headers and fatal MND - which caused Rob Burrow's premature death

Long before Rob Burrow's brutal illness and premature death launched Sir Kevin Sinfield on his quest to raise millions for research into motor neurone disease (MND) there was Willie Maddren.

For Teessiders of a certain age, Maddren needs no introduction.

For the benefit of others, he was a local hero at the heart of a glorious era for Middlesbrough, a fearless centre forward converted into a fearless centre half in Jack Charlton's brilliant team promoted as runaway second tier champions in 1974.

They rattled the elite on their return to the topflight with an unlikely tilt at the title before a late fade to finish seventh.

England recognition came for Maddren at Under-23 level and senior call-ups in the 1974-75 season, but there would be no full cap before knee problems set in and cut short his playing career.

At 26, with 351 Boro appearances behind him, he retired. Later, he returned as physio and manager and, at the age of 44, was diagnosed with MND. He died in 2000 at 49.

Middlesbrough icon Willie Maddren needs no introduction on Teesside but following his retirement, the centre half received a heartbreaking MND diagnosis

After his death at the age of 49, his widow Hilary has become outspoken raising awareness of the connection between the disease and his playing career

More than a quarter of a century on, Sinfield is on a mission to beat the disease that killed his teammate Burrow, raising more than £11million to fund much-needed research.

There is still no sign of a cure. Precious little is known about the causes but as the list of sports stars with MND extends, Maddren's widow Hilary has become increasingly convinced that their athletic pursuits are central to the problem, whether that be the shuddering contact in rugby or heading the ball in football.

'There's got to be a connection,' Hilary tells Daily Mail Sport from her home in North Yorkshire. 'I follow it all closely and it takes me back with a slight sadness to see it happening to such a huge extent.

'It's quite frightening there's so many of them, that's the problem. I realise that you can't just go around bandying these things about, but it feels strange to me nothing is said.

'We know in football, heading the ball is causing neurodegenerative diseases. Years ago, we found out there was a bigger chance of getting lung cancer if you smoked. Not everybody with lung cancer smoked but now we know it is a contributing factor.

'When you see the percentage of rugby players and footballers, this has got to be the same thing with MND. There's nothing definitive, I know nothing is proven but it's got to be.

'I'm not trying to blame anybody. Willie would not want to blame anybody. I'm not on a witch hunt. I don't want to stop anyone playing the game, but I have nine grandchildren and nearly all of them are football mad. It's about education and being aware of heading the ball.'

The Maddrens are one of five families – all connected to Boro – leading a new campaign for clear legal limits to reduce heading in training which they believe will protect future generations from the post-career health problems they have witnessed at close quarters.

It is led by the Head Safe charity founded by Judith Gates, whose husband was a friend and teammate of Maddren's. Bill Gates, who retired before he was 30 suffering serious migraines, died three years ago at the age of 79 after living for years with dementia.

Others at the forefront of the campaign are families of England World Cup hero Nobby Stiles, Gordon McQueen and Hugh McIlmoyle.

Stiles, who died in 2020 aged 78, played for Boro after leaving Manchester United. Scotland legend McQueen, who died in 2023 aged 70, coached at the club for seven years and later worked for them as a scout.

McIlmoyle, 86 years old and diagnosed with Alzheimer's eight years ago, spent two seasons at Ayresome Park during his prolific career as a centre-forward in the 60s and 70s.

Gary Pallister, a former Boro, Manchester United and England defender, is also backing the cause.

When Pallister spoke at the launch of a new petition which the group hopes will force the matter into the House of Commons, he was embarrassed because he could not summon the name of Maddren, the man who had plucked him from the obscurity of non-league Billingham Town.

Former Manchester United star Gary Pallister is among the ex-players to throw their support behind the cause

Hilary teased him afterwards. 'Oh my God, you've got it already,' she said, although acutely aware that behind this light-hearted exchange between friends lurked a serious point.

'Gary and his contemporaries are into their early 60s. They've played their football and headed all those balls. It must be a little bit worrying when they start forgetting things.

'What's ahead? Are they going to suffer dementia? It feels like a ticking time bomb.'

Studies have proved the link between heading the ball and chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), a degenerative brain disease which can lead in later life to different forms of dementia.

MND is slightly different but nevertheless a neurodegenerative condition which damages the nerves sending messages to the muscles. Over time, they stop working and the muscles weaken. It is terminal and often health deteriorates quickly.

Maddren's first sign of the disease was a twitch in a thumb later spreading to an arm, then to the other arm, by which point it had become clear it was not a trapped nerve as he hoped.

In search of reason, he wondered if it was to do with stress from the end of his playing career, and the long hours spent on his business running sports shops and managing Boro in crisis when the club he loved was going into liquidation.

But there seemed no point wasting time searching for answers he could never expect to find, he was determined to spend what limited time he had trying to enjoy life and make a difference.

Middlesbrough held a benefit match and proceeds enabled Maddren to adapt his home and transport to his wheelchair, and he threw himself into raising funds and awareness.

He took part in a clinical trial for riluzole, a drug that is now prescribed in treatment.

Proceeds from his book 'Extra Time' went to the MND Association and funds continued to be raised long after his death, estimated close to £500,000. His family including four children from two marriages, friends, former colleagues and Boro fans joined forces.

His eldest daughter, artist Lucy Pittaway, maintains an active partnership with the charity.

'Willie was convinced if you threw enough money at it, you would find a cause and a cure,' says Hilary, who has continued to campaign tirelessly and worked in volunteer roles for MND charities and others.

'We still don't have a huge amount of hope anybody can be given when they receive the diagnosis. It's not a lot different.

'The incredible amount raised in Rob Burrow's name will make huge inroads.'

Leeds Rhinos legend Burrow died in 2024 at the age of 37. Other international stars from the two codes of rugby include Scotland's Doddie Weir who died in 2022 at 52 and Joost van der Westhuizen of South Africa who died in 2017 at 45.

Lewis Moody, 48, revealed last year he was living with MND. Earlier this month, former Wallabies hooker Nathan Charles, 37, revealed he too had been diagnosed.

The MND Association notes the patterns but notes 'correlation does not prove causation' and that the health benefits of playing sport far outweigh any risks involved.

From football, Marcus Stewart and Stephen Darby are living with MND. Former Rangers favourite Fernando Ricksen died in 2019 at the age of 43. Lenny Johnrose, who played for Bury and Burnley among others, died in 2022 at the age of 52.

'Willie loved his life,' says Hilary. 'He thought he'd had an amazing life and was so lucky to have done the things he wanted to do. He played football for a living. He managed his club, albeit that wasn't brilliant, but he was involved in football, he loved it.

'And if you would have said to him, well this might be the cause of what's going to kill you, would he have done any different? Possibly not. And that's how I feel now. Don't blame anybody, let's draw a line, but we need to learn from it.

'Anybody who has seen the slow-motion footage of a clash of heads or a rugby tackle when you see the head thrown back, it's not a good sign, it's not the way our bodies are meant to work and it's got to be doing something. It's just got to be.'

Sports.title: Victories like this show Bournemouth's top stars that the club is no stepping stone as they enjoy another night to cherish in 3-0 humbling of Ruben Amorim's AC Milan, writes KIERAN GILL
Sports.content:
Victories like this show Bournemouth's top stars that the club is no stepping stone as they enjoy another night to cherish in 3-0 humbling of Ruben Amorim's AC Milan, writes KIERAN GILL

At £15 a pop, the half-and-half scarf sellers outside of the Vitality Stadium were cleaning up, and while those souvenirs are often derided as cringe fodder for tourists, there was no blaming those Bournemouth fans queueing to buy one this time.

On the one half, Bournemouth, a club beaten 2-1 at home by Bury in League One 15 years ago on this night. On the other, AC Milan, the Italian behemoths and seven-time conquerors of Europe.

It was only once inside the Vitality that those supporters found a free scarf awaiting them courtesy of their club, reading: ‘We are all going on a European tour.’ Not to worry. They would happily take multiple mementoes from this – the night AFC Bournemouth famously flattened AC Milan.

There was a special feel to it all, from the fireworks exploding over the Vitality to the playing of Andy Williams's The Impossible Dream to the enormous tifo reading: ‘How did we end up here?’

A few in the Milan end may have been asking themselves the same, especially when their once-great team was trailing 1-0 after eight minutes and 2-0 after 32 in this Europa League fixture.

Both of those goals were penalties – Justin Kluivert scoring one and Marcus Tavernier the other – while Milan then spent the remainder of this match playing with 10 men as their goalkeeper Mike Maignan was red carded for shoving Tyler Adams in the face.

Bournemouth rolled over visitors AC Milan 3-0 in a historic outing at the Vitality Stadium

15 years on from facing liquidation, fans will savour this impressive showing on the continent

By the end, when Amine Adli delivered the coup de grâce with a 25-yard free-kick, Ruben Amorim could only laugh. Literally, the former Manchester United manager now in charge of Milan chuckled as Bournemouth’s supporters serenaded him with: ‘Ruben Amorim, it’s happened again.’

Considering one Italian journalist in the press box angrily ripped his accreditation to smithereens as the visitors trailed 3-0, Amorim’s smiling response may not go down too well back home.

Yet our newspaper counterparts from Italy saw this coming. They were wearing a told-you-so look after it all, having warned us this would happen. ‘You don’t understand,’ one said when asked before kick-off. ‘This isn’t the AC Milan of old.’ Indeed it is not, and Amorim tried to hide behind Maignan’s dismissal afterwards: ‘We need 11 players on the pitch at all times. We killed our game.’

Bournemouth boss Marco Rose added: ‘Our club, we stay humble. We know we are good. If we have the whole squad, we know we can compete with anyone, anywhere. But the season is long. We have so many games. Sunday, Wednesday, Sunday. It’s so demanding.’

Bournemouth might not have even existed were it not for their former chairman Jeff Mostyn, who was here as a fan, writing another £100,000 cheque to save them from liquidation in 2008.

This represented a major milestone for them in their first-ever season in Europe, and while Bournemouth were happy to embrace this as extraordinary on this occasion, they want these nights to become the norm. Their owner, Bill Foley, is striving for that and victories like this cannot hurt show their better players such as Chelsea target Alex Scott why this club is no stepping stone.

Bournemouth won here even without the injured Scott. Rose’s side took the lead when Evanilson headed Tavernier’s cross, but Koni De Winter handled the ball on its way wide. Nobody in the stadium noticed it, but VAR Dennis Higler of the Netherlands did, and then referee Vassilis Fotias of Greece did, too, via his monitor. Kluivert rolled the ball into the bottom-right corner for 1-0.

Amorim’s anger with his players was already rising in the technical area when Maignan pushed Adams in the face at a Bournemouth corner. The whistle was blown. Again, hardly a soul in the crowd knew what was happening until Maignan was shown a straight red card.

AC Milan are a far cry from their status in the game as the seven-time European champions

Milan were further reduced when Mike Maignan was handed a straight red card for pushing Tyler Adams in the face

Needing to bring on replacement goalkeeper Lorenzo Torriani, the unfortunate one sacrificed was Omari Hutchinson, the 22-year-old whose shin pads carry a picture of himself representing England’s Under 21s. A new taker in Tavernier made it 2-0.

Adli’s free-kick in the 84th minute capped this victory with Milan ending the match without a single shot on target. Even with 10 men, that was an embarrassing statistic.

This was a night to cherish for Bournemouth, now winners in all three of their Europa League outings. Indeed, a fair few will hang those scarves in their homes as a reminder. But as a club aiming to go places, they hope this is just the first of many matches with European heavyweights.

Sports.title: Jean-Philippe Mateta gives Crystal Palace hope, Sunderland squander lead against the Europa League's WORST team - and free-scoring Brighton misfire in drab draw with Czech minnows
Sports.content:
'After the dark the eagle rises,’ read the gigantic banner unfurled across one stand inside the Tupras Stadium. For so long, against all expectations, against all form, it looked as if it was going to be the Eagles of south London, not of 10-man Besiktas, that soared on this night in Istanbul. How much better this Crystal Palace side looked even with a half-fit Jean-Philippe Mateta leading the line. How much his performance, scoring what briefly looked to be the winner in his first start since the opening game of the season after a hamstring injury, showed what they have missed. How much character they looked to have showed to turn up at the loudest stadium in Europe - ‘welcome to hell,’ as the old saying goes - with the worst defence in the Premier League, on the back of a thumping 5-0 defeat to Brighton that left Pierre Sage hanging by a thread, to come from behind and so nearly win it - only for, once again, their old failings to cost them victory. Sage had talked of using the intense atmosphere that would be waiting for them to their advantage. He called on Palace to fight. And, for so long, they did. Palace pressed relentlessly from the front and Besiktas could not deal with it. Mateta thought he’d scored his first Palace goal since the winner in the Conference League final last season when he rounded off one of many slick passing moves only for VAR to rule it out for a marginal offside. Jean Philippe-Mateta's return to the starting line-up instantly made Crystal Palace look better and he scored Mateta could have a bunch. He only just missed getting on the end of Adam Wharton’s cross, and then volleyed one of his corners straight at the keeper. And yet, even without Mateta, it’s never been Palace’s willingness to attack that’s caused them all their problems. It’s been what happens behind it. For most of it, there was such a better balance to Palace’s play. They were much tighter at the back, for so long they kept Besiktas to just a handful of shots. They looked compact, they celebrated tackles like goals. But on this stage, you only need to switch off briefly to get punished and that, again, is what happened. On the stroke of half-time, a simple long ball over the top found Wilfed Ndidi, who had raced forward untracked to latch on to it and drill it into the bottom corner. Palace, to their credit, refused to crumble. They came out for the second half strong and despite the officials trying to rule out another goal for offside, levelled when Yeremy Pino scored from Anan Khalaili’s cross. And then Mateta pounced on a poor back pass from Tiago Djalo and drilled his effort into the top corner. But this Palace and they simply cannot rely on keeping the ball out. Daichi Kamada and Dario Osorio stood still to watch substitute Junior Olaitan drift past them and fire past Walter Benitez from distance. Umit Akdag’s red card with 15 minutes to spare gave Sage’s side hope of snatching a winner but couldn’t find a way through. The performance was so much better but it was the same old issues that clipped the Eagles wings once again. Lech Poznan 1-1 Sunderland, by Luke Power Goalkeeper Robin Roefs looked to the heavens and shouted 'f***!’ Regis Le Bris stood brooding off stage. Sunderland had been breached, and it had been coming. In a dismal domestic season for Sunderland, they have been able to count on their European travels for a sprinkle of light relief, however hard-fought. Until now, that is. There is no papering over the cracks after a troubling night at Lech Poznan, where a strong starting XI that included Granit Xhaka hobbled to a draw against the Europa League’s basement boys. It had all started so rosily when Timur Tutierov – a Crimean refugee whose very existence is a tribute to his resilience – scored his first goal for the club with a header after just 78 seconds. But in front of one of central Europe’s more forbidding crowds, Sunderland failed to handle the frenetic, end-to-end pulsations of this game and eventually wilted. To their credit, the Black Cats were on top for large swathes of the game, having 22 shots, but Nordi Mukiele, Malick Fofana, and Chris Rigg all saw chances go begging and the visitors were punished for their profligacy. Sunderland drew 1-1 at Lech Poznan in the Europa League despite leading after just 78 seconds Timor Tutierov had given Sunderland the lead with a header after just 78 seconds But Leo Bengtsson spoiled the party with a deserved equaliser for the hosts in the second half It is not the end of the world for Sunderland, who sit eighth in the Europa League standings, but it leaves much to be desired after narrow wins over AZ and second-tier Portuguese outfit Torreense. To put the result in context, Lech Poznan arrived at this game bottom of the Europa League after 4-0 drubbings by Crystal Palace and Bayer Leverkusen. This is not the side who once beat Manchester City. And for the 2,000 Mackems who made this trip, and filled Poznan’s Old Town with their songs, the performance did little to part the dark clouds which have recently congealed over the Stadium of Light. Sunderland sit bottom of the Premier League with one point in their last five games and Le Bris, for all his brilliant achievements in the North East, has started to come under pressure. There are no suggestions of the Frenchman’s position being immediately at threat – and there should not be – but even he has admitted that Sunderland have not been themselves recently. A side known for their solidity last season have opened this campaign with a comedy of errors and ill discipline. They lead the way for mistakes leading to goals in the league, having already committed five. Mukiele recently accused his own team-mates of 'arrogance'. This performance was no different, with Kevin Danso error-prone once again, and picking up a booking for dragging down Mikael Ishak while trying to atone for his own miscontrol. Most worrying was the ping-pong feel of the game, which saw 32 shots, and several gilt-edged chances for the Polish side to snatch a win after Leo Bengtsson's 70th-minute equaliser. Roefs had to make an incredible double save shortly after the goal to hold off the hosts. In the absence of Brian Brobbey and Wilson Isidor, Sunderland's front four buzzed around with energy, but the wastefulness will worry Le Bris. Leeds are up next before a trip to Coventry on Halloween, with the chance for things to get hairy if Sunderland flop again. Jablonec 0-0 Brighton, Press Association Brighton drew a rare blank as they were held to a goalless draw by Czech minnows Jablonec in the Conference League. The Premier League’s top scorers, who have scored 23 goals across their first seven matches, misfired badly in the foothills of the Jizera Mountains in northern Czechia. Jablonec coach Lubos Kozel had said his side would need a “miracle” to get anything from the match. It turned out they only needed a below-par display from the favourites to lift the trophy to take a point, and in fact they could have had all three. Around 1,000 Seagulls fans made the trip from the Sussex coast to the homely Stadion Strelnice in the city of Jablonec nad Nisou. These are heady days for their team, who lie third in the English top flight, fresh from Sunday’s 5-0 thrashing of M23 rivals Crystal Palace. Brighton, typically so prolific this season, were held to a goalless draw by Czech side Jablonec Boss Fabian Hurzeler, in his 100th match in charge, made eight changes from that memorable win with only Bart Verbruggen, Olivier Boscagli and the omnipresent Pascal Gross keeping their places. They pinned the hosts in their own half for the first 20 minutes but Jack Hinshelwood’s shot was saved by Jablonec keeper Jan Hanus while Gross and Ibrahim Osman were off target. Jablonec eventually got far enough forward to win a corner, which Antonín Rusek headed narrowly wide. Goalkeeper Verbruggen also had to be alert to smother a cute backheel from Rusek. But they were rare moments of concern for the Seagulls, although they were frustrated in front of goal in the first half. Georginio Rutter was cleverly put through by Gross but flashed his shot across the face of goal and wide, and Boscagli fired over from long range. Early in the second half Rutter’s pass found Osman, but his effort flew wide before Malick Yalcouye tucked the ball into the net, only to be flagged offside. Then Osman’s reverse pass got Matt O’Riley in behind, but his fizzing ball across the six-yard box could not find Rutter. Hurzeler had seen enough after Osman blazed another chance high over the crossbar, making four changes with Chema Andres, Luka Vuskovic, Yasin Ayari and Promise David sent on. However, the changes had little effect and Jablonec were looking the likelier to score towards the end. Rusek almost capitalised on a mistake by Joao Costinha before Verbruggen had to make a spectacular fingertip save to prevent Jiri Slama’s drive from hitting the top corner. Rutter, who scored twice in Brighton’s opening 4-0 victory over Kauno Zalgiris, had a chance to win it in stoppage time but his snapshot was beaten away by Hanus.

Sports.title: Lewis Hamilton vows to carry on in F1 until he's 46: Seven-time world champion says he's been forced to stay because of planned race in Africa
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton has vowed to carry on racing in Formula One until at least 2031 to complete a long-desired ambition to compete in Africa.

He is 41 now and will be 46 then, if the earliest date for the first grand prix planned for Rwanda is delivered upon – though it may be a year later depending on how the development of a proposed circuit being built in Bugesera, 25 miles south of the capital Kigali, progresses.

The exact year the much-vaunted race will start is yet to be decided, set to be 2031, yet conceivably a year later.

The deal with Africa was announced last week and answered Hamilton’s desire for a new race to be staged on the continent from which his paternal family descend, after the last event there took place in Kyalami, South Africa, in 1993.

Ahead of the US Grand Prix in Austin, Texas, this weekend, Hamilton said: ‘I’m now forced to stay a bit longer because we have a race in Africa and that has been my dream to race in Africa. So, I’m going to have to keep fighting to stay fit. If I can keep punching out results over the next years, we will keep it going.’

Rwanda is a controversial presence in British sport over its human rights record and alleged ‘sportswashing’ with the ‘Visit Rwanda’ brand drawing criticism as a sponsor of Arsenal for eight years, before ending in June. ‘Visit Rwanda’ are now Aston Villa’s main shirt sponsor.

Lewis Hamilton is determined to race in Africa before he retires, which could see him race at 46

Amnesty International UK’s head of campaigns Felix Jakes said recently: ‘Rwanda is buying into the world's biggest sports to polish its image and deflect from its appalling human rights record.

‘Formula One says sport can be "a positive force for good". That rings hollow if F1 shrugs off who it is partnering with. Formula One must not be a bystander. It should use its influence with the Rwandan authorities to push for change, rather than lend its brand to a PR exercise.’

The United Nations and Western governments accuse Rwanda of backing the armed rebel group M23 with weapons and troops to fight a proxy war inside the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). Rwanda deny supporting the insurgency.

Millions of civilians in eastern DRC have been displaced or killed as the conflict spirals into a humanitarian crisis.

Sports.title: Ruben Amorim FUMES at officials after AC Milan goalkeeper is sent off for pushing Bournemouth star in the FACE - as ex-Man United boss tries to bring on a replacement without taking anyone off!
Sports.content:
Ruben Amorim went ballistic on the touchline as he suffered a nightmare return to England, losing 3-0 with AC Milan at Bournemouth in the Europa League. The former Manchester United manager was furious that his goalkeeper Mike Maignan was sent off in the first half for pushing Tyler Adams in the face. Amorim flew off the handle on the sidelines and fronted up to the fourth official, but had little cause for complain as his side's European middling campaign took a turn for the worse. And there appeared to be a mix-up on the touchline as he sent on replacement Lorenzo Torriani before bringing anybody off, leading to ridicule. Bournemouth could hardly have imagined a more generous start to their glamour tie, as Milan gifted them two penalties in a first half of anarchy and farce. They were already 1-0 up thanks to Justin Kluivert's penalty when Maignan's head-loss gifted Marcus Tavernier a spot-kick, which he promptly scored. Ruben Amorim was furious when his goalkeeper was sent off as AC Milan visited Bournemouth Mike Maignan was given his marching orders after shoving Tyler Adams in the face Amorim gave the fourth official a piece of his mind but ducked out of confronting the referee Maignan hung around for a couple of minutes during a VAR check and left the field reluctantly, giving referee Vassilis Fotias a piece of his mind. Omari Hutchinson appeared disappointed to come off early to make way for substitute goalkeeper Torrianai and Amorim comforted him. Milan regained their composure to get to half-time only 2-0 down, but Amorim waited by the touchline for the officials, seemingly ready to give them an earful. Yet when the officials reached him, the Portuguese gaffer seemingly bit his lip and it was unclear if he said a word to them before stalking off. Towards the end of the match, Amorim could only hang his head in disappointment as Amine Adli curled in a free-kick for Bournemouth to make it 3-0. Amorim has had an average start at AC Milan, who sit fourth in Serie A and 24th in the Europa League - the final play-off spot. The 41-year-old has stuck by the three-at-the-back system which saw him fail at United but has hinted he could adapt. While derided for his stubbornness at Old Trafford, he said after a 2-0 defeat by Benfica last month: 'I change all the time, we need to start with a base, we have two months of work. Amine Adli's stunning free-kick gave Bournemouth a 3-0 win and left Amorim stunned 'We lost tonight, but we will find the solutions to adapt to these games, because we need to create an idea, but we also need to win, so of course we can adapt.' Amorim was sacked in January with United sixth in the Premier League after a £250million summer spend. He was in charge at Old Trafford for 14 months during a turbulent period in which United endured their worst season in more than half a century and missed out on Europe for only the second time in 35 years. In an explosive final press conference, the man who led United to the 2025 Europa League final said: 'I came here to be the manager of Manchester United… not to be the coach of Manchester United. That is clear.' Returning to England, he has been asked about the future of Michael Carrick, his successor who has United 13th in the Premier League. 'The most important thing is that I am here as the manager of Milan, and I need to respect that,' he said. 'What I said when I signed for Manchester United, that I love that club and the people there, remains true. 'What happened since doesn't change that. That's all I want to say on the matter. I've moved on and I'm at another great club now. My club, Milan, has plenty of issues to address. 'I'm focused on my own life and our collective journey here because, as you know, at any big club, challenges are always just around the corner. So, I am fully focused on my work, my team, my players and my staff, not on what's happening at another club. 'But, as I said, it doesn't matter what happened in the past with Manchester United. My feelings from when I first joined that club remain exactly the same. I still love that club.'
