The governor said the 2027 budget represented a 2.57 per cent increase compared with the 2026 budget.

“Capital expenditure accounts for about 72 per cent of the total budget, while recurrent expenditure stands at N279.38 billion, representing 28.28 per cent,” he said.

The governor said his administration had not obtained fresh domestic or external loans since assuming office in 2023, noting that the state’s existing debt burden was mainly inherited from previous administrations.

He pledged to strengthen internally generated revenue and attract private investment to finance development projects.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Reviewing the 2026 budget, Mr Otu said the government raised the spending framework to N963.07 billion through a supplementary budget to accommodate urgent interventions and counterpart-funding requirements.

He listed past achievements, including about 608 km of road projects, support for 8,000 farmers with over 20,000 bags of fertiliser, and the distribution of one million improved seedlings, among others.

READ ALSO: ICPC indicts Budget Office over inclusion of fake agency in 2026 budget

The governor also listed improvements to healthcare and education infrastructure, payment of WAEC fees for indigenes, and the promotion of 14,000 teaching and non-teaching staff as other achievements.

“Infrastructure received the largest sectoral allocation of N246.1 billion, followed by education with N99.6 billion, health with N85.4 billion, and agriculture with N28.2 billion,” he said.

Mr Otu also identified aviation, transportation, and maritime development as key areas for economic diversification.

He urged the assembly to consider and pass the appropriation bill, and pledged his administration’s commitment to prudent management of public resources.

The governor said the budget would consolidate ongoing projects and promote inclusive growth and improved welfare for Cross River residents.

(NAN)

World.title: NEC endorses 90-day plan to ease cost of living for Nigerians, but no specific details yet
World.content:
The National Economic Council (NEC) has endorsed what it described as a “90-day economic action plan” to ease the cost-of-living crisis caused by government policies and worsened by international wars.

The plan was announced by the spokesperson to Vice President Kashim Shettima, Stanley Nkwocha, in a statement on Thursday.

The statement did not, however, contain specific details of the plan but stated that

“The plan focuses on reducing the cost of living, improving food affordability, attracting investment, and accelerating the delivery of projects with direct benefits to Nigerians.”

Mr Nkwocha added that “The 90-day action plan identifies five priority areas: food affordability, tax harmonisation, completion of high-impact projects, resolution of investment bottlenecks and regulated household support.”

PREMIUM TIMES reports that Nigerians have, since President Bola Tinubu assumed office, been experiencing the country’s worst cost-of-living crisis in a generation. This was first caused by government policies, including the removal of petrol subsidies and the deregulation of the foreign exchange market. The wars between the US/Israel and Iran, as well as the Russia-Ukraine war, exacerbated the crisis.

The government has repeatedly argued that the policies were essential to stave off a government collapse and that Nigerians will soon enjoy the benefits of the policies.

The policies have improved Nigeria’s macro-economy, with external reserves and foreign investment increasing significantly. However, most of Nigeria’s 200 million people have had to grapple with higher food costs than when Mr Tinubu assumed office.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The 90-day plan was presented by the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, during the NEC’s 161st meeting held virtually and chaired by Vice President Kashim Shettima on Thursday.

According to Mr Nkwocha, the NEC also deliberated on Nigeria’s preparedness following the detection of a case of Ebola virus in Abuja, as well as the efforts to eradicate all types of polio from the country.

PREMIUM TIMES reports that the NEC is statutorily headed by the vice president and includes all sitting state governors.

Read Mr Nkwocha’s full statement below.

The National Economic Council (NEC) has endorsed a 90-day economic action plan proposed by the Federal Ministry of Finance to consolidate gains from President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms.

The plan focuses on reducing the cost of living, improving food affordability, attracting investment, and accelerating the delivery of projects with direct benefits to Nigerians.

The council’s endorsement on Thursday followed a presentation by the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, during its 161st meeting held virtually and chaired by Vice President Kashim Shettima.

This is just as the vice president said that while President Tinubu’s economic reform programme was designed to achieve broader national prosperity, governments at all levels have a responsibility to translate its objectives into improved living conditions for Nigerians.

The 90-day action plan identifies five priority areas: food affordability, tax harmonisation, completion of high-impact projects, resolution of investment bottlenecks and regulated household support.

NEC also approved the establishment of a national dashboard to track ongoing projects across the federation, with particular emphasis on transparency, accountability and accurate reporting of how proceeds from fuel subsidy removal are being utilised.

Presenting the economic outlook, Mr Oyedele expressed optimism about the progress recorded under the Tinubu administration’s reform programme and the prospects for further economic recovery.

He identified the reduction of headline inflation and interest rates to single digits by 2027 as key policy objectives, noting that the next phase of reforms would require coordinated implementation across federal and state institutions.

The finance minister’s presentation placed particular emphasis on translating macroeconomic improvements into measurable benefits for households and businesses through targeted interventions, improved fiscal coordination and the removal of barriers to investment.

Addressing members of council, Vice President Shettima charged state governors and relevant government institutions to ensure that the gains of the administration’s economic reforms translate into affordable transportation, improved healthcare, employment opportunities and greater financial security for Nigerians.

He said the success of economic policies must ultimately be measured by their impact on citizens’ daily lives, stressing that the responsibility of government extends beyond announcing reforms to building institutions that enable Nigerians to plan their futures with confidence.

“The first dividend of prosperity should be the confidence to plan a life. Our task is to make such confidence less dependent on fortune,” he said.

According to him, the council’s deliberations on transportation, healthcare, police reform, and livestock development represent critical decisions about the quality of life Nigerians should expect from economic progress.

“Our separate jurisdictions must serve a common public interest,” Mr Shettima said, emphasising that Nigeria’s federal structure must strengthen cooperation rather than become an obstacle to the delivery of essential services.

On the National Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) Bus Initiative, the vice president underscored the need for state governments to support affordable transportation systems that would reduce the financial burden on commuters.

He maintained that the success of the programme should be determined by affordability and accessibility rather than the number of vehicles deployed.

“The cost of reaching a livelihood should never consume the livelihood itself. The passenger’s experience must guide our ambition, because the value of public transport resides in the journeys it makes possible. We should assess success through affordability and access, rather than fleet size alone,” he said.

Mr Shettima maintained that President Tinubu’s economic reform programme was designed to achieve broader national prosperity, noting that governments at all levels have a responsibility to translate its objectives into improved living conditions.

“His Excellency, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR, has made economic reform the instrument of a larger national ambition. Our contribution must give that ambition social depth and productive strength,” he stated.

He urged governors to bring their understanding of local realities into national policy decisions, insisting that effective implementation requires clear responsibilities and practical agreements among the tiers of government.

“Our separate mandates must not become competing excuses. Each Governor carries knowledge that no federal document can supply,” he said.

The vice president challenged members of the Council to judge every policy proposal by its capacity to reduce uncertainty, create opportunities and strengthen public confidence in government.

“Nigerians deserve institutions on which they can organise their lives. Providing that assurance is among the most consequential uses of public authority. That is the assurance we owe them,” the vice president said.

NEC Reviews Ebola Response, Tasks States On Preparedness

Meanwhile, the council received an update on the reported Ebola outbreak in the Federal Capital Territory from the Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Pate, who allayed fears of a major public health crisis, assuring members that Nigeria possesses the institutional capacity to contain the situation.

The minister briefed the council on efforts by the ministry, in collaboration with relevant stakeholders, to operationalise a robust national response system.

He identified coordination and governance, detection at points of entry, laboratory testing capacity, logistics for essential kits and personal protective equipment, and effective strategic communication as critical components of the response.

The minister acknowledged the efforts of 21 state governments that had updated their response plans and urged the remaining 15 states to expedite the establishment of appropriate preparedness and response mechanisms.

NEC directs states to strengthen polio eradication efforts

The council also received the report of the NEC Ad Hoc Committee on Polio Eradication, chaired by the Governor of Gombe State, Muhammadu Yahaya, and resolved to direct states to conduct post-campaign reviews, particularly in areas where children were missed during immunisation exercises and communities affected by insecurity.

The council emphasised the need for timely release of counterpart funds, strengthened routine immunisation, improved coordination with security agencies and closer cooperation among states to ensure better coverage in subsequent campaigns.

It further stressed that sustained political commitment from governors, traditional rulers and security agencies would remain critical to achieving the complete eradication of polio in Nigeria.

NEC moves to unlock livestock sector’s economic potential

On livestock development, the council received the report of the NEC Ad Hoc Committee on Livestock Development, chaired by the Governor of Kebbi State, Nasir Idris, and acknowledged the sector’s potential to stimulate economic growth, create employment and improve livelihoods across the country.

The council noted that all states had indicated interest in supporting the federal government’s livestock development initiatives and resolved to strengthen collaboration between the federal and state governments to accelerate reforms and unlock the sector’s economic potential.

FG, States to establish joint financing framework for CNG, electric vehicles

In another major resolution, the council received a presentation on the National Affordable Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) Transit Programme by the Chairman of the Presidential Initiative on Compressed Natural Gas and Electric Vehicles, Ismaeel Ahmed, and resolved to establish a joint financing framework between the federal and state governments to accelerate the deployment of CNG and electric vehicles across the country.

The council specifically directed that the programme must deliver tangible benefits to citizens through reduced transportation costs, rather than limiting its impact to the provision of alternative-energy vehicles.

It further resolved that relevant authorities should engage transport unions and operators to ensure that savings arising from the adoption of CNG and electric vehicles are passed on to commuters through lower fares.

To give effect to the decision, the council agreed to constitute a committee to coordinate the proposed financing arrangement, engage relevant stakeholders and develop practical measures to ensure that the economic benefits of the programme translate into affordable, accessible and sustainable transportation for Nigerians.

Stanley Nkwocha

Senior Special Assistant To The President on Media & Communications

(Office of The Vice President)

22nd October, 2026

World.title: Ebola: Nigerian govt says no restrictions on large gatherings for now
World.content:
The Nigerian government has said there is currently no need to restrict large gatherings following the confirmation of an imported Ebola case in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja.

The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Pate, said this on Thursday during a ministerial press briefing in Abuja, adding that any decision to introduce restrictions would be based on public health evidence and expert advice.

“At this moment there is no indication that requires us to alter the course of large gatherings that have been planned,” Mr Pate said.

“But if the situation changes, we would decide; we would consult broadly with the right experts and make that determination.”

He urged Nigerians to remain calm, saying the government’s response would be guided by evidence rather than political considerations.

“So Nigerians should be assured that whatever the public health community will come out with will be based on good evidence. At this moment we have not indicated that,” he said.

Patient recovering

Mr Pate also said the woman at the centre of Nigeria’s first confirmed case is recovering and that laboratory results were showing improvement.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He said he had spoken with the clinicians treating her and there is a possibility that she would recover from the disease.

“We cannot hold our breath. We have to continue to pray and work hard to ensure that she survives it,” he said.

The minister reiterated that the case was imported based on the patient’s travel history and that she was asymptomatic when she arrived in Nigeria.

According to him, she developed symptoms several days after arrival, after which she sought medical attention.

The government has traced people who had contact with her in the hospital, at home and at a private clinic she visited. The contacts have been categorised by risk level.

Mr Pate said high-risk contacts had been quarantined in a facility, while others had been isolated and were being monitored in line with public health guidelines.

Response expanded

The minister said the government had activated its incident management system, with the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) leading the operational response in coordination with the FCT authorities.

He said all state governments had been informed and that most states already had response plans developed with guidance from the NCDC.

He said states that have yet to complete their plans have been directed to do so quickly.

The government has also mobilised additional resources for the response, including funding from the Basic Health Care Provision Fund (BHCF) and additional resources released to the NCDC by President Bola Tinubu.

Mr Pate said the government was also working with development and technical partners, including the World Health Organisation (WHO) and Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC).

He said experts who had supported Ebola responses in other countries, including Kenya, have also arrived in Nigeria to strengthen the response.

Mr Pate said Christian Happi, a virologist and director of the African Centre of Excellence for Genomics of Infectious Diseases at Redeemer’s University, has been brought into the response to complement the work of the NCDC.

“This is to let Nigerians know that the capabilities are in the country, and the investments that have been made to get us here are bearing fruit,” he said.

‘Do not politicise Ebola’

The minister also criticised attempts to politicise the Ebola response, urging political leaders and the media to treat the situation as a public health issue.

“We certainly would encourage them not to politicise a humanitarian and public health issue,” he said.

Mr Pate said any decisions on restrictions or other measures would be based solely on scientific evidence and what was considered in the best interests of Nigerians.

He also warned against misinformation about the confirmed case, saying the patient had tested positive for Ebola three times.

He said the government could not release the patient’s test results publicly because of medical confidentiality.

The minister urged Nigerians to rely on information from trusted public health authorities and warned that misinformation could undermine efforts to contain the disease.

“The alternative to trusting the expert is a tragedy,” he said.

Border surveillance strengthened

Mr Pate said Nigeria had maintained enhanced surveillance at points of entry for the past five months following the worsening Ebola situation in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).

He said more than 14,000 travellers had entered Nigeria during the period and that the government was strengthening port health capacity, including thermal imaging and risk-based assessment of travellers from affected countries.

He said the government would continue to monitor the situation and adjust its recommendations if the evidence changes.

For now, he urged Nigerians to observe basic preventive measures, including regular hand washing, avoiding unnecessary contact with bodily fluids, and promptly reporting symptoms such as fever, headache, and muscle aches, particularly if they have relevant travel history.

He also urged people identified through contact tracing to comply with isolation and quarantine measures.

“We are assuring Nigerians that we can be able to deal with it, but to do that we need the cooperation of Nigerians to follow expert advice,” Mr Pate said.

World.title: Anambra seeks ₦70 billion from Nigeria’s stabilisation fund
World.content:
The Revenue Mobilisation, Allocation and Fiscal Commission (RMAFC) has reviewed Anambra State’s request for ₦70 billion from the stabilisation fund to address security, erosion and infrastructure challenges.

‌‌‍‌‍⁠⁠‍Olusegun Wright, chairman, Indices and Disbursement Committee, disclosed this in a statement issued by Maryam Yusuf, the commission’s Head of Information and Public Relations Unit, on Wednesday in Abuja.

Mr Wright, who also represents Lagos State on the commission, acknowledged the state government’s presentation of its financial challenges for consideration.

He said the stabilisation fund provides fiscal assistance in deserving circumstances, subject to established guidelines, available resources and appropriate approval procedures.

Mr Wright explained that requesting states must formally present their proposals before the commission conducts on-the-spot assessments of targeted projects.

He said the committee would examine financial records, project viability, estimated costs, implementation requirements and expected socioeconomic benefits before making recommendations.

He stressed that the technical review did not constitute automatic approval, adding that the request required further scrutiny and verification.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Why we need the money – Anambra govt

Presenting Anambra’s case, the Secretary to the State Government, Chiamaka Nnake, said the state had 21 local government areas, 179 communities and an estimated population of 8.9 million.

Ms Nnake put the state’s gross domestic product at approximately $12.7 billion and its projected 2026 budget at ₦766 billion.

She said Anambra had increased its internally generated revenue from about ₦2.2 billion to ₦7.2 billion, driven by commercial centres, industries and petroleum-producing areas.

However, she identified insecurity, erosion, flooding, inflation and rising public service costs as major fiscal challenges.

She added that sit-at-home orders had disrupted businesses and weakened investor confidence, further increasing pressure on the state’s economy.

On security, Ms Nnake said the government had enacted a Homeland Security Law, established a security outfit and strengthened collaboration through a joint task force.

She said the proposed funding would support operational vehicles, surveillance and communication equipment, personnel training and improved coordination to protect lives and stimulate economic activities.

Ms Nnake said Anambra had more than 1,000 erosion sites affecting 146 communities, with approximately ₦170 billion required to address identified critical locations.

She said ongoing interventions included erosion control, flood management, road rehabilitation, land reclamation, waterway clearance and tree planting.

The state had also restricted sand mining near vulnerable areas to mitigate environmental damage, she added.

On healthcare, Ms Nnake said the state’s free antenatal care and delivery programme had supported more than 206,000 deliveries, including 642 caesarean sections.

She added that the government had recruited 8,415 teachers and introduced free education from nursery to senior secondary school, increasing demand for personnel, facilities and learning materials.

Ms Nnake identified agriculture, solid minerals and tourism as investment opportunities requiring additional funding and supporting infrastructure.

She said the state had distributed more than 2.3 million coconut and oil-palm seedlings but needed improved processing, storage and market access.

She also highlighted mineral deposits, petroleum-related opportunities and tourist attractions, including Agulu Lake, calling for geological surveys, better access roads and improved visitor facilities.

Ms Nnake reiterated that the ₦70 billion request would support security, environmental management, infrastructure, healthcare, education, agriculture, solid minerals and tourism.

She said the proposed intervention would protect livelihoods, address critical development challenges and diversify the state’s economy.

The Commissioner representing Anambra on RMAFC, Enefe Ekene, thanked the committee leadership and members for their observations.

Mr Ekene said the feedback would help strengthen the state’s presentation ahead of the proposed assessment visit.

He acknowledged that any recommendation would depend on verified financial documentation, project feasibility, estimated costs, implementation requirements and expected benefits, in line with established procedures.

(NAN)

World.title: 2027: Group targets 10,000 supporters for Tinubu’s campaign flag-off in Kaduna
World.content:
Arewa for Asiwaju (A4A), a political support group backing President Bola Tinubu, says it is targeting 10,000 supporters from the 19 northern states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) for the flag-off of the president’s 2027 re-election campaign in Kaduna State.

The group said the mobilisation was aimed at demonstrating its organisational capacity and strengthening grassroots support for Mr Tinubu’s re-election bid.

In a statement issued on Thursday, Edwin Olofu, the group’s head of media relations, quoted its Director-General, Badaru Abubakar, as saying the mobilisation would be coordinated through the movement’s national leadership, state coordinators and grassroots structures.

He said the group was engaging supporters at the state, local government and community levels to ensure the targeted turnout.

Mr Abubakar, a former governor of Jigawa State, described the campaign flag-off as an opportunity for supporters of the president, party stakeholders and allied political groups to demonstrate their commitment to his second-term ambition.

He also said the event would allow A4A members to reaffirm their support for Mr Tinubu’s political agenda and strengthen cooperation among supporters across Northern Nigeria.

The director-general urged state coordinators and local mobilisation teams to intensify preparations, expand grassroots engagement and maintain effective communication ahead of the event.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He called on members to keep activities peaceful and orderly, emphasising the importance of discipline and coordination to achieve the mobilisation target.

The statement did not specify which states the 10,000 supporters would come from or how they would be transported to Kaduna.

The president is expected to arrive in Kaduna on Saturday with seven governors from the North West states, national party leaders, and their supporters.

PREMIUM TIMES observed security personnel deployed across the state metropolis ahead of the event, to be held at the State Township Stadium.

World.title: Judge gives Trump Dec. 11 deadline to testify in BBC lawsuit
World.content:
WASHINGTON, DC – OCTOBER 22: U.S. President Donald Trump speaks to the media o the South Lawn before departing the White House on October 22, 2026 in Washington, DC. President Trump is traveling to Iowa to stump for midterm candidates with 12 days until Election Day. Aaron Schwartz/Getty Images/AFP (Photo by Aaron Schwartz / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP)

A US judge on Thursday issued President Donald Trump a December 11 deadline to testify under oath in his $10 billion defamation lawsuit against the BBC.

Judge Enjolique Lett in Miami gave the order in response to complaints by the British broadcaster that Trump has refused to sit for a deposition, including canceling a previously agreed date of October 16.

If Trump fails to attend the deposition by then, he risks sanctions, including dismissal of his lawsuit, the court said.

Trump has accused the BBC of deceptively editing its documentary “Trump: A Second Chance” to make it seem as if he was inciting violence when he told supporters to march on the US Capitol on January 6, 2021, after losing the presidential election.

The crowd proceeded to storm Congress in an attempt to stop the formal certification of Democrat Joe Biden’s victory.

While the BBC has apologized for the incident, which prompted the resignation of multiple senior executives, the broadcaster has denied it caused Trump any real injury and moved for the case to be dismissed.

Trump filed his suit against the BBC in December 2025 and is seeking at least $5 billion on each of two counts.

Charles Tobin, a lawyer for the BBC, said in court that Trump had no real excuse not to testify and that on October 16, he had only been campaigning, “participating in party politics.”

“No plaintiff is above the law,” Tobin said.

In a court filing Wednesday, Trump’s legal team argued that he was not seeking to avoid a deposition but had been constrained by “matters of national importance.”

The lawyers said Trump would be able to give a deposition between January 11 and 22.

Trump has made attacks on the media a signature of his two presidential terms, insulting reporters who ask questions he doesn’t like and seeking to ban outlets airing critical reports from the White House.

Most recently, the administration has plunged into a legal dispute with CNN, MSNOW and Politico over attempts to bar them from the White House.

With his approval ratings in the low 30 percent range and polls showing his Republican Party likely to lose control of the House of Representatives in the November 3 midterm elections, Trump faces increasing headwinds as he approaches his final years in power.

AFP

World.title: N10bn untouched – APC accuses Atiku of politicising Ebola response
World.content:
Atiku Abubakar

The All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council has accused former Vice-President, Atiku Abubakar, of politicising Nigeria’s Ebola response, insisting that approved emergency funds remain untouched.

The council’s spokesperson, Mr Dele Alake, said this in a statement issued on Thursday in Abuja.

Alake said President Bola Tinubu approved N10 billion for the Ebola emergency in June, but relevant agencies deployed other available resources.

“On accountability, the Atiku camp should note that the N10 billion the President approved for the Ebola emergency in June remains untouched,” he said.

He said the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN) and other agencies strengthened surveillance at entry points.

According to him, the surveillance network alerted the government to the index case and facilitated contact tracing for 44 contacts.

The council commended the agencies for their contributions to monitoring the Ebola threat and supporting the public health response.

It also criticised Atiku’s reference linking President Tinubu’s name to Ebola, saying it risked turning a serious health concern into political ridicule.

“We believe linking and rhyming President Bola Tinubu’s name to Ebola only risks turning a serious health concern into a vehicle to ridicule the President,” Alake said.

The council also defended the handling of the infected Nigerian’s detection, citing the virus’s incubation period and the timing of symptoms.

“For anyone infected with the virus, the incubation period ranges from two to 21 days, with symptoms typically appearing eight to 10 days after exposure.

“An infected person cannot spread or transmit Ebola to others until they actively develop symptoms,” he said.

Alake urged opposition politicians to support health authorities rather than criticise the government’s response to the public health threat.

“A responsible opposition will applaud the Task Force for being responsive. But the Atiku camp always goes for cheap shots at the government,” he said.

The council also rejected Atiku’s allegation that a ministerial briefing was intended to discourage Nigerians from attending campaign rallies or voting.

Alake described the allegation as speculative, adding that the briefing instead urged Nigerians to comply with protocols announced by the task force.

He called on Atiku and his supporters to avoid politicising public health concerns, urging Nigerians to shun rumours and follow health authorities’ guidance.

“We advise Atiku Abubakar and his hirelings to avoid politicising public health issues,” he said.

The council said protecting Nigerians from the deadly disease should remain the priority. (NAN)

World.title: Tinubu names former DSS DG Bichi NISS board chairman
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu has appointed former Director-General of the Department of State Services, Yusuf Bichi, as Chairman of the Governing Board of the National Institute for Security Studies.

The appointment was announced in a statement issued on Thursday by the institute’s Director of Coordination and Liaison, Lilian Omo-Odigwe, and published through the DSS’s X account.

According to the statement, Bichi’s appointment followed a recommendation by the incumbent DSS Director-General, Oluwatosin Ajayi.

“The Commander-In-Chief of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, President Bola Tinubu, GCFR, has approved the appointment of Y. M. Bichi, CFR, FWC, the immediate past Director-General of the Department of State Services (DSS), as Chairman of the Governing Board of the National Institute for Security Studies (NISS), Lower Usuma Dam, Abuja.”

The statement added, “Bichi’s appointment was approved by President Tinubu based on the recommendation of the current DG-DSS, Oluwatosin Adeola Ajayi.”

Bichi’s appointment took effect on Thursday, October 22, 2026, and will run for an initial four-year term.

“His appointment is for an initial four-year term, effective 22nd October, 2026, in accordance with Section 4 of the National Institute for Security Studies (Establishment) Act, 2019,” the statement said.

He succeeds A.A. Gadzama as chairman of the institute’s governing board. Bichi previously led the DSS before handing over to Ajayi in August 2024.

“Bichi, who will succeed A.A. Gadzama, OFR, mni, on the Governing Board, handed over leadership of the DSS to the incumbent Director-General in August 2024,” the statement added.

Bichi began his career in the Security Division of the Kano State Cabinet Office before his transfer of service in 1984.

The institute said his appointment would bring “extensive experience in intelligence, security administration, operational leadership and institutional training to the governance of the National Institute”.

World.title: We sought Aso Rock venue because APC uses it too – Sowore
World.content:
Omoyele Sowore

Presidential candidate of the African Action Congress, Omoyele Sowore, has defended his party’s request to hold the inauguration of its 2027 Presidential Campaign Council at the Presidential Villa in Abuja, arguing that opposition parties should enjoy the same access as the ruling All Progressives Congress.

Sowore made the remarks on Thursday at an event organised by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nigeria, explaining that the request was prompted by the APC’s use of the facility for political activities.

The AAC had written to President Bola Tinubu seeking approval to inaugurate its Presidential Campaign Council at the Villa ahead of the 2027 general elections.

“We asked to use Aso Rock because the APC uses Aso Rock to do political party events. So we are saying, as a matter of right, since Aso Rock is our own, other political parties must be granted the opportunity to use Aso Rock the way APC uses Aso Rock,” Sowore said.

In addition to the venue, the party requested food, drinks and other logistical arrangements for attendees at the proposed inauguration scheduled for November 11, 2026.

A letter dated October 21 and signed by the AAC National Secretary, Oshiokhai Ikpeminioghena, stated that the request was anchored on multiparty democracy, political inclusiveness and equal treatment of political parties.

The party maintained that approving the request would affirm the Presidency’s commitment to fairness and demonstrate that public institutions were available to all Nigerians, irrespective of political affiliation.

The request triggered a disagreement between Sowore and the APC National Secretary, Ajibola Basiru, who criticised the AAC candidate and questioned the party’s electoral strength.

Sowore insisted that the move was aimed at securing equal access to the Presidential Villa. He also ruled out joining a proposed opposition coalition ahead of the 2027 elections.

“I don’t want to be part of your coalition because your rainbow coalition is going to die after 2027,” he said.

The AAC candidate also lamented the economic and social difficulties facing Nigerians, saying, “They have brought sorrow, and honestly, things are hard for the people of this country.”

World.title: Trump slams LeBron James for national anthem actions
World.content:
US President Donald Trump lashed out at NBA superstar LeBron James on Thursday for what he called disrespectful behaviour during the playing of the national anthem.

Trump posted a video of the basketball legend doing apparent warm-up movements while lined up with his Philadelphia 76ers teammates.

“While listening to our National Anthem, LeBron James disrespects our Country! I said right from the beginning that he’s no good, a TOTAL DISGRACE,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social network.

“LeBron James should apologize to all of those Great American Warriors and Heroes who died for the American Flag, and all that our Country stands for!” he wrote.

The video used by Trump had an internal caption that read: “LeBron working on his golf swing pregame.” It showed him doing lateral swing motions and basketball shooting movements.

It was not immediately clear when the video was filmed.

There was no immediate reaction from James, 41, who is entering a record-extending 24th NBA season with his fourth team, the 76ers.

Trump has been critical of athletes before — particularly Black athletes — for their behaviour during the playing of the US national anthem before games.

During his first term, Trump singled out NFL star Colin Kaepernick for his decision to kneel during the “Star-Spangled Banner” to protest racial injustice and police brutality.

AFP

World.title: FG to bar defaulting contractors from public procurement for five years
World.content:
Akume

The Federal Government has directed the strict implementation of the National Guideline on Debarment of Contractors, Consultants and Service Providers.

The directive is contained in a circular issued by the Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Sen. George Akume, with reference number 59780/S.2/B/585.

This is according to a statement by Ngozi Anyaelezu, Acting Head of Public Relations, Bureau of Public Procurement (BPP), in Abuja on Thursday.

Anyaelezu said that the guidelines provide for the exclusion of defaulting contractors from public procurement for up to five years.

She said the circular mandated all Accounting Officers in Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs) to ensure full compliance with the guidelines.

“It aims to prevent fraud and corruption in contract execution by ensuring that contractors who violate the provisions of the Public Procurement Act, 2007, are promptly reported and excluded from further participation in government procurement.”

The guidelines said that the BPP may initiate debarment proceedings following findings from its reviews, surveillance or audits, or based on a properly supported recommendation from a procuring entity approved by its Accounting Officer.

It provides that an affected contractor must be notified of the allegations and given 10 working days to respond, with provision for a limited extension in appropriate circumstances.

“Where the Debarment Committee establishes a case against a contractor, it may impose a debarment period of between three years and five years.

“A debarred contractor will be prohibited from being invited to bid for or awarded Federal Government contracts.

“The contractor will also be barred from conducting government business as an agent or representative of another contractor, consultant or service provider.”

The guideline further provides that the name of every debarred entity will be entered into the BPP database and published on the Bureau’s website, the Federal Tenders Journal and other relevant platforms.

It, however, allows for the reinstatement of debarred contractors after the expiration of the sanction, subject to an application supported by evidence of reform.

“The Federal Government reiterated its commitment to transparency, accountability and fiscal discipline in public expenditure.

“All Accounting Officers are to ensure that the guidelines are brought to the attention of Tenders Boards, Procurement Planning Committees, procurement departments and all officers involved in public procurement.”

Meanwhile, following the circular, Dr Adebowale Adedokun, Director-General of the BPP, said the guideline was designed to eliminate corrupt, fraudulent and non-performing contractors from the public procurement system.

Adedokun said the measure would safeguard public funds and promote value for money in government expenditure.

He said that the government would no longer tolerate compromises that undermined the integrity of public procurement processes.

The director-general said that any Accounting Officer or procuring entity that bypassed the debarment registry or violated the provisions of the Public Procurement Act would face administrative and legal sanctions.

“Moving forward, all procuring entities are mandated to verify compliance,” he said.

He said the guidelines identify several grounds for debarment, including offering money, gifts or other benefits to influence procurement decisions, and providing employment or financial benefits to procurement officials for improper purposes.

“Other grounds include conviction for fraud relating to public contracts, falsification of documents, and wilful or persistent failure to fulfil contractual obligations.

“It also allows the Federal Government to consider for debarment contractors already sanctioned by multilateral organisations,” he said.

(NAN)

World.title: Obasanjo’s son joins Tinubu Must Stay Movement
World.content:
Olujonwo Obasanjo, son of former President Olusegun Obasanjo, has joined the Tinubu Must Stay Movement, pledging to promote policy continuity and explain President Bola Tinubu’s reforms.

He announced his decision at a news conference in Abuja on Thursday, where the leadership of the Tinubu Movement for Sustainable Governance Foundation (TMS) welcomed him.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that TMS is a political advocacy platform promoting policy continuity, sustainable governance and public understanding of Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda.

Olujonwo said his decision was shaped by his political experience, understanding of Nigeria’s reform history and belief in sustaining government policies across administrations.

“I’ve been in the APC since 2014. I was there when my father hosted late President Muhammadu Buhari and President Bola Tinubu to form the movement. I’m not new to the party,” he said.

He said inadequate communication about the Tinubu administration’s policies had created opportunities for misinformation and misinterpretation among Nigerians.

“There’s a lot of noise out there, and people are distorting what’s going on. ASUU has had no strikes. Students now have access to education loans.

“Nigeria has become a massive construction site and an investors’ haven again. These are things we need to promote,” he said.

Olujonwo said communicating government policies required explaining their objectives, implementation processes and implications for citizens rather than relying solely on political slogans.

The National Coordinator of TMS and Director-General of the National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA), Kashifu Abdullahi, welcomed him into the movement.

Abdullahi said Olujonwo’s family background gave him an understanding of economic reforms and their implications for national development.

“You grew up in a family that led the second wave of reforms in Nigeria. Telecommunications liberalisation and banking reforms — these laid a solid foundation.

“Being raised in that family, you understand what reforms mean,” he added.

Abdullahi said policy consistency was essential for national development, warning that frequent reversals could undermine investor confidence and disrupt long-term planning.

“We are building investors’ confidence; the naira is becoming strong, our stock exchange is one of the fastest-growing.

“The Dangote Refinery is a game changer. If we start reversing these policies, we’ll go back to where we were,” Abdullahi said.

He said TMS would expand its nationwide structures and engage stakeholders across professional, political and social groups.

Abdullahi said the movement supported policy continuity beyond 2027, while seeking to strengthen institutional development and the sustainability of government programmes.

The Director-General of TMS, Marcel Ngogbehei, described Olujonwo’s entry as significant, citing his family’s association with economic reforms and democratic consolidation.

Ngogbehei, a former coordinator of the Obidient movement, recalled former President Obasanjo’s telecommunications liberalisation policies and Nigeria’s external debt relief.

He said those reforms helped lay the foundations for subsequent economic development.

“We are happy you have decided to take this step. Your father was one of those who revolutionised this country.

“The debt was paid off, and major innovations were introduced in liberalising the economy,” he said.

Ngogbehei said TMS was established to encourage informed public engagement on government policies, address misconceptions about ongoing reforms and promote assessments based on evidence and measurable outcomes. (NAN)

World.title: UEL: Juventus denied at the death, Sunderland make point in Poland
World.content:
Bayer Leverkusen made it three straight wins in the Europa League with a Jonas Hofmann double earning a 2-0 away win at OFI Crete as both Juventus and Sunderland lost ground in Thursday’s third matchday.

The once mighty Hungarian side Ferencvaros kept pace with Leverkusen on nine points thumping Portuguese outfit Torreense 4-1, while Belgium’s Union Saint-Gilloise won 4-0 against Israeli outfit Hapoel Be’er Sheva.

Saint-Gilloise, Sunderland and Juve all have seven points from three games.

Juventus thought they had come from behind to beat French side Rennes but had their late ‘winner’ ruled out for a marginal offside.

Zeki Celik put Juve ahead after five minutes only for a poor clearance 10 minutes later allowing Musa Al-Taamari to poke home an equaliser. Jut before the break Boulaye Dia put the visitors ahead.

Juventus made it 2-2 thanks to a handball and a spot-kick transformed by Nick Woltemade before VAR provided the biggest talking point, disallowing Jhon Lucumi’s 88th minute strike.

Clad in a new all-pink kit, Sunderland were left kicking themselves after a 1-1 draw in Poland.

The Blacks Cats took a second-half lead in Poznan thanks to Timur Tutierov and dominated the game without being able to close out the win.

With two home games remaining, however, the second round still beckons for Regis Le Bris’ men.

In the Conference League, former Liverpool striker Mohamed Salah opened the scoring from the penalty spot in Trabzonspor’s 2-0 win over Scottish side Hearts.

AFP

World.title: THE NORTH AND THE 2027 ELECTIONS
World.content:
Vote for results, not empty promises, urges

ABBA DUKAWA

Democracy delivers little when citizens are unsafe, hungry and unable to find work. As Northern Nigeria approaches the 2027 general elections, voters face a choice that goes beyond party loyalty, regional identity or campaign rhetoric: whether to continue rewarding promises or demand measurable performance.

The central question is whether political leaders can demonstrate that they have improved people’s lives and present credible, practical plans for addressing the region’s persistent challenges. Security, the cost of living, employment, education and economic opportunity must become the principal tests of leadership, supported by clear targets, realistic timelines and public accountability.

From insurgency and displacement in the North-East to banditry in the North-West and poverty and unemployment across the North-Central, millions of people face challenges that cannot be resolved through campaign speeches. Families struggle with rising food and transportation costs, farmers face threats to their livelihoods, young people confront limited opportunities, and communities continue to question the government’s ability to protect them.

Across parts of Northern Nigeria, bandits, kidnappers and insurgents continue to threaten communities, killing and abducting civilians, disrupting economic activities and forcing families to abandon their homes. These conditions raise serious questions about the effectiveness of security measures and the accountability of those entrusted with public office.

The 2027 elections should therefore be treated as a performance review. Voters must ask which leaders have improved security, eased economic hardship, expanded opportunities and strengthened public services—and which candidates can explain, in practical and financially credible terms, how they intend to do better.

Fuel Subsidy: A Debate About Survival. Since the removal of Nigeria’s petrol subsidy in May 2023, households and businesses have faced higher transportation and operating costs. Although the government has defended the reform as necessary to ease fiscal pressure and redirect public resources towards development, many Nigerians continue to ask when its promised benefits will become evident in their daily lives.

In Northern Nigeria, where long distances separate farms, markets, schools and healthcare facilities, higher fuel prices have consequences far beyond the filling station. Transportation becomes more expensive, food distribution costs rise, farmers face higher production expenses, and small businesses struggle to remain profitable.

Low-income households, particularly those dependent on informal employment, small-scale trading and subsistence agriculture, are especially vulnerable. The combined costs of food, transportation, healthcare and education leave many families with little money for other essential needs.

Fuel subsidy removal is therefore likely to remain a major electoral issue in 2027. Opposition politicians may promise cheaper petrol, the restoration of subsidies or alternative forms of economic relief, while the ruling party may defend the policy as a difficult but necessary reform.

Voters must look beyond these competing arguments and examine the practical consequences of each proposal. The economic debate should focus not only on whether subsidy, removal has improved government finances but also on whether the resulting savings and additional public resources have translated into meaningful relief for households and businesses.

The government should explain how the fiscal benefits of its reforms are being converted into better infrastructure, agricultural support, affordable transportation, quality education, accessible healthcare and effective social protection. It should also provide transparent information about public spending and the measurable benefits delivered to vulnerable households.

Opposition parties, meanwhile, must demonstrate that their alternatives are economically credible and financially sustainable. Promising to restore subsidies or reduce petrol prices without explaining how the policies would be funded, implemented and sustained offers voters little basis for making an informed decision.

Ultimately, economic reform should be judged by whether it improves living standards, expands productive opportunities and strengthens household financial security—not merely by increases in government revenue or improvements in economic indicators.

Insecurity: The North’s Most Urgent Challenge. If rising fuel prices threaten household welfare, insecurity threatens lives and livelihoods. Across parts of Northern Nigeria, banditry, kidnapping, insurgency and communal violence have displaced families, disrupted agriculture and trade, and weakened public confidence in the government’s ability to protect its citizens.

Farmers abandon their land or risk their lives to cultivate it. Traders face dangerous roads, businesses struggle to operate, and parents worry about the safety of their children. Families lose breadwinners, children miss school, and displaced people struggle to rebuild their lives.

Insecurity also worsens economic hardship. Agricultural production suffers when farmers cannot safely access their fields, food becomes more expensive when transportation routes are unsafe, and investment declines when businesses face persistent threats of violence. The resulting poverty and lack of opportunity can further expose vulnerable communities to criminal exploitation and recruitment.

The security debate ahead of 2027 must move beyond declarations of commitment and announcements of military operations. Voters need evidence that interventions are producing lasting improvements in community safety.

Political leaders should be assessed on whether attacks and kidnappings are declining, abducted victims are being rescued, displaced families can return home voluntarily and safely, and farmers can cultivate their land without fear. The public also deserves credible information about investigations and prosecutions involving serious crimes.

Candidates should explain how they intend to improve intelligence gathering, strengthen coordination among security agencies, protect vulnerable communities and transportation routes, and provide security personnel with the equipment, training and logistical support necessary to perform their duties.

Community engagement must also form part of the strategy. Traditional rulers, local authorities, community organisations and residents can help identify emerging threats, provided their involvement operates within the law and includes safeguards against abuses and reprisals.

Security performance should not be measured solely by arrests, weapons recovered or operations announced. The ultimate test is whether people are safer and can resume their normal activities without fear.

Candidates must therefore present clear security priorities, realistic implementation timelines and measurable indicators of progress. They should also explain how they intend to address underlying vulnerabilities, including poverty, youth unemployment, educational exclusion and weak local institutions.

For Northern voters, the question is not simply which candidate promises to defeat insecurity, but which has a credible, lawful and accountable plan to protect lives, restore livelihoods and prevent violence from recurring.

The Economy: Beyond Government Statistics: Economic performance will be another decisive factor in the 2027 elections. Government officials may point to economic growth, increased investment or reforms designed to strengthen public finances. While these developments matter, national economic growth does not automatically translate into improved living conditions for every household.

For many Northern Nigerians, economic performance is measured by whether families can afford food, graduates can find jobs, traders can restock their shops and farmers can earn reasonable profits after paying for fertiliser, transportation and labour.

Northern Nigeria continues to face widespread poverty, inadequate infrastructure, educational disadvantages and limited employment opportunities. Addressing these challenges requires sustained investment in agriculture, manufacturing, healthcare, education, transportation and small businesses.

Agriculture remains particularly important to the region’s economy. However, farmers cannot maximise productivity when insecurity prevents access to their land, agricultural inputs are unaffordable, irrigation infrastructure is inadequate and transportation costs consume a substantial share of their earnings.

Candidates should explain how they intend to improve agricultural productivity, expand access to affordable financing, strengthen rural infrastructure and create conditions in which small and medium-sized businesses can grow and employ more people.

They must also demonstrate how vocational training will translate into actual jobs and how public spending will benefit communities beyond state capitals.

Government projects should be evaluated by their functionality, accessibility and impact rather than the funds allocated to them or the ceremonies held to inaugurate them. Roads, schools, healthcare facilities, irrigation systems and rural electrification programmes must deliver tangible benefits to the communities they are intended to serve. The 2027 elections should provide an opportunity for serious debate about practical economic solutions rather than competing interpretations of government statistics.

Education, Youth Unemployment and the Future; Northern Nigeria’s large young population offers enormous potential, but that potential may be lost when young people lack access to quality education, employable skills and realistic economic opportunities.

Children who are out of school face severely limited prospects, while unemployed graduates may become increasingly frustrated by their inability to secure meaningful work. Educational exclusion also weakens the region’s long-term economic prospects by limiting the skills and knowledge available to its workforce.

Addressing these challenges requires qualified teachers, functional classrooms, well-equipped vocational institutions, digital skills training, apprenticeships and accessible higher education. It also requires an economic environment in which businesses can invest, expand and create jobs.

Education and employment cannot be addressed in isolation from poverty and insecurity. Children cannot learn effectively when their families are hungry, their communities are unsafe or their schools are inaccessible. Similarly, young people cannot contribute meaningfully to economic development when they lack the skills and opportunities required to participate in the workforce.

Candidates seeking public office should explain how their policies will improve school enrolment, attendance and learning outcomes, expand vocational training and create pathways to productive employment. They should also identify realistic targets against which their performance can be assessed.

Northern Nigeria cannot afford a future in which millions of young people remain excluded from education and economic opportunity while political leaders continue making promises about development.

The region’s young population should be treated as an asset to be developed through investment, effective policies and meaningful employment opportunities—not merely as a demographic challenge to be discussed during election campaigns.

Will 2027 Be Another Election of Empty Promises? The greatest danger is that political parties will discuss these problems extensively during their campaigns but do too little to address them after winning office. Nigerians have heard promises of affordable fuel, secure communities, millions of jobs, agricultural transformation and improved education. Yet many communities continue to experience serious hardship.

Campaign speeches, political rallies and defections are not evidence of good governance. Voters must examine candidates’ records, scrutinise their proposals, demand realistic implementation timelines and insist on transparent reporting of results.

They must also reject attempts to exploit religious, ethnic or regional loyalties to avoid public scrutiny and accountability.

Northern Nigeria is not a uniform electoral bloc. The security challenges facing Borno differ from the agricultural concerns of Kebbi, just as the employment challenges confronting young people in Kaduna and Kano may differ from those experienced elsewhere.

The priorities of rural farming communities may also differ from those of urban residents, traders, civil servants and young graduates. Effective policies must recognise these differences and respond to the specific needs of individual communities.

Candidates should therefore demonstrate an understanding of local realities rather than assume that religious affiliation, regional identity or party loyalty will automatically secure electoral support.

Voters should also assess the performance of state and local governments, not just the federal administration. Education, primary healthcare, rural infrastructure and local economic development depend on effective governance and coordination across different levels of government.

Each administration must be held accountable for the responsibilities within its control. Disagreements between federal and state authorities should not become excuses for poor performance.

Ultimately, democracy becomes meaningful when citizens judge leaders by their achievements, integrity and ability to deliver results rather than their rhetoric or capacity to mobilise supporters.

The Verdict: Performance Must Replace Propaganda; The 2027 elections will feature debates about fuel subsidy removal, insecurity, economic hardship, education and competing claims about political performance. The importance voters attach to each issue will depend on their experiences and priorities.

For some, security will be paramount. Others will prioritise the cost of food, fuel and transportation, while many young people will be more concerned about education, employment and the prospect of building a decent future.

These concerns are interconnected. A secure community needs a functioning economy, while sustainable economic development depends on education, infrastructure and reliable public institutions. Neglecting any of these areas will undermine progress in the others.

Northern Nigerians should therefore demand evidence, clear targets and transparent reporting from candidates. Every serious contender should explain what they intend to achieve, how their proposals will be funded, when results should be expected and how the public will assess their performance.

Political office is a public trust, not a reward for party loyalty or an opportunity for personal enrichment. The ballot must be an instrument for securing better governance, not merely a ritual repeated every four years.

Dukawa writes from Abuja. He can be reached at abbahydukawa@gmail.com.

World.title: NEC Approves 90-Day Action Plan To Ease Cost Of Living For Nigerians
World.content:
.Reviews Ebola response, tasks states on preparedness

Deji Elumoye in Abuja

The National Economic Council (NEC) on Thursday Rose from its monthly meeting and endorsed a 90-day economic action plan proposed by the Federal Ministry of Finance to consolidate gains from President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms.

The plan focuses on reducing the cost of living, improving food affordability, attracting investment, and accelerating the delivery of projects with direct benefits to Nigerians.



NEC’s endorsement followed a presentation by the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Mr. Taiwo Oyedele, during its 161st meeting held virtually and chaired by Vice President Kashim Shettima.

This is just as the Vice President said while President Tinubu’s economic reform programme was designed to achieve broader national prosperity, governments at all levels have a responsibility to translate its objectives into improved living conditions for Nigerians.

The 90-day action plan identifies five priority areas: food affordability, tax harmonisation, completion of high-impact projects, resolution of investment bottlenecks and regulated household support.



The Council also approved the establishment of a national dashboard to track ongoing projects across the federation, with particular emphasis on transparency, accountability and accurate reporting of how proceeds from fuel subsidy removal are being utilised.

Presenting the economic outlook, Oyedele expressed optimism about the progress recorded under the Tinubu administration’s reform programme and the prospects for further economic recovery.



He identified the reduction of headline inflation and interest rates to single digits by 2027 as key policy objectives, noting that the next phase of reforms would require coordinated implementation across federal and state institutions.

The Finance Minister’s presentation placed particular emphasis on translating macroeconomic improvements into measurable benefits for households and businesses through targeted interventions, improved fiscal coordination and the removal of barriers to investment.

Addressing NEC members, Shettima charged state governors and relevant government institutions to ensure that the gains of the administration’s economic reforms translate into affordable transportation, improved healthcare, employment opportunities and greater financial security for Nigerians.



He said the success of economic policies must ultimately be measured by their impact on citizens’ daily lives, stressing that the responsibility of government extends beyond announcing reforms to building institutions that enable Nigerians to plan their futures with confidence.

“The first dividend of prosperity should be the confidence to plan a life. Our task is to make such confidence less dependent on fortune,” he said.



According to him, the Council’s deliberations on transportation, healthcare, police reform, and livestock development represent critical decisions about the quality of life Nigerians should expect from economic progress.

“Our separate jurisdictions must serve a common public interest,” Shettima said, emphasising that Nigeria’s federal structure must strengthen cooperation rather than become an obstacle to the delivery of essential services.

On the National Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) Bus Initiative, the Vice President underscored the need for state governments to support affordable transportation systems that would reduce the financial burden on commuters.

He maintained that the success of the programme should be determined by affordability and accessibility rather than the number of vehicles deployed.



“The cost of reaching a livelihood should never consume the livelihood itself. The passenger’s experience must guide our ambition, because the value of public transport resides in the journeys it makes possible. We should assess success through affordability and access, rather than fleet size alone,” he said.

Shettima maintained that President Tinubu’s economic reform programme was designed to achieve broader national prosperity, noting that governments at all levels have a responsibility to translate its objectives into improved living conditions.

“President Bola Tinubu has made economic reform the instrument of a larger national ambition. Our contribution must give that ambition social depth and productive strength.”



He urged governors to bring their understanding of local realities into national policy decisions, insisting that effective implementation requires clear responsibilities and practical agreements among the tiers of government.

“Our separate mandates must not become competing excuses. Each Governor carries knowledge that no federal document can supply,” he said.



The Vice President challenged members of the Council to judge every policy proposal by its capacity to reduce uncertainty, create opportunities and strengthen public confidence in government.

“Nigerians deserve institutions on which they can organise their lives. Providing that assurance is among the most consequential uses of public authority. That is the assurance we owe them,” Shettima said.

NEC also received an update on the reported Ebola outbreak in the Federal Capital Territory from the Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate, who allayed fears of a major public health crisis, assuring members that Nigeria possesses the institutional capacity to contain the situation.

The Minister briefed Council on efforts by the ministry, in collaboration with relevant stakeholders, to operationalise a robust national response system.



He identified coordination and governance, detection at points of entry, laboratory testing capacity, logistics for essential kits and personal protective equipment, and effective strategic communication as critical components of the response.

Pate acknowledged the efforts of 21 state government that had updated their response plans and urged the remaining 15 states to expedite the establishment of appropriate preparedness and response mechanisms.



Council also received the report of the NEC Ad Hoc Committee on Polio Eradication, chaired by the Governor of Gombe State, Alhaji Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, and resolved to direct states to conduct post-campaign reviews, particularly in areas where children were missed during immunisation exercises and communities affected by insecurity.

The Council emphasised the need for timely release of counterpart funds, strengthened routine immunisation, improved coordination with security agencies and closer cooperation among states to ensure better coverage in subsequent campaigns.

It further stressed that sustained political commitment from governors, traditional rulers and security agencies would remain critical to achieving the complete eradication of polio in Nigeria.



On livestock development, NEC received the report of the NEC Ad Hoc Committee on Livestock Development, chaired by the Governor of Kebbi State, Comrade Nasir Idris, and acknowledged the sector’s potential to stimulate economic growth, create employment and improve livelihoods across the country.

Council noted that all states had indicated interest in supporting the Federal Government’s livestock development initiatives and resolved to strengthen collaboration between the Federal and State Governments to accelerate reforms and unlock the sector’s economic potential.



Also, NEC received a presentation on the National Affordable Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) Transit Programme by the Chairman of the Presidential Initiative on Compressed Natural Gas and Electric Vehicles, Ismaeel Ahmed, and resolved to establish a joint financing framework between the Federal and State Governments to accelerate the deployment of CNG and electric vehicles across the country.

Council specifically directed that the programme must deliver tangible benefits to citizens through reduced transportation costs, rather than limiting its impact to the provision of alternative-energy vehicles.



It further resolved that relevant authorities should engage transport unions and operators to ensure that savings arising from the adoption of CNG and electric vehicles are passed on to commuters through lower fares.

To give effect to the decision, Council agreed to constitute a committee to coordinate the proposed financing arrangement, engage relevant stakeholders and develop practical measures to ensure that the economic benefits of the programme translate into affordable, accessible and sustainable transportation for Nigerians.

World.title: Terrorism: Man Bags 40 Years for Spying for Late Benue Militia Leader, Gana
World.content:
*Father of 10 sentenced to 10 years imprisonment for protecting Boko Haram members

*Another gets 20 years over membership of proscribed IPOB

Alex Enumah in Abuja

Three individuals bagged various jail terms on Thursday in Abuja, over offences relating to terrorism.

While Mr Sunday Frank was sentenced to 40 years imprisonment for spying for an alleged notorious bandit leader in Benue State, the late Terwase Akwaza, popularly known as Gana, a father of 10 children, Ali Shaban Hamma, on his part was jailed for 10 years for giving protection to members of the Boko Haram terrorists in his Borno Community.

Similarly, a self-confessed member of the Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB), Mr. Paul Okechukwu, was sentenced to 20 years jail term for belonging to the proscribed organisation.

Their conviction and sentencing on terrorism related offences was following the renewed efforts of the federal government to check the menace of terrorism and sound a warning to supporters and sympathizers of the heinous crime.

In a four-count charge brought before the court by the federal government, it was alleged that the convict, Frank, who hails from Katsina-Ala Local Government Area of Benue State, monitored and provided information to Gana about the movement of security agents.

It alleged that the convict’s coverage for Gana spanned Benue and Taraba states.

Gana, was said to have started as part of a militia group defending Benue communities against attacks by suspected herdsmen, but was killed in September 2020 by security operatives.

Specifically, in the charge, which was personally prosecuted by the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, SAN, it was alleged that the convict had also kidnapped one Samuel in 2022 and held him hostage until the sum of N40,000 was paid for his release.

He was accused of committing offences contrary to sections 21 and 24 of the Terrorism Prevention and Prohibition Act (TPPA) 2022.

Even though the defendant denied counts 1, 2 and 3 of the charge, which related to his alleged involvement in abduction, he pleaded guilty to count 4, which related to providing information to the Benue bandit leader.

Following his plea, the AGF applied for the counts the defendant denied to be struck out, a request the court granted.

Afterwards, the prosecution produced a witness who told the court that he was part of the team that investigated the defendant, adding that the convict had confessed to being a bandit and an informant to the late Gana.

He said the defendant, who was arrested in 2022, admitted that aside from giving updates on the movement of security agents to Gana, he also confessed to his involvement in banditry and participation in the abduction of two persons.

According to the witness, the defendant’s confessions were both oral and written.

Delivering judgment, Justice Hawa Yilwa of the Federal High Court, Abuja, found the defendant guilty and sentenced him to 40 years imprisonment, starting from the day of his arrest.

The court held that the convict should, upon completing his prison term, be subjected to a rehabilitation and deradicalisation programme.

In the case of Hamma, he was handed a 10- year jail term by Justice Binta Nyako of the Federal High Court, Abuja, shortly he pleaded guilty to the terrorism charges brought against him by the federal government.

The convict admitted knowing the Boko Haram members in his village and that he ignorantly refused to report them to the federal troops for arrest and prosecution.

He confessed that he had been associating with the terrorists since they arrived his village to unleash criminal activities on the people.

Upon his admission of guilt, the AGF pleaded with Justice Nyako to sentence the convict to a minimum of 20 years in view of the gravity of the heinous offence of terrorism.

Fagbemi argued that the terrorists would have been brought to book if the convict had not rendered protection to them.

However, the judge sentenced the convict to 10 years imprisonment, which she observed was the minimum jail term the Act on which the defendant was charged stipulated.

Besides, the judge ordered that the sentence should commence from 2012 when the convict was apprehended and kept in custody.

Meanwhile, Okechukwu, 48, was sentenced to 20 years imprisonment after he pleaded guilty to one of the two-count charge the federal government preferred against him.

The prosecution alleged in the first count that the defendant, who is from Nnewi South in Anambra State, had in 2021, while in Imo State, committed an offence by belonging to IPOB, a proscribed organisation, contrary to and punishable under Section 16 of the Terrorism (Prevention) (Amendment) Act, 2013.

In the second count, the federal government alleged that the defendant participated in an attack in which two security operatives were killed, and thereby committed an offence contrary to Section 2(1) of the Terrorism (Prevention) (Amendment) Act, 2013.

After the charge was read to him, the defendant pleaded not guilty to the second count.

In view of this development, and following an application by the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, SAN, who was in court to lead the prosecution, the court struck out the second count after it was withdrawn.

Relying on Section 72 of the Terrorism Prevention and Prohibition Act (TPPA) 2022, the Attorney-General applied for the court to allow a witness from the Department of State Services (DSS) to review some facts of the case.

The witness, whose name was given as “ABC” for the purpose of the trial, identified the defendant as a member of IPOB, which he said had since been outlawed.

He told the court that the defendant was involved in acts of terrorism, which he said included attacks on security agents.

The witness, who said he was part of a team that investigated the defendant, tendered a copy of the report, which was admitted as Exhibit A.

While applying for the defendant to be convicted, the AGF argued that the law prescribed a minimum sentence of 20 years for the offence.

“We therefore urge my lord to impose the maximum sentence, at least to serve as a deterrent to others and to also show that the nation cannot condone any act of terrorism,” the AGF added.

Meanwhile, immediately after the AGF made the application, the defendant broke down in tears in the dock, begging the court to temper justice with mercy.

Delivering judgment in the matter, Justice Hawa Yilwa found the defendant guilty and sentenced him to 20 years.

The court said it took note of the charge against the defendant and “the ripple effect it has on the nation.”

It held that the defendant should be remanded in any correctional facility chosen by the Comptroller-General of the Nigerian Correctional Service to serve his sentence, which should count from the day he was arrested.

The court held that the convict should be rehabilitated and redecalised upon the completion of his prison sentence.

World.title: 2027: Obasanjo’s Son Joins Tinubu Must Stay Movement, Backs Policy Continuity, Reforms
World.content:
Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja

Olujonwo Obasanjo, son of former President Olusegun Obasanjo has joined a political advocacy platform, Tinubu Movement for Sustainable Governance Foundation (TMS), popularly known as Tinubu Must Stay — promoting policy continuity, sustainable governance and public understanding of President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda.

The former president is supporting former Governor of Anambra state, Peter Obi while his son is supporting President Tinubu ahead of the 2027 presidential election.

Olujonwo, who serves as President of the Buhari Youth Organisation (BYO), President of Project One Nigeria, and Senior Special Assistant to the Ogun State Governor on Housing, announced his decision at a press conference in Abuja, where TMS leadership officially welcomed him into the organisation.

He said his decision was shaped by his political experience, understanding of Nigeria’s reform history and belief in the importance of sustaining government policies across administrations.

Speaking on his political background, Olujonwo said he has been a member of the All Progressives Congress (APC) since its formation.

He argued that several policies of the Tinubu’s administration have not been adequately explained to Nigerians, creating opportunities for misinformation and misinterpretation.

“I’ve been in the APC since 2014. I was there when my father hosted the late President Muhammadu Buhari and President Bola Ahmed Tinubu to form the movement. I’m not new to the party,” he said.

Olujonwo emphasised that communicating government policies should involve explaining their objectives, implementation processes and implications for citizens rather than relying on political slogans.

He added: “There’s a lot of noise out there, and people are distorting what’s going on. ASUU has had no strikes. Students have access to loans. Nigeria has become a massive construction site and an investors’ haven again. These are things we need to promote.”

Also, the Director‑General of the National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA) and National Coordinator of TMS, Kashifu Abdullahi, welcomed Olujonwo into the movement, describing his background as relevant to TMS’s advocacy for sustained economic reforms.
