Inuwa drew parallels between reforms introduced during the Obasanjo administration and those currently being implemented by President Tinubu.

He argued that national development requires consistency in policy implementation, warning that frequent reversals undermine investor confidence and disrupt long‑term planning.

Imuwa added: “You grew up in a family that led the second wave of reforms in Nigeria. Telecommunications liberalisation, banking reforms—these laid a solid foundation. Being raised in that family, you understand what reforms mean.

“We are building investors’ confidence. The naira is becoming strong. Our stock exchange is one of the fastest‑growing. The Dangote Refinery is a game changer. If we start reversing these policies, we’ll go back to where we were.”

Inuwa noted that the movement would continue expanding its nationwide structures while engaging stakeholders from diverse professional, political and social backgrounds.

He added that while TMS supports continuity beyond 2027, its broader mission is to strengthen policy sustainability and institutional development.

On his part, the Director‑General of TMS, Marcel Ngogbehei described Olujonwo’s entry as significant, noting his family’s historical association with major economic reforms and democratic consolidation.

Ngogbehei, who is a former Obidient cordinator recalled the liberalisation policies of former President Obasanjo, including telecommunications reforms and Nigeria’s external debt relief, which he said laid foundations for modern economic growth.

“We’re happy you have decided to take this step. Your father was one of those who revolutionised this country. The debt was paid off, and major innovations were introduced in liberalising the economy,” he said.

Ngogbehei explained that TMS was established to promote informed public engagement on government policies, address misconceptions about ongoing reforms and encourage citizens to assess governance through evidence and measurable outcomes.

He stressed that the movement intends to distinguish itself through factual communication and constructive dialogue.

“This is not about propaganda. We will engage respectfully, factually and transparently,” he said.

World.title: DSS Secures Seventh Death Sentence As Adamawa Court Convicts 3 Persons for Kidnapping Catholic Priests
World.content:
A high Court of Adamawa State, on Thursday, sentenced to death three persons who kidnapped two Catholic priests in February 2025.

Delivering judgement, Justice Christopher Mapeo found the three men guilty of criminal conspiracy to commit kidnapping, kidnapping, conspiracy to commit armed robbery, armed robbery, harboring a kidnapped person and negotiating to receive ransom for the release of

Reverend Fathers Matthew Dutsemi and Abraham Sauman.

The judge sentenced the three men, Taledo Demiel, Namomai Medan and Mikaila Yusuf, to death for kidnapping, armed robbery and other offences.

Thursday’s death sentence is the seventh secured by the DSS this year. On 20th May, 2026, Ekiti High Court sentenced two men, Ibrahim Abubakar and Abdullahi Abubakar to death by hanging for kidnapping.

About two weeks later, on 3rd June, 2026, a Federal High Court in Abuja sentenced to death by hanging, four men who, in June 2022, massacred scores of worshippers at the St. Francis Catholic church, Owo, Ondo State.

The convicts are Idris Abdulmalik Omeiza, Alqasim Idris, Jamiu Abdulmalik and Abdulkareem Idris.

Less than two weeks later, on 15th June, 2026, a Katsina High Court sentenced a female arms courier, Hauwa’u Mukhtar, to death by hanging.

The following day, on 16th June, 2026, a Kogi High Court sentenced Jibrin Halilu to death by hanging for kidnapping and murdering his neighbour in Obajana, an industrial town in the state.

About a week after the Kogi sentencing, on 22nd June, 2026, a Sokoto High court sentenced three persons Muhammed Yusuf Sallau, Jabbi Ahlaji Yale and Kabiru Muhammed, to death by hanging, for terrorism and for transporting arms.

Less than three months later, on

28th September 2026, a Sokoto High Court sentenced Ibrahim Usman aka Dan Iyali to death by hanging over his involvement in the killing of three kidnapped persons in the state.

World.title: Court Orders Speedy Trial of 3 Suspected Kidnappers of NYSC Members, Suspects to Remain in DSS Custody
World.content:
A high Court of Imo State, on Thursday, ordered the speedy trial of five persons accused of kidnapping 20 prospective National Youth Service Corps members on Independence Day.

The court set aside four days, starting from 27th October, to the 30th of the month for continuation of the trial,

urging prosecution and defence counsel to cooperate with the court to ensure judgment is delivered before January 2027.

Presiding Judge, Justice Emeka Orafu, made the appeal during proceedings in the cases involving three defendants accused of abducting prospective NYSC members and two others facing charges over a separate kidnapping case.

During the hearing, an officer of the Department of State Services (DSS), Ikem Emmanuel, testified on the investigation that led to the arrest of the three defendants in the NYSC-related case.

He told the court that the investigation involved intelligence gathering, data analysis, record checks, interviews and statements obtained from the defendants, victims and witnesses.

He stated that an identification parade was conducted, during which victims and witnesses identified the defendants as members of the criminal gang that kidnapped them.

The officer further told the court that one of the defendants, Usman Aliyu, admitted in his statement to participating in the operation and allegedly disclosed that 11 persons were involved.

The investigator maintained that the defendants’ statements were obtained in the presence of their legal representatives and DSS legal officers.

In a related proceeding involving two other defendants, the DSS officer also gave evidence on the investigation, stating that their statements were taken in the presence of their lawyers and DSS legal officers.

Following the proceedings, Justice Orafu adjourned the cases to October 27, 28, 29 and 30 for continuation of hearing, and ordered that the five defendants remain in the custody of the DSS.

World.title: Ebola: FG Directs Information Agencies to Intensify Enlightenment
World.content:
The Minister of Information and National Orientation, Alhaji Mohammed Idris, has directed agencies under his ministry to intensify public education on Ebola Virus Disease (EVD).

According to a statement issued by the minister’s Media Aide, Rabiu Ibrahim, the agencies include the National Orientation Agency (NOA), Nigerian Television Authority (NTA) and Federal Radio Corporation of Nigeria (FRCN).

Others are the Voice of Nigeria (VON) and the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN).

The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) had confirmed a case of Ebola involving a woman who recently travelled to Abuja from Uganda.

The woman is in isolation and receiving treatment, while health authorities have identified her contacts and are monitoring them.

The minister said: “The Federal Government is taking every necessary step to contain this case and protect Nigerians. Accurate and timely information is one of our strongest defences.

“Our agencies must reach every community, in every language, with clear facts on how Ebola spreads, how to protect ourselves and where to report suspected cases.”

Idris directed the agencies to collaborate with the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare and the NCDC to ensure all public information is verified and evidence-based.

He also tasked the NOA with deploying its nationwide offices for grassroots sensitisation, in collaboration with traditional and religious leaders, community groups and the media.

The minister urged Nigerians to remain calm, rely on official information and avoid spreading unverified claims on social media.

He advised members of the public to report suspected cases immediately by calling the NCDC’s toll-free, 24-hour emergency line on 6232. (NAN)

World.title: Suliman Carrim hit with fresh charges in vehicle theft case
World.content:
Businessman Suliman Carrim faces fresh criminal charges linked to the alleged attempted theft of two vehicles and the use of fraudulent bank documents. His case returns to court on 30 October 2026. Image: X

North West businessman Suliman Carrim faces fresh criminal charges linked to the alleged attempted theft of two vehicles belonging to Absa.

Carrim appeared in the Musina Magistrate’s Court in Limpopo on Thursday, 22 October, in connection with allegations involving fraudulent bank documents and an attempt to move vehicles across the border.

The case was postponed to 30 October for a bail application.



The latest development adds to Carrim’s legal troubles as he awaits a separate bail ruling over his alleged failure to appear before the Madlanga Commission.

CARRIM LINKED TO ALLEGED VEHICLE THEFT

According to police, the latest charges stem from an incident at the Beitbridge border post on 22 July 2026.

Officers intercepted two vehicles that were allegedly being transported from Mahikeng in the North West to Malawi.

Police spokesperson Brigadier Athlenda Mathe said investigators established that arrangements had allegedly been made to obtain bank authorisation documents for the vehicles to leave South Africa.

However, the required authorisation was allegedly not provided.

Investigators believe fraudulent bank documents were subsequently arranged to facilitate the vehicles’ movement across the border.



The vehicles were still under finance and were returned to the bank.

Two suspects were initially arrested in connection with the incident.

The Commission’s Recommendations Task Team added Carrim as an accused in the two cases on Wednesday, 21 October.

The National Prosecuting Authority alleges that Carrim acted with others in an attempt to remove the vehicles from South Africa using fraudulent documentation.

The allegations remain before the courts.

MADLANGA COMMISSION CASE CONTINUES

Carrim’s latest court appearance follows his arrest at OR Tambo International Airport earlier this month.

He was arrested while preparing to travel abroad after allegedly failing to return to the Madlanga Commission despite being directed to appear.

He appeared in the Pretoria Magistrate’s Court, where the State opposed his release on bail.

Prosecutors argued that he posed a flight risk.

Carrim’s legal representatives disputed this and maintained that he intended to return to South Africa.

The Pretoria court postponed its bail ruling to 28 October.

Carrim remains in custody and is expected back in the Musina Magistrate’s Court on 30 October in connection with the vehicle case.

World.title: Bank account costs: How South Africa compares with Botswana
World.content:
Bank customers in South Africa and Botswana face different charges for maintaining transactional accounts, with monthly fees and everyday transaction costs varying between banks.

The differences highlight why consumers need to consider more than just the advertised monthly fee when choosing where to bank.

How much do South African Bank customers pay?

According to its official 2026 pricing guide, Capitec charges customers R7.50 per month to maintain its main account. The fees took effect on 1 March 2026.



The bank also charges R2 for payments to other South African banks, R1 for payments to other Capitec customers and R3 for debit orders.

Customers who withdraw cash at another bank’s ATM pay R10 for every R1 000 withdrawn, according to Capitec’s published tariffs.

Meanwhile, First National Bank (FNB) offers an Easy Zero account with no monthly account fee. However, customers may still incur charges when conducting transactions.



FNB publishes separate pricing guides for its various accounts, meaning customers need to check the charges applicable to their chosen product.

What do Botswana bank customers pay?

In Botswana, Botswana Savings Bank (BSB) lists a monthly maintenance fee of P60 for its transactional account.

The account is designed for working people, young customers, pensioners and self-employed individuals. According to the bank’s official website, customers can deposit and withdraw money at BSB branches and ATMs.



Opening the account costs P100, while its listed features include free monthly statements, transaction notifications and transfers between BSB accounts.

BSB also offers an ordinary savings account with a lower monthly maintenance fee of P12. However, this is a different product, with withdrawal conditions that distinguish it from a standard transactional account.

The bank lists a P3.30 fee for withdrawals at its ATMs and charges P25 for subsequent over-the-counter withdrawals after the first free withdrawal.



Why the fees matter

The published tariffs show that banking costs depend on the account customers choose and how frequently they transact.

In South Africa, Capitec’s R7.50 monthly fee provides a clear baseline, while FNB’s Easy Zero account demonstrates that some products have no monthly maintenance charge.

In Botswana, BSB’s P60 transactional account fee is higher than its P12 ordinary savings account fee, but the two products offer different facilities and conditions.



Customers comparing banking costs across the two countries should therefore consider monthly maintenance, ATM withdrawals, electronic payments and other charges together.

The figures are based on the banks’ published tariffs and should be checked against the latest pricing guides before opening an account.

World.title: Mandla Ncikazi finds new home after Orlando Pirates departure
World.content:
Lamontville Golden Arrows have welcomed Mandla Ncikazi back to the club as their new head coach following his departure from Orlando Pirates.

The 57-year-old left the Buccaneers on Thursday, with Arrows announcing his return shortly afterwards. The club described him as a “proud son of the club” with a deep understanding of its traditions.

Ncikazi previously coached Golden Arrows during the 2020/21 season, guiding them to a club-record fourth-place finish in the PSL before joining Orlando Pirates as an assistant coach.



During his five-year spell at Pirates, Ncikazi contributed to the club’s success, helping the Soweto giants win nine trophies.

His return to Arrows follows discussions with the Pirates management on Thursday morning, during which he expressed his desire to pursue an opportunity to lead a team again. The club subsequently gave him its blessing to take up the new challenge.

Ncikazi leaves Pirates for Arrows

“Mandla leaves with our gratitude and our blessing. His contribution to Orlando Pirates has been evident throughout his time with us. We respect his wish to pursue this new opportunity and wish him success as he takes on a new responsibility,” said Pirates chairman Dr Irvin Khoza.

Ncikazi returns to a familiar environment, bringing valuable experience gained during his time at Pirates. His appointment will give Arrows an experienced coach as they look to build on their previous achievements.

Meanwhile, several Orlando Pirates supporters have wished the 57-year-old well following his departure.

Some fans have highlighted his contribution during the early stages of the Buccaneers’ success in the 2020s, acknowledging the role he played during his time at the club.



How do you rate Ncikazi as a coach?

World.title: Fake kidnapping: R40k ransom plot backfires
World.content:
A woman accused of staging her own kidnapping in a R40 000 ransom plot appeared in the Kwa-Thema Magistrates' Court on Thursday, 22 October 2026. Image: X

A Gauteng woman accused of staging her own kidnapping to demand R40 000 from her family has appeared in court, with prosecutors revealing how the alleged scheme unravelled.

Ntombifuthi Mavis Rumo, 37, appeared in the Kwa-Thema Magistrates’ Court on Thursday, 22 October.

The National Prosecuting Authority (NPA) alleges that Rumo conspired with two other people to fake her abduction after experiencing financial difficulties.



The case has been postponed to 29 October.

GAUTENG WOMAN ACCUSED OF FAKING KIDNAPPING

According to the NPA, Rumo allegedly met Bonginkosi Mndebele, 27, and another person on 7 October to discuss their financial problems.

Prosecutors allege that the three decided to stage her kidnapping and demand money from her family.

Her relatives subsequently received a ransom demand of R40 000.

However, the alleged plan ran into trouble when the family could not afford to pay.

The NPA said Rumo was dropped off along Vlakfontein Road on 12 October, with relatives instructed to collect her.



Police initially investigated the matter as a kidnapping.

However, the investigation later shifted towards an alleged staged abduction.

HUSBAND TAKES WIFE TO POLICE

The court heard that Rumo’s husband brought her to the police on 20 October.

During the investigation, she allegedly identified Mndebele as one of the people involved.

Police subsequently arrested the two suspects.

Rumo and Mndebele face charges of defeating the administration of justice.

A third alleged participant has not been charged.

Mndebele did not appear alongside Rumo on Thursday because he was in hospital.

STATE TO OPPOSE BAIL

The Kwa-Thema Magistrates’ Court postponed the case to 29 October for bail investigations and Mndebele’s appearance.

The State intends to oppose bail for both accused.

The court proceedings mark a major turn in a case that initially sparked concern for Rumo’s safety after her family reported her missing and received a ransom demand.

World.title: You can buy a holiday home in these coastal towns for R4 000 a month
World.content:
Owning a holiday home doesn’t have to be expensive.

South Africa’s vast coastline means there are dozens of opportunities to find or build an affordable holiday home.

5 Coastal towns with R300 000 holiday homes

These are your options for an affordable move-in-ready coastal home. Most are on KwaZulu-Natal’s South Coast, where the water’s warm year-round and there’s ample local tourism to keep the property occupied.



Scottburgh

Among the 178 sales this year in Scottburgh, the average sale price is R1.2 million.

But in Scottburgh Central, buyers can acquire a 1-bedroom flat with partial sea views for R300 000.

Without a deposit, the bond should be roughly R3 000 a month on this property. Levies in this block are R995, and rates and taxes start at R400.

Elsewhere in Scottburgh, buyers can purchase a 3-bedroom townhouse for R550 000.

The area periodically lists some very affordable homes.

Port Edward

In Port Edward, buyers can purchase a studio apartment for R400 000 in the Edwardian Hotel.



The apartment sleeps 2 adults and 2 children under 16.

The property includes amenities like a pool and restaurant.

Rates and taxes are R650, and levies are R1 134.

The nightly rate in peak season starts at R960.

Ramsgate

In Ramsgate, buyers can get a generously sized flat 100 metres from the beach.

One listing on Private Property is for a fully furnished 1-bedroom, 78-square-metre flat on Marine Drive within walking distance to Lawrence Rocks.

The bond on the property should be roughly R4 000 a month, while rates and taxes are R600.

Other flats in the building rent for R600 a night.

Bathurst

The only town on this list that’s not on the South Coast, Bathurst is a 20-minute drive to Port Alfred.

The average sale price in Bathurst is R690 000, but for R399 000, a buyer can get a 1-bedroom cottage on a quarter-acre plot. The property allows buyers a place to stay while they build their dream house.

Rates and taxes on the property are R235. In total, a buyer can expect to spend R4 219 on the home.

Margate

In Margate, buyers can get a 24-square-metre studio apartment starting at R335 000.

For this price, buyers can expect to spend R3 400 a month on a bond.

Other listings in Margate include a 2-bedroom flat 300 metres from the beach, which is listed for R450 000. Rates on this seaside flat are R500 and levies are R600.

Questions to ask before buying a holiday home

It can be tempting to buy a home thinking of all the good times you’ll have, or all the money it could make.

But just because a holiday home is cheap doesn’t mean it is affordable.

What’s the maintenance on a property?

The best holiday home costs almost nothing to maintain. Flats and townhouses are the best option. You won’t need to pay to maintain a garden or roof.

These are typically common areas you pay to maintain through your levies.

Is there any interest in the area?

If you decide to sell, there should be enough interest in the area that offloading it is easy. If the town isn’t developed or has less than desirable service delivery, selling the property could become a hassle.

What does it cost to own all-in?

Besides the bond, rates and levies should be your number one concern. Also consider insurance and home maintenance. If you want to rent it to others, consider what it will cost to have someone manage the property.

Will it be a reliable income source?

If you’re thinking of turning the place into a short-term rental, there must be enough demand year-round. If you want to use it as a holiday home for your family, you may miss out on peak season rates.

Then consider whether the body corporate or municipality allows short-term lets.

Can you only afford it if it is generating income?

The best holiday home is one you can afford to own even when it’s not to let. Rental income is never guaranteed.

Before buying, consider how long you could keep paying to maintain the property if it stops generating income.

World.title: DJ Warras murder: ‘Trial delayed long enough,’ says judge
World.content:
The murder case of DJ Warras (left), involving accused Victor Majola (centre) and Hlengiwe Buthelezi (right), has been postponed again following delays over legal representation. Images: X

The murder case of popular radio personality Warrick “DJ Warras” Stock has suffered another setback, with a Johannesburg judge expressing frustration over repeated delays.

Two accused, Victor Mthethwa Majola and his girlfriend Hlengiwe Goodness Buthelezi, appeared in the Gauteng High Court in Johannesburg on Thursday, 22 October.

However, outstanding issues surrounding their legal representation once again prevented pre-trial proceedings from moving forward.



Judge William Karam postponed the matter to 2 November.

DJ WARRAS MURDER CASE HITS ANOTHER DELAY

Both accused approached Legal Aid South Africa after experiencing difficulties securing private legal representation.

The court heard that Legal Aid had received the case docket, including electronic evidence, from their previous attorneys.

However, concerns about a possible conflict of interest between the accused complicated arrangements for their defence.

Legal Aid is now considering appointing private practitioners to represent them.

Karam made it clear that the delays could not continue indefinitely.



“This matter has been delayed long enough, with respect,” the judge said.

The prosecution also raised concerns about the lack of progress.

The State indicated that it was ready to set a trial date but had been unable to make meaningful progress with pre-trial proceedings for several months.

Both accused remain in custody.

WHAT HAPPENED TO DJ WARRAS?

Stock was shot and killed outside Zambesi Flats near the Carlton Centre in Johannesburg on 16 December 2025.

He had reportedly been overseeing security-related work at the building when gunmen approached his vehicle and opened fire.

Majola and Buthelezi face charges of premeditated murder and conspiracy to commit murder.

Meanwhile, Armindo Joaquim Pacula has already been sentenced to 25 years in prison for Stock’s murder after admitting his involvement.

Pacula also received sentences for firearm, ammunition and immigration offences.

The case against Majola and Buthelezi will return to court on Monday, 2 November, when the parties are expected to address outstanding pre-trial arrangements.

World.title: Mantashe ordered to apologise for sexist remarks
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The African National Congress (ANC) has ordered National Chairperson Gwede Mantashe to apologise for sexist remarks he made while campaigning for the party in the North West.

Mantashe was asked about allegations that councillors in a mining town demanded sex from women for jobs.

READ | 'We should have done better' - Podcasters apologise for crude comment

He used explicit language referring to female genitalia when answering the question and argued that it was an individual matter rather than an ANC issue.

The National Working Committee said Mantashe has been instructed to apologise and that the party now considers the matter closed.

World.title: Soweto teacher denies rape allegations
World.content:
SOWETO - Rape-accused teacher Kabelo Temba has denied forcing himself on a Grade 4 pupil.

The teacher has pleaded his innocence in an exclusive interview with eNCA.

He questioned allegations that the incident took place in the school toilet, arguing that the area would have been busy with pupils and staff at the time.

“At that time in the morning it's very busy, and someone could’ve asked, 'Sir, what are you doing here’ or there could’ve been other kids in the toilet,” he alleged.

However, the minor's mother said she believed her daughter's account and wanted the teacher to remain behind bars.

"I want him to rot in jail. I trust whatever my daughter has said is true, even if some people are trying to say it's not true. I'm standing with my daughter 100%."

She also called for greater awareness of sexual abuse and more support for children who experience it.

Temba has since handed himself over to police and has been charged with the rape of the nine-year-old girl.

Temba made his first appearance at the Protea Magistrate's Court on Thursday, following days of community protests demanding his removal from the primary school in Soweto.

He remains in custody until next Thursday's bail application

World.title: Probe initiated by Public Protector office
World.content:
PRETORIA - The Public Protector has launched a probe into the failures that led to the water crisis in Pretoria East.

The probe was initiated after the EFF and Freedom Front Plus approached the Public Protector's office.

READ | Bronkhorstspruit water crisis: Chlorine supply and costs under scrutiny

The Bronkhorstspruit Water treatment plant ran out of chlorine weeks ago.

Residents were never told. Over 400 people have since fallen ill.

The Public Protector will look into the failures in water treatment, and why the metro failed to issue warnings.

World.title: Revised White Paper launch shifts focus towards implementation- SALGA
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The South African Local Government Association (SALGA) said government's launch of a White Paper is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to rebuild and reinvent local government, further calling it a reset.

SALGA joined hands with the Dullar Omar Institute to submit proposals to shape this reviewed draft White Paper.

Reacting to the White Paper launch, SALGA CEO Sithole Mbanga said the review came after more than two decades of democratic local government during which the country has made progress, but also identified weaknesses disabling local government to achieve its objectives.

“In that period, we have learned that there are certain good things that have happened, but we've also realised that there are certain things that are disabling local government to achieve its objectives. So it is an opportunity for us to look at a new way of transforming local government,” he said.

The same sentiments were echoed by Local Government expert Miyelani Holeni, who said previous attempts to fix struggling municipalities had often relied on individual turnaround strategies rather than addressing weaknesses across the entire system

World.title: Pirates confirm Ncikazi exit as Golden Arrows comes calling
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Orlando Pirates have now confirmed the departure of assistant coach Mandla Ncikazi.

Ncikazi will return to Golden Arrows to take over as head coach from Pitso Dladla.

He departs with nine trophies earned as part of the Pirates technical team, where he served predominantly as assistant coach, including a brief spell as co-coach in 2025.

“Mandla leaves with our gratitude and our blessing. His contribution to Orlando Pirates has been evident throughout his time with us. We respect his wish to pursue this new opportunity and wish him success as he takes on a new responsibility,” said Pirates chairman Irvin Khoza.

World.title: R40,000 ransom plot? Woman accused of faking her own abduction
World.content:
KWATHEMA - A shocking twist in the case of 37-year-old Ntombifuthi Rumo, who is accused of staging her own kidnapping.

Together with her alleged accomplice, she was arrested after investigations by Kwa-Thema detectives, the Anti-Kidnapping Unit, and Crime Intelligence.

Investigations revealed that Rumo allegedly conspired with an accomplice to stage her own kidnapping in an attempt to extort money from her cousin.

Both suspects face charges of fraud, defeating the ends of justice, and staging a crime scene.

Authorities have indicated that they are pursuing an additional suspect in the case.

Rumo was reported missing on 7 October.

Later, a man called from her cellphone, demanding R40,000 for her release.

Threatening messages followed, along with a video showing her naked, injured and pleading with her mother for help.

During the search for Rumo, Thomas Sibeko was wrongfully arrested for kidnapping.

Rumo was found near Kwa-Thema cemetery on 20 October, just a day before a community prayer service for her safe return.

The incident has sparked fears that false reports of GBV and kidnapping may undermine genuine victims' quest for justice.

The matter returns to court on 28 October to allow the second suspect to appear in person.

eNCA's Bafedile Moerane has more details in the video above.

World.title: Our people must never be held hostage by political instability - Ramaphosa
World.content:
BOKSBURG - With less than two weeks left before citizens head to the polls, President Cyril Ramaphosa has acknowledged that the local government system has failed to meet expectations of the people it is meant to serve.

From unreliable water and electricity supply issues to deteriorating roads and poorly maintained infrastructure, these consequences, Ramaphosa said, are felt in the daily lives of residents.

He was speaking at the launch of the final blueprint of the revised White Paper on local government at the Birchwood Hotel in Bokesburg on Thursday.

READ | New local govt policy aims to improve service delivery within 18 months - Hlabisa

While the revised White Paper seeks to correct historical wrongs, it is also aimed at reforming service delivery, governance and financial management in municipalities.

“Too many communities have grown accustomed to services that are unreliable, infrastructure that is deteriorating and municipal administrations that are unresponsive. This cannot continue," Ramaphosa said.

According to the President, the original White Paper published in 1998 set out what he called a blueprint for democratic local government.

At the time, he said they worked from "certain assumptions"; those included joining unequal municipalities which would produce viable institutions while believing that economic growth would strengthen municipal revenue.

But over time this system would prove otherwise.

READ | Ramaphosa to unveil revised White Paper on local government

Ramaphosa said municipalities were assigned power and responsibility that in some cases "outstripped their capabilities and funding".

“We underestimated the importance of training up a new generation of engineers, town planners and municipal managers. We underestimated how politicised appointments would open the door to corruption, malfeasance and a lack of accountability. Today our people live with these consequences.”

Ramaphosa conceded that the revised White Paper "sets out to tackle dysfunction by reforming the entire system, not merely by responding to its symptoms".

His speech also extended to the role of political leaders who he said must lead with integrity, provide oversight, with accountability being exercised fairly, lawfully and consistently.

World.title: Varsities' mess: Broken promises, students in limbo as strike drags on
World.content:
TUK lecturers enter Day 10 of strike over pay, working conditions and CBA implementation. [Benard Orwongo, Standard]

It is a mess that is taking a toll on university students, disrupting the learning calendar and threatening the future of thousands of students while the government seems slow to act.

The lecturers’ strike is now in its 22nd day with no sign of an end, even as the Government remains locked in a dispute over a new pay deal it had committed to resolve within a month of ending last year’s 49-day industrial action, leaving thousands of students facing another disrupted academic year.

World.title: Ruto hands over COMESA chairmanship, pushes for levy to fund regional programmes
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President Ruto and Zimbabwean President Emmerson Mnangagwa during the handover of the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa chairmanship at the bloc’s 25th Summit of Heads of State and Government in Harare, Zimbabwe, on Thursday, October 22, 2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto has handed over the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (COMESA) chairmanship to Zimbabwean President Emmerson Mnangagwa.

Ruto took over the one-year chairmanship from Burundi’s President Évariste Ndayishimiye at the 24th COMESA Summit in Nairobi on October 9, 2025.

His tenure focused on using digital technology to deepen regional integration, expand trade and promote inclusive growth.

He handed over the role on Thursday, October 22, during the 25th Comesa Summit of Heads of State and Government in Harare, Zimbabwe, where he urged the regional bloc to fast-track a market levy to finance its programmes and institutions.

“We cannot be ambitious in our plans and timid in our financing. Every programme we agree upon must be matched by the resources to deliver it. Otherwise, our communiqués will promise what our budgets cannot pay for,” Ruto said.

He urged the Comesa Secretariat to fast-track Article 168 of the COMESA Treaty, which provides for the Comesa Market Levy, as the organisation seeks sustainable and predictable financing.

The treaty establishes the levy to generate resources for financing the bloc’s activities.

Ruto said officials from finance ministries, central banks and other relevant agencies would meet to consider a draft COMESA Resource Mobilisation Strategy aimed at strengthening member states’ ownership of regional programmes and finding new ways to raise funds.

He called on member states to make financing central to their discussions, warning that the bloc’s institutions and integration agenda would depend on their ability to fund agreed commitments.

“Can we finance what we commit, and deliver what we finance?” he asked.

Ruto also urged African countries to channel more of their domestic financial resources into African institutions rather than leaving funds in foreign accounts while development projects lack capital.

He said Africa holds more than $4 trillion in domestic financial assets, arguing that regional financial institutions could mobilise more of these resources to support trade, infrastructure and development.

Ruto named the Trade and Development Bank (TDB), the African Trade and Investment Development Insurance (ATIDI) and ZEP-RE among the institutions that could mobilise capital for regional priorities.

He urged African governments to place more reserves with these institutions, finance more projects through them and support their bonds and guarantees.

The outgoing Comesa chairperson said the bloc needed stronger regional value chains and more trade among member states as global supply chains faced disruption and protectionism returned.

“Regional integration is no longer a dream we discuss. It is an economic and strategic necessity,” he noted.

Ruto said Comesa’s economic growth rose from 5.6 per cent in 2024 to 6.4 per cent in 2025, while inflation fell from 31 per cent to 13.2 per cent.

Exports among member states increased by 10.5 per cent to $14.7 billion, their highest level between 2020 and 2025, while exports to global markets rose by 6 per cent to $212 billion, he said.

He argued that African countries needed to process more raw materials locally instead of exporting them and importing finished products.

“To every partner who seeks our minerals, our markets and our young workforce, our offer is clear: invest with us, process with us, build with us,” Ruto added.

He called for partnerships based on mutual benefit and equal treatment, saying African countries should have a greater role in determining how their resources and markets contribute to economic development.

World.title: Judge certifies fresh bid to jail Sakaja, Charles Kerich over Sh76.7m debt as urgent
World.content:
Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja. [File, Standard]

The High Court has certified as urgent a fresh application seeking to have Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja, former Finance Executive Charles Kerich and two other county officials jailed over an alleged breach of a court-approved payment plan in a Sh106.7 million legal fees dispute.

Justice Francis Gikonyo certified the application by Kwengu & Company Advocates seeking to reinstate a three-month jail sentence previously imposed on Kerich and hold Sakaja, current Finance County Executive Committee Member Ibrahim Auma Nyangoya and Chief Officer for Finance Asha Abdi accountable for the alleged failure to pay Sh76.7 million.

World.title: Kenya confirms third Ebola case
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kenya has confirmed a third case of Ebola involving a 65-year-old woman who is a close relative of the first two patients.

The Ministry of Health, in a statement, said the woman developed a fever, sore throat and malaise while in quarantine, prompting her isolation and testing.

Her samples tested positive for Ebola at both the National Virology Reference Laboratory and the Kenya Medical Research Institute (KEMRI).

According to the Health Director-General Patrick Amoth, the patient has been transferred to an infectious disease unit, where she is receiving supportive care and being monitored.

“Having been in quarantine, she was diagnosed early and is currently receiving supportive care, improving her chances of recovery while limiting the risk of further spread of the disease,” the statement read.

The second patient, on the other hand, is in stable condition and responding well to supportive care.

The latest case brings the number of confirmed Ebola infections in Kenya to three.

According to the Ministry, of the 130 contacts identified so far, 127 had been traced and placed in quarantine, with efforts ongoing to trace the remaining three.

World.title: Motorists, households face fresh fuel price hikes
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

EPRA attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East. [FIle, Standard]

The Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA) has increased fuel prices, raising the cost of super petrol by Sh12.93 per litre, diesel by Sh9.90, and kerosene by Sh28.49.

The new prices, effective from October 15 to November 14, 2026, will see motorists in Nairobi pay up to Sh226.96 per litre for super petrol, Sh227.76 for diesel, and Sh219.85 for kerosene.

EPRA Director-General Edward Mwirigi Kinyua attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East, which has disrupted petroleum supply chains and driven up the cost of importing fuel.

The rise in kerosene prices is likely to hit low-income households that rely on the fuel for cooking and lighting.

Meanwhile, higher diesel prices could raise the cost of transporting goods and operating public service vehicles, potentially driving up fares and commodity prices.

Diesel is a key fuel for the country's freight transport sector and a significant portion of public service vehicle operations, meaning the increase could have a ripple effect across the economy.

The latest review comes after EPRA maintained pump prices during the September 15 to October 14 pricing period, despite a decline in the cost of importing petrol.

World.title: Oburu Oginga to leave hospital soon - ODM
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

ODM SG Catherine Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician.

ODM Secretary General Catherine Omanyo has dismissed social media reports about the health of party leader Oburu Oginga, saying he is recovering well and is expected to be discharged from hospital either today or tomorrow.

Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician, accusing them of exploiting his health condition to attract online attention and increase engagement.

“It's unfortunate what I've been reading on social media. Those people who are seeking to have more likes or viewers, they will be disappointed because he's up, he's well, he's fine. In fact, he's headed home either today or tomorrow,” she said.

Omanyo insisted that the reports had exaggerated his situation, dismissing claims of his death and assuring the public that he was doing well.

She noted that health conditions could fluctuate, saying Oburu's position as ODM party leader had made his well-being a subject of heightened public interest.

“Everybody, everybody, including you and me, our health is not static. You can be under the weather any time. It's just that he's a party leader, and it makes breaking news,” Omanyo said.

She urged social media users to exercise restraint when discussing the health of public figures, warning against spreading unverified reports, particularly claims of death, before confirmation from credible sources.

Her remarks come amid growing speculation on social media about Oburu's health, with some users circulating unverified claims about his condition.

World.title: Kenya declares Ebola a formidable epidemic disease, sets new rules
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale, who declared Ebola caused by the Bundibugyo virus a formidable epidemic disease under the Public Health Act. [File,Standard]

Kenya has declared Ebola virus a formidable epidemic disease, introducing new rules governing screening, isolation, quarantine, contact tracing and the handling of bodies.

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale issued the declaration through a legal notice published in the Kenya Gazette on Monday, October 12, under Section 35 of the Public Health Act.

The declaration follows Kenya’s confirmation of its first imported case of Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease on October 6, after a Kenyan citizen who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo travelled through Uganda to Nairobi. The patient died despite receiving supportive treatment.

The case prompted health authorities to trace people who may have come into contact with the patient and strengthen screening at points of entry.

In an update on October 12, the World Health Organization (WHO) said Kenya had listed 127 contacts, with 94 in quarantine, and screened more than 665,000 travellers at points of entry.

WHO also supplied protective equipment and testing materials worth about US$70,000 to support the response.

The government published two legal notices on October 12. Legal Notice No. 203 declares the disease a formidable epidemic, while Legal Notice No. 204 establishes the Public Health (Ebola Disease) Rules, 2026.

The regulations provide for screening at points of entry, medical assessment, isolation, referral, quarantine and monitoring.

They also assign responsibilities to transport operators, health facilities, medical practitioners and laboratories.

Health authorities will conduct investigations and contact tracing, while designated health facilities will manage suspected and confirmed cases. The rules also provide for the inspection and decontamination of premises.

The regulations cover the safe and dignified disposal of bodies, burial procedures, record-keeping, transportation and repatriation. They also address public communication, media houses’ responsibilities in public sensitisation and assistance from enforcement agencies.

The rules provide for offences and penalties, although the Gazette extract does not specify the penalties for individual violations.

What the declaration means

Bundibugyo virus disease is a form of Ebola that spreads through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person or contaminated materials.

Contact with the body of someone who has died from the disease can also expose people to infection during unsafe burial practices.

Symptoms can include fever, fatigue, muscle pain, headache and sore throat, followed by vomiting and diarrhoea. The incubation period ranges from two to 21 days.

WHO says no approved vaccine or specific treatment currently exists for the Bundibugyo strain, making early detection, isolation, supportive care and contact tracing central to controlling its spread.

The health agency has advised against travel or trade restrictions on Kenya, Uganda and the Democratic Republic of Congo based on the information available.

The new rules establish a legal framework for managing the disease, from identifying suspected infections and monitoring contacts to caring for patients and preventing exposure during burials.
