Bradesco, one of Brazil’s largest private banks, earned R$7.1 billion (about US$1.4 billion) in the third quarter of 2026, matching analyst forecasts. The bank published the results on the evening of Thursday, 22 October, and said tight cost control offset slower income from lending.

The result shows how high interest rates are squeezing credit in Brazil’s economy. Profit grew, but more customers fell behind on payments, and the bank set aside more money for bad loans.

The Numbers Behind the Profit

Profit: R$7.1 billion (US$1.4 billion), up 0.8% from the second quarter and 14.6% from about R$6.2 billion (US$1.2 billion) a year earlier.

R$7.1 billion (US$1.4 billion), up 0.8% from the second quarter and 14.6% from about R$6.2 billion (US$1.2 billion) a year earlier. Loan book: R$1.15 trillion (US$228 billion), up about 1% in three months and 11% in a year.

R$1.15 trillion (US$228 billion), up about 1% in three months and 11% in a year. Bad loans: 4.6% of loans were more than 90 days overdue, against 4.3% in June and 4.1% a year ago.

4.6% of loans were more than 90 days overdue, against 4.3% in June and 4.1% a year ago. Provisions: The bank set aside R$10.6 billion (US$2.1 billion) for expected losses, up 6.6% in three months and 24.3% in a year.

The bank set aside R$10.6 billion (US$2.1 billion) for expected losses, up 6.6% in three months and 24.3% in a year. Profitability: Return on average equity, a measure of profit relative to shareholder capital, was 15.6%. Before the new capital, it was 16.1%.

All amounts in US$ use the EODHD rate of 5.05 reais per dollar on 22 October. The 90-day overdue rate is the standard gauge of how many borrowers have stopped paying.

Why Rising Bad Loans Matter

Provisions grew much faster than profit, which is the main caution in the report. A bank that sets aside more for losses is telling investors it expects more borrowers to struggle.

Chief executive Marcelo Noronha told reporters, as Folha de S.Paulo reported: “The credit market is more restricted. Interest rates remain high and the economy is slowing. It is a challenging scenario for everyone.” He said the bank focused on loans backed by collateral and on customers with strong credit records.

In Plain English Recurring profit: profit after removing one-off items, the figure analysts track. Provisions: money a bank sets aside today for loans it expects to lose. Overdue 90 days: loans where the borrower has not paid for three months.

How Bradesco Held Up

The bank said slower credit income was offset by income that does not depend on lending, such as fees for managing money, capital-markets work and group purchase plans called consórcios. It also kept a close hold on spending.

Bradesco raised about R$10 billion (US$2 billion) from new shares, following the capital raise announced in July. The bank said the money will support technology, sales efficiency and growth. See also Bradesco’s customer-complaint ranking and Bradesco’s company profile.

What It Means for US Readers

Bradesco’s shares trade in New York as the ADR BBD, so US investors hold this risk directly. In line profit with rising overdue loans gives investors both a steady earnings base and a reason to watch credit quality in Brazil’s stock market.

The report also reads as a gauge of Brazil’s households and companies. A slowing economy and costly credit usually show up first in bank provisions, which makes this line a useful early signal for the rest of the sector.

What Is Not Known

Share reaction: The results came out after the Brazilian market closed, so the first full trading reaction is likely on Friday.

The results came out after the Brazilian market closed, so the first full trading reaction is likely on Friday. Peak for bad loans: It is not yet clear whether the overdue rate has peaked.

It is not yet clear whether the overdue rate has peaked. Next date: Brazil votes in the presidential runoff on Sunday, 25 October, which can move the real and bank shares.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much profit did Bradesco make in the third quarter of 2026?

Bradesco reported recurring profit of R$7.1 billion (about US$1.4 billion). That is 0.8% more than in the second quarter and 14.6% more than a year earlier.

Did Bradesco meet analyst expectations?

Yes. Analysts expected a profit of about R$7.1 billion, so the result was in line.

Why are Bradesco’s bad loans rising?

Loans overdue by more than 90 days reached 4.6% from 4.3% in June. The chief executive pointed to high interest rates and a slowing economy.

Is Bradesco listed in the United States?

Yes. Its American depositary receipts trade on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker BBD.

World.title: Serbia Votes Sunday After Student Protests
World.content:
Serbia votes in a snap parliamentary election on Sunday, 25 October 2026, after nearly two years of student-led street protests. This is the latest chapter in our Europe political crisis series, which explains why Europe’s politics are breaking country by country.

The vote is the first national test of whether a protest movement can turn into votes. President Aleksandar Vučić resigned on 27 September to run for prime minister.

Key Facts What: Serbia holds an early parliamentary election after almost two years of student-led protests.

Serbia holds an early parliamentary election after almost two years of student-led protests. When: Sunday, 25 October 2026; Belgrade is five to six hours ahead of US Eastern Time that day.

Sunday, 25 October 2026; Belgrade is five to six hours ahead of US Eastern Time that day. Who: Vučić’s Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) faces the student-backed “Students Win” list.

Vučić’s Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) faces the student-backed “Students Win” list. Why it matters: Vučić’s SNS has been in power since 2012 and faces a vote shaped by the protests.

Vučić’s SNS has been in power since 2012 and faces a vote shaped by the protests. Prediction markets: Kalshi prices the SNS-led list at 66% and the student list at 28% to win (22 October 2026, 5:25 pm ET).

What Happened

The protests began after a concrete canopy collapsed at the Novi Sad railway station on 1 November 2024, killing 16 people. Protesters blamed corruption and demanded accountability for the disaster.

Vučić, who cannot run for another presidential term, resigned as president on 27 September 2026 and plans to lead the SNS ticket as its candidate for prime minister. Parliament Speaker Ana Brnabić is acting president, according to Al Jazeera.

File photo: a protest crowd in central Belgrade, March 2025. Photo: Emilija Knezevic / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 4.0.

Who Is Running

The Republic Election Commission (RIK) registered the “Student List – Students Win” for the vote, with 250 candidates, according to N1. The list is led by Ilija Srđanović and includes professors and other experts.

What Prediction Markets Say

Serbian parliamentary election winner: SNS-led list 66%, student list 28% (Kalshi, about 14,500 contracts traded).

Next prime minister: Vučić 73%, Ilija Srđanović 13% (Kalshi, about 20,800 contracts traded).

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

Kalshi is regulated in the US by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC). Prices are bets, not polls.

Europe’s Wider Protest Wave

In Albania, student-led protests have run for about a week, with demonstrators demanding Prime Minister Edi Rama’s resignation. In Greece, teachers and students rallied on 21 October demanding more education funding.

In France, a new Yellow Vest protest is called for Saturday, 24 October, after weekend rioting. In Italy, the government said it would send 500 soldiers to Milan, Deputy Prime Minister Matteo Salvini announced on 19 October.

In Spain, a snap election is scheduled for 29 November 2026 after parliament failed to pass housing measures. Reporting stresses that these movements are largely separate, not centrally coordinated.

What It Means for US Readers

Serbia’s result will show whether sustained street protest can unseat a long-serving government at the ballot box. A student win would be read across Europe, where governments face anger over living costs and public services.

A strong SNS result would show that protest alone has limits. Either way, Serbia’s ties with Brussels, Moscow and Washington will be watched.

What Is Not Known

We have not confirmed the voting hours or an official turnout forecast. It is also unclear how large the gap between the two main lists really is.

Frequently Asked Questions

When is Serbia’s election?

Serbia votes on Sunday, 25 October 2026. Belgrade is five to six hours ahead of US Eastern Time that day.

Why is Serbia holding an early election?

Nearly two years of student-led protests demanded it after the 2024 Novi Sad station collapse. Vučić resigned as president on 27 September 2026 to run for prime minister.

Who is the main challenger?

The student-backed “Students Win” list, with 250 candidates, is the main challenger to the SNS. Ilija Srđanović leads it.

What do prediction markets say?

Kalshi priced the SNS-led list at 66% and the student list at 28% to win on 22 October 2026. These are bets, not polls.

World.title: McLaren Brings Upgrades to US Grand Prix
World.content:
Key Facts

What: McLaren brings braking and small floor upgrades to Austin.

McLaren brings braking and small floor upgrades to Austin. Who: Chief technical officer Rob Marshall calls it a ‘modest selection of upgrades’.

Chief technical officer Rob Marshall calls it a ‘modest selection of upgrades’. Why: McLaren scored 33 points in three races; Red Bull is seven points behind.

McLaren scored 33 points in three races; Red Bull is seven points behind. Race: Sunday, 25 October, 4:00 p.m. ET (3:00 p.m. CDT), 56 laps.

Sunday, 25 October, 4:00 p.m. ET (3:00 p.m. CDT), 56 laps. Practice: Friday, 23 October: FP1 at 1:30 p.m. ET and FP2 at 5:00 p.m. ET.

McLaren will bring a ‘modest selection of upgrades’ to the United States Grand Prix in Austin, Texas, says chief technical officer Rob Marshall. The package targets braking reliability and performance, and our US Grand Prix 2026 updates follow the weekend.

McLaren Targets Braking Gains

Besides the brake work, McLaren will test small floor changes at the Circuit of The Americas. The reigning constructors’ champions say their last three races fell ‘significantly short of expectations’, with only 33 points scored.

This story is part of our coverage of the us grand prix 2026. Dates, times and how to follow it are in our guide.

Red Bull took four top-three finishes in that run, including two wins for Max Verstappen. That cut McLaren’s lead in the fight for third in the constructors’ standings to just seven points.

Archive photo: a Formula 1 car passes the tower at Circuit of The Americas in 2018.

Five Teams Run Special Liveries

Five of the 11 Formula 1 teams will race with revised liveries or race-weekend designs in Austin: Ferrari, Mercedes, Aston Martin, Haas and Cadillac. Ferrari’s SF-26 cars for Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc carry an engineering-themed design with blueprint-style artwork.

Mercedes has added blue sections to its W17 and special race suits for George Russell and championship leader Kimi Antonelli. Aston Martin’s design marks five years of its Cognizant partnership, Haas promotes the film Godzilla Minus Zero, and Cadillac uses Texas and western-leather motifs.

Austin Weekend Schedule

Free Practice 1 is on Friday, 23 October at 12:30 p.m. CDT (1:30 p.m. ET), and Free Practice 2 is at 4:00 p.m. CDT (5:00 p.m. ET). On Saturday, final practice is at 12:30 p.m. CDT (1:30 p.m. ET) and qualifying at 4:00 p.m. CDT (5:00 p.m. ET).

The race starts on Sunday, 25 October at 3:00 p.m. CDT (4:00 p.m. ET) and runs 56 laps. Austin opens an Americas triple-header, followed by Mexico and Brazil.

What It Means for US Readers

This is a home race for American fans, and the times above are ready for an Eastern Time viewer. Ferrari arrives after Charles Leclerc finished second in Singapore.

Kimi Antonelli could secure his first drivers’ championship in Austin, though the exact points arithmetic has not been published.

What Is Not Known

It is not known whether McLaren’s revisions will deliver a measurable gain or change the order against Red Bull and Ferrari. No FIA technical ruling or measured performance data had been published by 22 October.

The finishing combinations Antonelli needs to clinch the title in Austin have not been reported. No prediction market on the McLaren upgrades was found.

What upgrades is McLaren bringing to Austin?

McLaren is bringing a ‘modest selection of upgrades’ aimed at braking reliability and performance. It will also test small floor changes at the Circuit of The Americas.

When does the United States Grand Prix start in Eastern Time?

The race starts on Sunday, 25 October at 4:00 p.m. ET (3:00 p.m. CDT). It runs 56 laps.

Ferrari, Mercedes, Aston Martin, Haas and Cadillac have unveiled special looks. Aston Martin marks five years of its Cognizant partnership, and Cadillac uses Texas and western-leather motifs.

McLaren scored only 33 points in the last three races and called the results ‘significantly short of expectations’. Red Bull has closed to within seven points in the constructors’ standings.

World.title: Grenada Election Race Enters Final Two Weeks
World.content:
Key Facts

Vote: Thursday, 5 November 2026; polls 6:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. local (5:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. ET).

Thursday, 5 November 2026; polls 6:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. local (5:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. ET). Seats: All 15 House seats are contested; eight form a government.

All 15 House seats are contested; eight form a government. Campaign: The opposition New National Party runs a ‘Better Grenada’ campaign.

The opposition New National Party runs a ‘Better Grenada’ campaign. Pledge: Leader Emmalin Pierre promises to cut corporate tax from 28% to 25%.

Leader Emmalin Pierre promises to cut corporate tax from 28% to 25%. 2022 result: The ruling NDC won nine seats; the NNP won six.

Grenada votes on 5 November, and the opposition New National Party (NNP) is pushing its ‘Better Grenada’ campaign into the final two weeks. Leader Emmalin Pierre told supporters to focus on defeating Prime Minister Dickon Mitchell’s National Democratic Congress (NDC), and our Grenada election updates follow the race daily.

Campaign Enters Its Final Stretch

Pierre is the first woman to lead the NNP into a general election. She succeeded former prime minister Keith Mitchell, who stepped down as party leader in 2024.

Grenada Election Race Enters Final Two Weeks

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Policy Platform and Reaction

Pierre’s platform cuts corporate tax from 28% to 25% and gives free transport to students who need help. It also expands night and weekend bus services.

Prime Minister Mitchell expects the NDC to win and rejects talk of a hung parliament. “While anything is possible, I don’t think we will have a hung parliament at all,” he said, adding that eight seats, not all 15, decide who governs.

How the Vote Works

Election day is Thursday, 5 November, with polls open 6:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Atlantic Standard Time (5:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Eastern). Police officers vote early on 2 November.

All 15 single-member House seats are contested across Grenada, Carriacou and Petite Martinique. Parliament was dissolved on 2 October, and voter registration closed the same day.

A Three-Party Contest

The NDC seeks a second consecutive term under Mitchell, an attorney. The Democratic People’s Movement, led by former foreign affairs minister Peter David, is also expected to contest seats.

In the 23 June 2022 election the NDC won nine seats and the NNP won six. The NNP won all 15 seats in 1999, 2013 and 2018.

What It Means for US Readers

Grenada is a Caribbean democracy of about 120,000 people, and this vote tests whether the NDC can keep its nine-seat majority. The result will shape tax, energy and public-service policy on the island.

The election comes almost a year before the constitutional deadline in October 2027.

What Is Not Known

No named-institute poll and no active prediction market on the Grenada vote were found, so there is no percentage forecast to publish. The final certified candidate list is not yet fully reported, and it is unclear how many seats the Democratic People’s Movement will seriously contest.

A High Court claim on the electoral process is pending, and the attorney general’s office says it is being handled. No separate time for the official results announcement has been reported.

Frequently Asked Questions

When is Grenada’s general election?

Grenada votes on Thursday, 5 November 2026. Polls are open 6:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. local time, which is 5:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Eastern Time.

Who leads the main opposition party?

Emmalin Pierre leads the New National Party and is the first woman to lead it into a general election. She succeeded former prime minister Keith Mitchell in 2024.

How many seats win a government?

Eight of the 15 House of Representatives seats are needed to form a government. In 2022 the NDC won nine seats and the NNP won six.

World.title: Court Gives Meta 24 Hours on Lula Channel
World.content:
The plenary chamber of Brazil’s Superior Electoral Court in Brasília. File photo, 12 May 2026. (Photo: TSE, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons)

BRAZIL · ELECTIONS

Published Thursday, 22 October, 5:12 p.m. ET · Source: Brazil’s Superior Electoral Court (TSE) order, as reported by Gazeta do Povo and O Tempo

Key Facts The country Brazil, Latin America’s largest country, holds its presidential runoff on Sunday 25 October between President Lula and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro.

What happened On Thursday 22 October, the head of Brazil’s electoral court gave Meta 24 hours to hand over a technical report on a pro-Lula WhatsApp channel.

Who asked Flávio Bolsonaro’s campaign says the channel, with more than 8 million followers, manipulates online algorithms by mobilising supporters.

The window The order covers activity from 18 to 20 October, and Google was also asked about coordinated amplification.

Power Index Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 75.0 points (October 2026 edition).

Prediction markets Polymarket gives Flávio Bolsonaro a 77.8% chance of winning the 25 October runoff and Lula 22.5% (22 October, 4:50 p.m. ET). Polymarket puts Flávio Bolsonaro’s chance of winning at 78% and Kalshi at 79% (Lula: 23% and 22% ), as of 22 October, 5:20 pm ET ; prices are bets, not polls.

Still open Neither Meta’s answer nor any response from Lula’s campaign had been published when we checked.

Kassio Nunes Marques, president of Brazil’s electoral court (TSE), ordered Meta on Thursday 22 October to deliver a detailed technical report within 24 hours on the pro-Lula WhatsApp channel “Exército do Lula” (Lula’s Army). The order came after a request from the campaign of Flávio Bolsonaro, senator for Rio de Janeiro, according to Gazeta do Povo.

The order lands three days before the Brazil election 2026 runoff on Sunday 25 October, in which Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, Brazil’s president, faces Flávio. For readers in the United States, it shows how far the fight over social media, a main campaign battleground, now reaches into a court that controls the vote.

What the Electoral Court Ordered

Nunes Marques asked Meta, which owns WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook and Threads, for an urgent technical report, O Tempo reported. It must cover coordinated action, reach, interaction and sharing, and paid promotion, across Facebook, Instagram and Threads.

The Channel and the Campaign’s Complaint

“Exército do Lula” is a WhatsApp channel with more than 8 million followers, according to Gazeta do Povo. It is run by federal deputy André Janones, and earlier reports put its size far lower.

Flávio’s lawyers say the channel tells supporters to post hashtags at set times, repeat ready-made messages and run coordinated Google searches, O Tempo reported. One example they cite is a call to search for the phrase “Bolsonaro mandou matar Lula” (Bolsonaro ordered Lula killed), according to Gazeta do Povo.

How the Dispute Reached This Point

On Sunday 11 October, Nunes Marques ordered the channel blocked, but the same day Ricardo Villas Bôas Cueva, the court’s inspector-general (corregedor-geral), suspended that decision, Correio da Manhã reported. Today’s order asks for information, not a new block.

Our earlier reporting on the court’s handling of the case is in our explainer on the channel. This latest step moves the focus from one channel to the platforms that carry it.

What Prediction Markets Say

Polymarket bettors give Flávio Bolsonaro a 77.8% chance of winning the 25 October runoff and Lula 22.5% (22 October, 4:50 p.m. ET). The market has drawn about US$191.9 million in bets, and these are bets, not polls.

Kalshi, a market regulated in the US by the CFTC, prices a Flávio win by 3–6 points at 37% and by 0–3 points at 33% (22 October, 4:49 p.m. ET).

What It Means for US Readers

Meta and Google are US companies, and a Brazilian court is now asking them for evidence about how election content spreads. Their answers, due on Friday 23 October by the court’s own deadline, could shape how US platforms handle the final days before the vote.

Investors watching Brazilian assets can treat this as one more source of campaign noise, not a change in the vote count. The court has not accused anyone of wrongdoing; it has asked for data.

What Is Not Known

Neither Meta, Google nor Lula’s campaign had published a response when we checked. It is not known what the companies will hand over, or whether the court will act on it before Sunday.

The campaign’s claims of coordinated manipulation are allegations, not findings. On 12 October, the court’s own technical staff said they had not found the content the campaign cited among the channel’s posts from 2 to 11 October, CNN Brasil reported.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did Brazil’s electoral court order Meta to do?

It gave Meta 24 hours to deliver a technical report on the “Exército do Lula” WhatsApp channel. The report covers 18 to 20 October 2026.

Who asked for the order?

Flávio Bolsonaro’s presidential campaign asked for it. It says the channel manipulates online algorithms by mobilising supporters.

What is the “Exército do Lula” channel?

It is a WhatsApp channel with more than 8 million followers, run by federal deputy André Janones. Lula’s campaign treats it as an important tool.

Does the order block the channel?

No. It asks for information from Meta and Google. A block ordered on 11 October was suspended the same day by another judge.

When is Brazil’s runoff?

Brazilians vote on Sunday 25 October 2026. The choice is between President Lula and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro.

The numbers Flávio Bolsonaro has 53% of valid votes and Lula 47%, while raw totals read 50% to 45%, with a 2-point margin of error.

A new poll gives Flávio Bolsonaro, senator for Rio de Janeiro, 53% of valid votes against 47% for Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, Brazil’s president, ahead of the Brazil election 2026 runoff on Sunday 25 October. The Gerp polling firm published it on Wednesday 21 October at about 5 p.m. ET.

What the Gerp Runoff Poll Found

Gerp Mercadologia interviewed 2,400 voters by telephone from 19 to 21 October, with a margin of error of 2 percentage points and a 95% confidence level, Poder360 reported. The survey is registered with the TSE as BR-03835/2026 and was paid for by Gerp itself, Exame reported.

Who leads Brazil’s latest runoff poll?

Flávio Bolsonaro leads Lula 53% to 47% of valid votes in the Gerp poll published on Wednesday 21 October. Raw totals read 50% to 45%.

Gerp reports a margin of 2 percentage points at a 95% confidence level. It interviewed 2,400 voters by telephone from 19 to 21 October.

Brazilians vote on Sunday 25 October. The winner becomes president for a four-year term.

Valid votes leave out blank and spoiled ballots. Pollsters use them because the electoral court reports results the same way.

World.title: Sudan’s Leader Lifts Import Ban on Food
World.content:
Sudan’s Leader Lifts Import Ban on Food

SUDAN · ECONOMY

Published Thursday, 22 October 2026, 4:42 p.m. ET (10:42 p.m. Port Sudan) · Source: Radio Dabanga, Sudan Independent, Sudan’s Central Bureau of Statistics

Sudan’s army chief has ordered the lifting of a ban on imports of dozens of goods, including basic foods. On the same day, the dollar sold for 10,300 Sudanese pounds (about US$1 each) on the parallel market.

Gen. Abdelfattah al-Burhan, who leads the country’s ruling Sovereignty Council and commands its army, gave the order on Wednesday 21 October 2026, according to Sudan Independent and Radio Dabanga.

The move comes amid the Sudan war, which has broken supply chains and pushed prices up. Radio Dabanga counts 46 goods in the cancelled ban; that number comes from one outlet, and no official list has been published.

Key Facts — What happened Sudan’s army chief ordered an import ban on dozens of goods cancelled, Radio Dabanga reports.

— Who decided Gen. Abdelfattah al-Burhan, who heads the ruling Sovereignty Council and commands the army.

— The numbers Parallel-market dollar sold at 10,300 pounds (about US$1 each) on Thursday; annual inflation hit 28.29% in September.

— What next Importers want a formal written order; ministers have not yet published the list of freed goods.

— US readers The war’s economic strain shapes food prices and aid needs across Sudan.

In plain English Sudan had banned imports of goods the government called non-essential, to ease pressure on its weak currency. Importers said the ban emptied shelves and raised prices, so the army chief has now ordered it lifted.

What the Order Changes

Sudan Independent reports that flour, rice, pulses, cooking oils, vegetables and fruit can now enter without customs duties. Other goods that were banned return to ordinary customs procedures, it adds.

Finance Minister Jibril Ibrahim said the decision takes account of consumers’ hardship while protecting local producers. He made the remarks on Thursday 22 October.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Sudan Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Pound Slides, Prices Climb

Currency dealers sold the dollar at 10,300 Sudanese pounds (about US$1 each) on Thursday and bought it at 10,200, up 100 from Wednesday, Radio Dabanga reports. This is a street rate, not an official central bank price, and traders expect further rises.

Our earlier report covers the pound’s fall past 10,000 to the dollar.

Sudan’s Central Bureau of Statistics says annual inflation reached 28.29% in September, up from 26.14% in August. Monthly inflation was 7.5%.

Food and drink prices rose 36.81% over the year. Urban inflation stood at 40.35%, against 21.18% in rural areas.

Importers Want It in Writing

The National Importers’ Chamber welcomed the move but wants Prime Minister Kamil Idris to issue a clear, enforceable decision cancelling Resolution No. 74, which introduced the restrictions. Its chairman, El Sadiq Jalal El Din Saleh, said the ban disrupted markets and caused substantial losses to importers.

Radio Dabanga reports that traders and consumers saw some prices fall right after the announcement. Economists quoted by the outlet blame inflation on wartime damage to production, reliance on imports, the weak pound and the use of the customs dollar, the exchange rate used to calculate import duties.

What It Means for US Readers

Cheaper and more available food imports could ease some pressure on households in a country where the war has cut farming and trade. Our guide to Sudan’s hunger crisis explains how aid groups are responding.

For companies and charities shipping goods into Sudan, the key question is how customs will treat cargo while the written order is pending. Dealers’ dollar rates also show how fast the pound is weakening.

What Is Not Known

It is unclear whether the order legally overrides Resolution No. 74 without a written cabinet decision. The list of 46 goods has not been published, and officials have not said whether the duty-free treatment is permanent.

The reports do not say how the duty-free list relates to the 46 goods, and the exact time of the order is not reported. It is also unclear if prices will keep falling, since the dollar is still rising.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did Sudan’s government decide?

Sudan’s army chief and Sovereignty Council chairman, Gen. Abdelfattah al-Burhan, ordered a ban on imports of dozens of goods cancelled. Radio Dabanga puts the number at 46; a list has not been published.

Which goods are now duty-free?

Sudan Independent reports that flour, rice, pulses, cooking oils, vegetables and fruit may enter without customs duties. Other goods return to ordinary customs procedures.

Is the ban legally cancelled yet?

Not fully, say importers. Their chamber wants Prime Minister Kamil Idris to issue a written order cancelling Resolution No. 74, which introduced the ban.

Why does the dollar rate matter?

Sudan imports many basics, so a weaker pound raises shop prices. Dealers sold the dollar at 10,300 Sudanese pounds (about US$1 each) on Thursday, up 100 from Wednesday.

How high is inflation in Sudan?

Sudan’s statistics bureau puts annual inflation at 28.29% for September, up from 26.14% in August. Food and drink prices are up 36.81% on a year earlier.

Sources: Radio Dabanga, 22 October 2026; Sudan Independent (Arabic), 22 October 2026.

BRAZIL · ELECTIONS

Published Thursday, 22 October, 4:22 PM ET · Source: Brazil’s electoral court (TSE) ruling, reported by Metrópoles

Key Facts The country Brazil, Latin America’s largest country, elects its president in a runoff on Sunday 25 October.

What happened On Thursday 22 October, a judge of the electoral court (TSE) refused to halt government WhatsApp messages to pensioners.

The messages Sent on Wednesday 21 October, they say that voting also counts as proof of life for the social security agency INSS.

The dispute Flávio Bolsonaro’s campaign argues the texts may push people over 70, who are not required to vote, to the polls.

Power Index Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 75.0 points (October 2026 edition).

Prediction markets Polymarket puts Flávio Bolsonaro’s chance of winning at 78% and Kalshi at 79% (Lula: 23% and 22% ), as of 22 October, 6:00 pm ET ; prices are bets, not polls.

Still open The campaign’s wider lawsuit over the use of public communication channels is still pending.

Brazil’s electoral court (TSE) on Thursday 22 October rejected a request by Flávio Bolsonaro, senator for Rio de Janeiro, to suspend federal government messages that tell pensioners voting counts as proof of life. The ruling leaves the texts in place three days before the Brazil election 2026 runoff, as Metrópoles reported.

Brazil Election Data Room Runoff poll average: Flávio Bolsonaro 50.9 %, Lula 49.1 % 36 national polls from 20 pollsters since 4 October, updated hourly. Every poll, free to download. Open the Data Room · Download the CSV · Embed the chart

Minister Ricardo Villas Bôas Cueva, the court’s electoral inspector-general, wrote that the messages look informative and name no candidate. They reach beneficiaries of the INSS, the national social security agency that pays pensions to millions of Brazilians.

What the Government Messages Say

The messages came from the official GovBR WhatsApp profile on the night of Wednesday 21 October. They tell beneficiaries that voting also counts as proof of life, Metrópoles reported.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Brazil ranks 1st of 14 with 75.0 points. Strongest pillar: military means (100); weakest: state capacity & security (56). Alignment group: Hedging. WatchRating below investment grade (BB); public debt at 93% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Proof of life is the check that a pensioner is still alive, so that payments are not made in error. A 2022 rule lets the agency use electoral records for this check, and people it cannot identify may get a notice on WhatsApp or in the Gov.br app mailbox.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Brazil Elections 2026 Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Why Flávio’s Campaign Went to Court

The campaign of Flávio Bolsonaro, the conservative challenger, asked the TSE to stop messages about social programmes and public services, including the INSS proof of life. It says the texts can also work as a nudge to vote, especially for people over 70, for whom voting is optional.

In the filing, the campaign accused President Lula, Vice President Geraldo Alckmin and Communications Minister Sidônio Palmeira of using public infrastructure to help the re-election bid, according to Metrópoles. Lula, formally Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, is the incumbent president and is seeking a new term.

How the Judge Ruled

Cueva said a blanket suspension would be too broad and could cut off public information, including health guidance and benefit notices. He said a suspension could keep people from relevant information about public services.

The dispute adds to a run of cases before the court, including the fight over big WhatsApp channels and a Cueva decision that restored one such channel in October. The latest Brazil election polls show a tight race.

What It Means for US Readers

For investors in Brazilian stocks, bonds or US-listed Brazilian shares, legal fights this close to the vote add one more source of headline risk. The ruling is a first decision, so the legal question is not closed.

For readers following US politics and trade, Brazil’s next president sets the tone with Washington for four years. Rules on what a government may tell voters are a recurring test in tight elections everywhere.

What Is Not Known

The ruling answers a preliminary request, and the case itself is not decided. It is not known whether the campaign will appeal or what the full court will say after the defence replies.

No data show whether the messages changed turnout among older voters. Any effect on the 25 October result is unproven.
