World.title: US dollar exchange rate against Iraqi dinar remains stable in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar against the Iraqi dinar remained stable on Thursday in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, and declined in the capital of Iraqi Kurdistan, Erbil.

The US dollar exchange rate remained stable in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,695 Iraqi dinars throughout the day.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,700 Iraqi dinars and 1,690 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate slightly declined, fluctuating between 1,694 and 1,693 Iraqi dinars.

US dollar exchange rates rose noticeably in the Baghdad and Erbil markets on October 7, following a cabinet’s decision to revalue the official rate of the local currency, causing turbulence and instability in the parallel market.

Iraq officially depreciated its national currency, with the baseline dropping from about 1,300 Iraqi dinars to 1,500 dinars per US dollar.

The Iraqi cabinet approved the structural adjustment, which marks a 14.5 percent decline compared to the previous official framework that had been in place since early 2023.

Following the announcement, parallel market rates in Baghdad and Erbil soared, with exchange shops reporting market gains of more than 1,700 Iraqi dinars per US dollar.

World.title: Gulf Keystone says Iraq’s Hamrin oilfield has 7 billion barrels of oil
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – CEO of Gulf Keystone Petroleum Jon Harris said on Wednesday that the firm believes that Iraq’s Hamrin oilfield has seven billion barrels of oil, of which 0.5 billion to one billion barrels are recoverable.

Harris told Reuters that the oilfield currently produces 20,000 barrels per day, and by the end of 2028, output is expected to reach 60,000 barrels per day.

This week, Gulf Keystone Petroleum and ShaMaran Petroleum have reached a merger agreement, becoming one of the top private oil producers in Iraqi Kurdistan.

According to a statement from the corporation, the all-share acquisition is worth $601 million.

As of October 19, shareholders of ShaMaran, who are listed on Euronext, will receive 0.075 shares of Gulf Keystone for each share of ShaMaran they own, reflecting a premium of 23 percent.

The agreement integrates operations in the four Iraqi fields of Hamrin, Sarsang, Atrush, and Shaikan.

If drilling begins next year, the Shaikan oilfield in Iraqi Kurdistan is likely to increase its gross output from around 45,000 bpd to over 90,000 bpd by 2030, according to Harris.

Harris anticipates that the corporation will take advantage of other possibilities in Iraq, such as stake sales on US assets in the country.

World.title: Iraq, UAE discuss options to de-escalate regional tensions
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein and UAE’s Foreign Minister Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan discussed on Wednesday options to de-escalate tensions in the region.

During a phone conversation, the two sides discussed bilateral relations between the two countries, reaffirming the depth of the bonds that bind them together as well as a shared commitment to strengthening and expanding these ties, according to a statement released by the Iraqi Foreign Ministry.

The discussion addressed the outcomes of the 52nd session of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation’s (OIC) Council of Foreign Ministers, which took place in Baghdad on October 17–18. Both parties emphasized the importance of leveraging these achievements to enhance communication, foster unity, and encourage collaborative Islamic initiatives.

Along with regional developments, the discussion included approaches to foster a peaceful understanding that helps reduce tensions and improve security and stability in the region.

Hussein said on Sunday that Baghdad is attempting to arrange a meeting between Iran and the Gulf States as part of diplomatic efforts to reduce tensions and advance regional stability.

There are ongoing discussions between Iraq, the Gulf countries, and Iran aimed at bringing their viewpoints closer together, according to Hussein.

“We are trying to organize a meeting in Baghdad between Iran and the Gulf States,” Hussein said, without specifying a date or the degree of representation expected.

The proposal comes amid regional tensions that severely impacted maritime shipping and security in the Arabian Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz.

World.title: Iraq’s Fly Erbil gets Air Operator Certificate
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq-based airline Fly Erbil announced on Thursday that it had obtained an Air Operator Certificate (AOC) by the Iraqi Civil Aviation Authority (ICAA)—a milestone the company says paves the way for a new phase of development and the expansion of its flight network.

The airline said in a statement that obtaining the license is a result of years of diligent work by its management and employees in different divisions.

Fly Erbil reaffirmed its commitment to safety and security requirements, as well as the regulations of the aviation sector.

The company mentioned that the step supports the development of air transport in both Iraqi Kurdistan and throughout Iraq.

The airline plans to broaden its flight network by adding more Iraqi cities and introducing new destinations both regionally and globally. Additionally, it aims to enhance its services to comply with international standards and meet travelers’ expectations.

The Iraqi Kurdish airline based at Erbil International Airport emphasized that obtaining this certification marks the beginning of a new phase in its journey.

World.title: Iraq signs seawater deal with ExxonMobil
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Oil announced on Wednesday that the state-run Basra Oil Company (BOC) and US-based ExxonMobil signed a memorandum of understanding for the second phase of an Iraq seawater supply project.

On the sidelines of a ceremony held to sign the agreement, Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair said that the second phase of the seawater project is designed to support oil fields and maintain reservoir pressure.

With a capacity of up to 2.5 million barrels per day, this initiative complements a separate project currently being carried out by France-based TotalEnergies, which has a capacity of five million barrels per day.

The project is part of the Iraqi government’s approach to attract foreign firms to develop the country’s oil industry, ensure the sustainability of operations, and increase production rates, according to Khudair.

The development highlights Iraq’s appealing investment climate for implementing promising projects.

Khudair confirmed on Saturday that US firms are showing increasing interest in entering the Iraqi market and developing the country’s oil resources and petroleum industry.

The oil minister clarified that the Iraqi government supports US corporations’ involvement in the Iraqi market, citing their significant expertise in the oil sector, as well as their ability to transfer knowledge to Iraqi staff.

Several American companies are operating in Iraq, including oil services and consulting firms such as Halliburton, Schlumberger, Baker Hughes, and KBR, according to Khudair. He indicated that the ministry reached agreements with Chevron, ExxonMobil, and ConocoPhillips.

World.title: Iraq plans to purchase 10 large oil tankers
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is moving toward the acquisition of supertankers to bolster its capacity for transporting and marketing crude oil globally—a strategic step intended to reduce transportation costs and enhance financial returns from crude exports.

The Iraqi Ministry of Oil is considering the purchase of 10 oil tankers as part of its efforts to develop its export infrastructure and expand options for delivering shipments to global markets.

The step is part of the government’s efforts to strengthen the role of the Iraqi Oil Tankers Company (IOTC) and leverage the ownership of maritime transport assets, which would provide greater flexibility in marketing crude oil and managing shipments.

The plan is considered crucial given Iraq’s desire to improve the terms of its oil sales and reduce the discounts associated with certain existing marketing and transportation arrangements.

In a televised statement, Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair revealed that the ministry is considering the purchase of 10 supertankers, with an estimated total cost of $2 billion, according to Attaqa News.

According to Khudair, the projected fleet will have a total capacity of 10 million barrels since each tanker has a capacity of around one million barrels.

Owning these tankers would increase export earnings; estimates indicate that Iraq might save between 30 percent and 40 percent on the losses it presently suffers from price reductions.

The Ministry of Oil has more alternatives than only direct procurement; it is also considering proposals from specialist companies to establish joint ventures for the supply of oil tankers.

According to Khudair, one of the suggestions is specialized businesses funding the acquisition of tankers in exchange for a portion of the revenues made from the vessels’ operations, with the price paid over a period of three or four years.

Direct procurement is still a possibility, and the Iraqi government has said that it supports this approach.

World.title: Iraq’s Diwaniyah refinery undergoes major $800 million expansion project
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – An oil refinery expansion project in Iraq is making tangible progress, as part of the country’s efforts to reduce its reliance on imported fuel and increase the value of its crude oil.

The Al-Barham Group (ABG) is carrying out an $800 million expansion project at the Diwaniyah refinery in Iraq.

This project is one of several refinery expansion initiatives that Iraq is pursuing, including those in al-Amarah, Muthanna, Kirkuk, and Qayyarah.

The refinery manager projected in September 2025 that monthly revenues would reach approximately $35 million once the expansion is complete.

The Diwaniyah refinery expansion is progressing steadily toward the operational phase. An atmospheric distillation unit with a capacity of 70,000 barrels per day will bring the refinery’s total production capacity to 90,000 barrels per day—more than four times its current capacity—according to the British magazine Middle East Economic Digest (MEED).

The Iraqi government signed the expansion deal in February 2025. The Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) declared that the contractor will start moving equipment on-site within days after securing the required finance.

In July 2025, work officially commenced at the site, with the Ministry of Oil establishing a five-year timeline for the project’s completion.

In addition to the main distillation unit, the project includes a liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) processing unit with a capacity of 180 tons per day, a naphtha hydro-treating unit with a capacity of 18,000 barrels per day, a gasoline upgrading unit with a capacity of 10,000 barrels per day, a naphtha isomerization unit with a capacity of 8,000 barrels per day, and a loading terminal with a capacity of 90,000 barrels per day.

The project also includes a power generation plant, a nitrogen plant, a water pumping and purification station, an industrial wastewater treatment plant, and 24 storage tanks for crude oil and petroleum products.

Beside high-quality gasoline, the refinery will produce naphtha, kerosene, red diesel, fuel oil, and LPG, supporting Iraq’s objective of achieving self-sufficiency in petroleum products.

World.title: Iraq’s customs revenues hit record high in September
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s General Authority of Customs has announced a revenue increase of over $72 million in September 2026 compared to the same month in 2025.

The authority said in a statement that total customs revenues rose from $222.8 million in September 2025 to $294.8 million in September 2026—a growth rate of approximately 32.34 percent.

The rise reflects the importance of developing the customs operational system and enhancing the efficiency of revenue collection in accordance with applicable laws and regulations, according to the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

The authority indicated that it is implementing a plan to enhance institutional performance, improve customs operational procedures, and increase the efficiency of revenue collection.

The measures are designed to protect public funds, strengthen the state’s financial resources, support financial reform, and promote the growth of non-oil revenues.

In January, head of the authority’s valuation department, Ahmed al-Akeedi, said that the deployment of the ASYCUDA system and the new customs tariff will improve earnings.

Al-Akeedi said that Iraqi customs revenues reached $1.9 billion in 2025, an unprecedented milestone in Iraqi customs history and an exceptional achievement.

Revenues are predicted to grow by at least four to six times with the application of the ASYCUDA system and complete compliance with customs rates, perhaps exceeding $7.63 billion by the end of 2026, according to al-Akeedi.

World.title: Will back all meaningful efforts for Ukraine peace, PM Modi assures Poland's Tusk
World.content:
PM Modi with Polish counterpart Donald Tusk at Hyderabad House Thursday.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Looking to further expand their strategic partnership, India and Poland agreed to double bilateral trade by 2030 and announced dialogue mechanisms for defence industrial collaboration and counterterrorism cooperation as PM Narendra Modi hosted his counterpart Donald Tusk for talks Thursday.Modi and Tusk expressed deepest concern in a joint statement over the war in Ukraine, including its tragic humanitarian consequences and the impact on Global South. In his media statement, Modi assured Tusk that whether it is Ukraine or West Asia, India will continue to support every meaningful effort for peace.Poland views the war in Ukraine as a direct threat to its national security and sovereignty due to its shared border, influx of refugees and the threat of future Russian aggression in eastern Europe.âThey reiterated the need for a comprehensive, just and lasting peace in line with international law, consistent with the purposes and principles of the UN Charter, including respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity,â said the joint statement. The leaders also noted the negative impacts of the war on global food and energy security, especially for the Global South.Modi and Tusk, the first Polish PM to visit India in 16 years, also backed an MoU under negotiation for cooperation in critical minerals.Modi said the friendship between India and Poland was based not only on diplomatic ties but also on a shared heritage of humanity and empathy. He recalled how, during the Second World War, the royal families of Jamnagar and Kolhapur had provided shelter in India to thousands of Polish children and families. He also thanked Poland for helping India evacuate Indian students from Ukraine shortly after the Russia-Ukraine war began in 2022.Modi said the world was passing through a period of uncertainty and change, and even in such times, both India and Poland were emerging as important hubs of growth, technology and innovation.âToday we have agreed to deepen ties in defence, space and nuclear energy. In all these strategic sectors, we invite Polish companies to engage in co-development and co-production with India,â he said.He also announced a startup bridge to facilitate cooperation in IT, Artificial Intelligence and critical technologies.âBoth India and Poland believe in democratic values and the rule of law,â Modi said, underlining that both sides considered reforms essential to make global governance institutions more empowered.The two countries agreed that the UN needed structural reforms, including expansion of UNSC in both permanent and non-permanent categories, to remain relevant, credible and effective. In the joint statement, Poland expressed support for Indiaâs membership of a more inclusive, reformed and expanded UNSC, as well as its candidature for a non-permanent seat on the council for 2028-29.Modi and Tusk unequivocally condemned terrorism, including cross-border terrorism, and stressed that there could be no justification for terrorism on any grounds.âThey condemned in the strongest terms the terrorist attack in J&Kâs Pahalgam on 22 April, 2025. They called for strong and concerted action against terrorists and terrorist entities, including those designated by the UNSC 1267 sanctions committee,â said the joint statement.Defence and security cooperation was a major focus, with the leaders underlining importance of an Agreement on Mutual Protection and Exchange of Classified Information and expressing expectation it would be signed soon.They proposed a defence industry dialogue to develop a âforward-looking framework for defence industrial cooperationâ, including business-to-business engagement and, where mutually agreed, partnerships in technology, co-development, co-production and other forms of collaboration.

World.title: From Jan 1, WhatsApp, Telegram won’t work without SIM cards, govt issues guidelines
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India has made SIM binding mandatory from Jan 1, 2027, and the move will mean that messaging apps like WhatsApp and Telegram will not work without a SIM card in the smartphone.

The department of telecom has issued guidelines requiring messaging platforms to integrate the accounts with live SIMs used for registration by Dec 31, 2026. If the SIM is removed, replaced or deactivated, the appâs functionality will stop until a valid SIM is reinserted.

The move is to curb cross-border cyber frauds, phishing, digital arrest scams using Indian mobile numbers and enhance telecom cyber security.

Apple has updated iOS with a software patch to help detect when an iPhone is operating without a physical SIM card to abide with the rules. It is learnt Signal has not yet responded to govt notices.

From Jan 1, messaging services to be used will have to ensure a registered SIM card is installed in a device. This is likely to impact users of WhatsApp or Telegram over Wi-Fi without registered SIMs. And also those who use more than one device or frequently change their SIM cards.





Last Nov, DoT had issued the rules after finding âthat some app-based communication services utilising Indian mobile numbers for identification of its customers allows users to consume their services without availability of the underlying subscriber identity module (SIM) within the device in which app-based communication services is running. This feature is being misused to commit cyber-frauds especially from outside the country,â a statement read.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

To curb this menace, many govt agencies had been asking for SIM binding to be made mandatory. Subsequently, DoT issued directions to major app-based communication services, under the Telecom Cyber Security (TCS) Rules, 2024. These include WhatsApp, Telegram, Snapchat, Arattai, Sharechat, Jiochat and Signal.

Now, app-based communication providers will have to ensure that their service is âcontinuously linked to the SIM card (associated with mobile number used for identification of customers/users or for provisioning or delivery of services) installed in the device, making it impossible to use the app without that specific, active SIM.â And also ensure that âweb service instance of the mobile app, if provided, shall be logged out periodically (not later than six hours) and allowing the facility to the user to re-link the device using QR code.

â

World.title: Govt plans colour-coded driving licence for Indians, foreigners
World.content:
NEW DELHI: In a first, govt has proposed mentioning the nationality of driving licence holders on DLs and introducing separate colour schemes for Indian andforeign nationals as well as doing away with affidavits sworn before an executive magistrate or notary as proof of age and address, which has the potential of being misused.

Life insurance policies, too, would no longer be accepted as proof. Proposing sweeping changes to the driving licence (DL) regime under Motor Vehicles Rules, the road transport ministry Wednesday issued a draft notification to raise the pass mark for the online safe-driving tutorial assessment from the current 60% to 75%.

It has also proposed making it mandatory for licences to carry the holderâs blood group, mobile number and emergency contact details.

The ministry has proposed waiving fees for specified DL services, including changes to address, name and contact number, if applicants avail themselves of these services through online Aadhaar authentication.

Govt plans colour-coded DLs for Indians, foreigners

At present, if an applicant cannot produce any of the 12 listed documents, the licencing authority âmay accept an affidavit sworn before an executive magistrate, judicial magistrate or notary public as proof of age and addressâ.





Anil Chhikara, an expert in motor vehicle licencing, said, âThe use of simple affidavits is being phased out after miscreants used them to register false addresses and dates of birth. Applicants must now provide verifiable documents.

â

Under the draft, the ministry has listed separate sets of documents for proof of address, age and identity. Address proofs include Aadhaar card, Electoral Photo Identity Card, e-ration card, electricity or gas bills for the preceding three months, and proof of legal presence for foreign nationals.

Acceptable age proofs include passports, school board mark sheets, birth certificates and identity cards issued by govt departments.

Aadhaar, passports, e-ration cards and PAN have been listed as acceptable identity proofs.

The proposed changes aim to curb the submission of false documents, tighten assessment requirements and make licence-related services more accessible. They also seek to streamline online DL services and set timelines for processing applications to change licence particulars.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Under the proposal, the safe-driving tutorial would have to last at least 30 minutes, while the higher qualifying score of 75% is intended to make the assessment more stringent. Licencing authorities would have to approve or reject online applications to change DL particulars, including name and address, within 15 days, giving reasons for rejection.

An application for a change of address that remains undecided for 30 days would be deemed approved. The draft also proposes a consolidated application form for services such as DL renewal, issuance of duplicate licences, addition of a vehicle class and changes to personal particulars. Specified applicant details would be retrieved electronically from the Sarathi portal wherever available.

World.title: Centre flags data gap, regulatory hurdles in curbing hospital mark-ups
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Amid SCâs scrutiny of hospitals charging patients steep mark-ups on medicines and consumables, govt officials have flagged gaps in data and regulatory hurdles in extending price controls to hospital supplies, saying the Centre first needs to establish the extent of margins before considering intervention.

The Union govt has told the SC in its affidavit that margins on hospital consumables can range from 100% to 1,000% or more, highlighting concerns over the high mark-ups patients often face on supplies used during treatment. However, a senior official told TOI that the govt does not have the data needed to assess margins across hospital supplies and determine whether wider controls are warranted.

âWe first need to get the data and then examine whether there is a margin and a need to control it,â another senior official said, explaining that the purchase price of medicines and consumables would need to be compared with what hospitals charge patients before deciding on any intervention.

Centre fixes ceiling prices for scheduled medicines and has limited annual price increases for non-scheduled drugs up to 10%. It has decided to cap trade margins on certain anti-cancer medicines at 30% of MRP. Extending similar controls to other medicines and hospital consumables, officials said, would require analysis and consultation.

A health ministry official, however, raised doubts about how far the govt could regulate hospital billing, saying hospitals, with health being a state subject and governed by the Clinical Establishments Act or other laws enacted by state govts..





The Centreâs role, the official said, is largely confined to drug-price regulation through the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority.

Regulating individual components of hospital bills would be difficult, the official said, pointing out that hospitals charge package rates without providing detailed itemised bills. Restricting charges on consumables could lead profitconscious hospitals to raise other fees, including surgeonsâ charges, the official argued.

The official also disputed the blanket use of the term âoverchargingâ when hospitals bill patients at the MRP, saying there is no general legal requirement to offer discounts below the printed price. They cited delayed reimbursements from insurance firms and govt health schemes as financial pressures on hospitals that would need to be factored in while deciding any broader intervention.

World.title: Movie glorifies violence, generalises graft in medical field: IMA

NEW DELHI: Indian Medical Association has written to I&B ministry to urgently review the promotional content of Sunny Deol-starrer âSuryaa â Ant Se Aarambh Takâ, alleging that it generalises corruption in the medical profession and depicts violence against healthcare workers in ways that could erode public trust and put doctorsâ safety at risk.In a letter, dated Oct 22, to I&B minister Ashwini Vaishnaw, IMA national president Dr Anilkumar J Nayak sought an impartial review of the promo video for the upcoming film and appropriate corrective measures from its makers. It also called for a ban or other action if justified under applicable law. The letter was also copied to the Union health and home ministries and the chairperson of National Medical Commission.IMA flagged what it described as the risk of portraying corruption and unethical practices as representative of the medical fraternity. While stressing that individual wrongdoing must be investigated and punished, it said the actions of a few should not tarnish the reputation of doctors as a community.It expressed concern over scenes depicting physical assaults on doctors, nurses and hospital staff, particularly when such acts appear heroic or justified.It warned that such portrayals could normalise violence against healthcare professionals, who already face safety challenges in hospitals.The letter said such depictions could fuel mistrust between patients and doctors, weakening the cooperation essential for treatment and healthcare delivery. It also warned that such negative portrayals could demoralise medical students and discourage young people from entering the profession.IMA said that while it respected freedom of creative expression, the same should be exercised responsibly when healthcare worker safety and public confidence in essential services are at stake.

World.title: Don’t blindly follow foreign custody order: Supreme Court
World.content:
Supreme Court

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

As cases of estranged NRI couples fighting for child custody increasingly result in cross-border litigation, with one spouse getting a favourable order from a foreign court while the other moves an Indian court, Supreme Court has said courts here must make an independent assessment of what is good for the child and the ruling of the foreign court should not be automatically followed, though it must be accorded proper consideration.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K V Viswanathan said cases already dealt with by foreign courts were coming before it time and again and their adjudication was not easy as they involved deeply emotional and sensitive issues. It added that the welfare of the child âmust be understood in the widest sense, not by money or physical comfort aloneâ.âThis position rests on two foundations. The first is that once the court is seized of the matter, it exercises its parens patriae jurisdiction. That jurisdiction obliges it to consider and assess the matter for itself, through the lens of the childâs welfare. The second is that the decision in such cases turns not on the legal rights of the parties but on the welfare of the child. The same emphasis on welfare over legal entitlement runs through our statutes on custody and guardianship. They make clear that a person otherwise entitled to custody or guardianship need not be granted it if that would not be for the welfare of the child.There is thus no ambiguity in the fact that an order of a foreign court must yield to the welfare of the child,â the bench said.âPut differently, a court in this country, when exercising its jurisdiction, cannot blindly follow the order of a foreign court and act merely as an executing court,â the apex court bench said.SC said a parentâs disobedience of a foreign court order did not, by itself, require the Indian court to give automatic effect to that order and also that the paramountcy of the childâs welfare did not mean that the order of the foreign court had to be disregarded. âIn deciding what the welfare of the child requires, the court must form its own independent judgement. In doing so, however, it must give proper weight to the order of the foreign court,â the bench said.SC passed the order while directing that a seven-year-old girl, a US citizen, who was brought to India by her mother in breach of a California custody order, return to US.A California court had in 2022 granted the couple joint custody of the child and specifically barred her removal from California without written consent or a court order. In violation of the ruling, the mother left for India with the child after two weeks, leading to the father starting legal proceedings against her in India.SC allowed the petition of the father, who approached the court through advocate Prabhjit Jauhar, against a Karnataka HC order dismissing his plea. After hearing both sides, it said the welfare of the child lay in her continuing to reside in US.

World.title: Tibet earthquake LIVE | At least sixteen dead, 32 injured after 7.0 quake strikes Tibet: China's state media
World.content:
Sixteen dead, 32 injured after strong 7.0-magnitude earthquake struck China’s Tibet region late Thursday (October 22, 2026), and casualties have been reported, state news agency Xinhua said, citing local authorities.

The epicentre of the quake, which struck at 10:33 p.m. (1433 GMT), was located in a mountainous area about 190 kilometres (120 miles) east-northeast of Nagqu, and 390 kilometres northeast of the regional capital Lhasa, the U.S. Geological Survey said.

Search and rescue efforts continued following the collapse of at least 339 homes, the Nagqu media office said, citing city government officials. Among the injured, 11 people were in serious condition and the other 21 sustained minor injuries, the media office said.

It struck at a shallow depth of 10 kilometres. A level-II earthquake disaster emergency response was activated in the area, Xinhua said earlier.

The epicentre was located in Maru township in Baqen county. Township deputy head Lhawang Dagpo said the quake was clearly felt at the township office, which sustained cracks in the walls, according to Xinhua.

World.title: BJP President Nitin Nabin on a three-day visit to Jharkhand from October 23
World.content:
The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) National President Nitin Nabin will be on a three-day visit to Jharkhand starting October 23. He will participate in the inaugural session of the Jharkhand BJP State Working Committee meeting, which will begin on October 24.

The state unit of the BJP has finalised all arrangements for his visit, and there is great enthusiasm among party workers regarding the National President’s visit. State capital, Ranchi, has been decorated with BJP flags, banners and his cutout to welcome him.

Jharkhand BJP State President Aditya Sahu on Thursday (October 22, 2026) held a meeting with party office-bearers at the state office to review the preparations for the National President’s visit and his welcome.

The meeting was attended by State Vice-Presidents Balmukund Sahay and Rakesh Prasad; General Secretary (Organization) Pawan Sai; State General Secretaries Ganesh Mishra, Amar Kumar Bauri, and Manoj Singh and others.

State General Secretary Amar Kumar Bauri said that it will be Nitin Nabin’s second visit to Jharkhand, the sacred land of ‘Dharti Aaba’ Bhagwan Birsa Munda—since assuming the role of National President. He added that party workers are particularly enthusiastic about his visit.

Mr. Bauri mentioned that the Mr. Nabin is scheduled to reach Ranchi Airport at 7:00 PM on October 23 and arrangements have been made to welcome him with traditional Jharkhandi customs, including the playing of drums and a shower of flower petals.

“Party workers will also welcome him at various locations across the capital. During his stay, he will attend the inaugural session of the State Working Committee meeting on October 24, where he will provide key guidance to party office-bearers and workers,”Mr. Bauri said.

A senior leader of the Jharkhand BJP asserted that during his visit, he will hold meetings with senior state-level leaders Members of Parliament (MPs), Members of the Legislative Assembly (MLAs), and party workers to discuss the future strategy. The BJP leader added that these meetings will serve to review the organization’s ongoing work, and roadmap for upcoming political and organisational activities.

The meeting scheduled for October 25 will focus on key issues such as strengthening the organization, ensuring the active engagement of party workers at the booth level, and effectively disseminating information about the central government’s schemes to the general public.

“Discussion is also likely to take place on ‘Mission 2029’, the next assembly election in Jharkhand. Potential candidates for the Giridih by-election will also be discussed, “the BJP leader said.

Giridih assembly seat has fallen vacant after the death of Jharkhand Mukti Morcha (JMM) MLA Sudviya Kumar.

World.title: ‘Indian architecture has critical markers for all generations’
World.content:
A Kochi-based student of architecture won the 28th Charles Correa Gold Medal in architecture in Mumbai on Thursday (October 22, 2026). His project, ‘Energy Commons: Reimagining energy infrastructure as a place for civic engagement,’ reimagined essential energy infrastructure as a civic resource, transforming a conventionally restricted space into a place of shared public life. Radhakrishnan M.S. is a student of Seed APJ Abdul School of Environmental Design in Kochi.

The Charles Correa Gold Medal, initiated in 1998, recognises outstanding undergraduate architectural thesis projects that engage meaningfully with the challenges of the built environment. The award ceremony was held at Tarq Gallery in Mumbai ON Thursday (October 22) evening.

“Through this year’s theme of ‘Equitability through Design’, young architects explored questions of access to space, shelter, infrastructure, and the commons. We hope that this theme becomes a touchstone for the students to return to throughout their career and professional lives,” Nandita Correa Mehrotra, Director of the Charles Correa Foundation, said.

Book release

‘The State of Architecture — Practices and Processes in India, A Research Framework’, a book on inquiry into the practice of architecture in the Indian subcontinent, was also released at the event. It led to conversations around architectural pedagogy, public engagement, and complex issues affecting architecture. The book also looks into how large-scale economic, social, cultural, political and ecological changes impact architecture. It has been published by Architecture Foundation India.

Speaking about the theme of the book, co-author Ranjit Hoskote said that for architecture to be relevant, it has to correspond to the greatest good of the greatest number. “Equity and solidarity have been key themes for us in the book. There is no way to think about architecture without foregrounding these key questions of power, participation and possibility,” he said.

The State of Architecture process has looked into the issues of caste, gender, environment, and equity. It also looks at how architecture meets the urgencies of the changing times, changing the ground rules. Speaking about the changing nature of architecture, co-author Rahul Mehrotra said that liberalisation was a clear marker for architecture in India. He gave insights into how coalition politics and the strengthening of regional parties led to greater pluralism and diversity in architecture.

The event began with a panel discussion on the book, the thought process behind it, and its impact. It was moderated by cultural theorist Nancy Adajania. Rahul Mehrotra, Ranjit Hoskote, and Kaiwan Mehta provided a historical perspective on architecture, discussing the impact of architectural exhibitions on public engagement. This was followed by the Charles Correa Gold Medal award ceremony, where the winners presented their theses. Manu Viswam E from Trivandrum’s College of Architecture received an honourable mention for his project “Urban Scar to Social Commons.” It explored how urban fabric can be stitched together to create a more inclusive city. It grounded equality in the reclamation of a disused industrial landscape as shared civic ground.

World.title: Congress MLAs burn Punjab CM effigy over poor law-and-order following anti-drugs crusaders murder
World.content:
The Punjab Assembly on Thursday (October 23, 2026), during the obituary references, paid tributes to anti-drug crusader Parvinder Singh Jhota, who was shot at in Punjab’s Mansa, even as, before the commencement of the session, Congress MLAs led by the leader of the Opposition, Partap Singh Bajwa, burned the effigy of Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann, demanding his resignation, outside the Punjab Assembly complex.

Mr. Bajwa said the Chief Minister, who also holds the Home portfolio, has completely failed to maintain law and order in the State. The broad daylight murder of Jhota, who raised his voice against the drug menace, is a glaring example of the government’s failure.

Outside the Assembly, speaking to journalists, Mr. Bajwa said “It is the voice of the entire Punjab that law and order has completely ended in Punjab. No person’s life is safe in this State, no one’s business is safe, no one’s work is safe, no one’s family is safe. So, we are asking for Bhagwant Mann’s resignation.”

Separately, Punjab Bharatiya Janata Party president Kewal Singh Dhillon hit out at the State government, accusing it of running away from its accountability. “This was evident from the fact that the Punjab Assembly session today lasted only a few minutes, during which neither Punjab’s concerns were discussed nor were any deliberations held on the issues facing the State,” he said in a statement.

Mr. Dhillon added, “The government will have to answer on issues surrounding the drug menace, gangsterism, extortion and the deteriorating law-and-order situation. The people of Punjab are demanding answers from the AAP government regarding the deaths of Parminder Singh Jhota, Bikramjit Singh, Gulzar Singh and others, who lost their lives for raising their voice against drug menace.”

Mr. Dhillon said that Home Minister Amit Shah had reiterated his commitment to eliminate drugs from Punjab at their roots and had also asserted that an NDA government would be formed in Punjab. “This meant that the BJP would form the government in 2027 in Punjab,” he said.

World.title: Russia ready for talks on plans for final Ukraine deal, not truce: Putin
World.content:
Russia is ready to resume three-way talks with Ukraine and the United States, but on the security parameters of a final peace deal and not a "short" ceasefire, President Vladimir Putin said Thursday (October 22, 2026).

"The goal of these discussions will be to address the issue of ensuring security for both Ukraine and Russia... within the framework of a final agreement, not after some kind of short pause in fighting," President Putin told a reporter from state TV.

World.title: Bihar Council elections today; Patna Graduates’ seat in focus as JD(U) faces internal tussle
World.content:
Ahead of Friday’s biennial elections to eight seats of the Bihar Legislative Council, State JD(U) president Umesh Kushwaha and party MLC Sanjay Kumar Singh on Thursday met Patna Graduates’ seat candidate Neeraj Kumar for a closed-door meeting.

The seat, from which Mr. Neeraj is seeking a fourth consecutive term, has become the centre of attention after JD(U)’s Mokama MLA Anant Singh declared support for Jan Suraaj Party (JSP) candidate Anuj Kumar Singh.

Mr. Anant claimed that Mr. Neeraj had opposed him in every Assembly election held in Mokama.

Polling for the four Graduates’ and four Teachers’ constituencies will be held from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Counting is scheduled for October 27. The terms of the sitting MLCs are set to expire on November 16.

The ruling allies BJP and JD(U) are contesting four seats each while the JSP is contesting all eight.

Bid to placate

The JD(U) twice tried to broker peace between Mr. Anant and Mr. Neeraj. It had tasked Munger MP and Union Panchayati Raj Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh to mediate. Mr. Lalan later said Mr. Anant had “reservations and grudges which the party should have addressed earlier”.

Former Chief Minister Nitish Kumar, Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary and Deputy Chief Minister Vijay Kumar Sinha had visited Mr. Neeraj after he was admitted to a private hospital on Monday for heart-related issues.

“I am not aware of what is going on for the election as my workers have taken the mantle on my behalf. I will go and find out,” Mr. Neeraj said after he was discharged on Wednesday.

World.title: Legal action ordered against officials over irregularities in voter list in Pilibhit
World.content:
Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) on Wednesday (October 23, 2026) ordered legal action against officials responsible for discrepancies in the electoral rolls of the Pilibhit Assembly Constituency, where searching certain voters’ EPIC numbers online displayed details of other electors.

“Legal action will be taken against both the current and former election officials responsible for the discrepancies found in the voter list for constituency 127 – Pilibhit. In addition to the legal action being taken against the two voter registration officials, instructions have also been given to initiate departmental action. The computer support staff will be terminated. The District Election Officer, Pilibhit, has received a detailed report regarding a complaint concerning the display of the EPIC number of one voter in the voter list of Assembly constituency 127 (Pilibhit), indicating the details of another voter,” reads an official statement by the State election commission.

According to the investigation report, the computer operator of the voter registration centre for Assembly Constituency 127 – Pilibhit, entered a total of 13,779 Form-8s between May 31, 2026, and August 29, 2026, to update voter details. Of these, a total of 4,717 forms were entered between July 16, 2026, and the remaining 9,062 forms were entered between July 17, 2026, and August 29, 2026. No Form-8s corresponding to any of these entries were found in the office records. A total of 10,470 Form-8s were approved, while 3,309 were rejected. This revealed discrepancies in 10,470 of the entries,” says the official statement.

The Election Commission of India has directed that the computer operator at the voter registration centre in 127-Pilibhit and the election registration officers (EROs) assigned to the Pilibhit constituency for the period between July 16, 2026, and July 17, 2026, be held responsible for the irregularities in the voter registration process.

“The commission has instructed that legal action be taken against them under Section 32 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, and relevant sections of the Indian Penal Code. Furthermore, the commission has directed a thorough investigation into the role of the relevant assistant election registration officers in this case, with a report to be submitted. The District Election Officer, Pilibhit, has been instructed to direct the computer assistants at voter registration centres to conduct a thorough review of all Form 6s and Form 7s submitted for voter registration and deletion, respectively, between April 10, 2026, and October 21, 2026, and to provide a detailed report within one day. In addition, all discrepancies found in Form 8 entries are being addressed according to established procedures and standards,” added the official statement.

The Congress on Wednesday (October 21) alleged large-scale manipulation of electoral rolls in the Pilibhit Sadar Assembly constituency, claiming that the names of 13,150 voters were changed while their EPIC and serial numbers remained the same. The party accused the Election Commission for the manipulation.

World.title: At least sixteen dead, 32 injured after 7.0 quake strikes China’s Tibet: State media
World.content:
Sixteen dead, 32 injured after strong 7.0-magnitude earthquake struck China’s Tibet region late Thursday (October 22, 2026), and casualties have been reported, state news agency Xinhua said, citing local authorities.

The epicentre of the quake, which struck at 10:33 p.m. (1433 GMT), was located in a mountainous area about 190 kilometres (120 miles) east-northeast of Nagqu, and 390 kilometres northeast of the regional capital Lhasa, the U.S. Geological Survey said.

It struck at a shallow depth of 10 kilometres.

A level-II earthquake disaster emergency response was activated in the area, Xinhua said earlier.

The epicentre was located in Maru township in Baqen county. Township deputy head Lhawang Dagpo said the quake was clearly felt at the township office, which sustained cracks in the walls, according to Xinhua.

Houses were reported collapsed in the area, the agency said. Power and telecoms services were disrupted in the county seat.

Workers have been sent to the area to coordinate the response, and local officials were carrying out checks of nearby villages, the report said.

Earthquakes in China are relatively common. In January 2025, at least 126 people were killed in an earthquake in Tibet’s rural Tingri county.

World.title: PM vows to bring back progress to KP, assails PTI's 'callousness' during its tenures
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday vowed that the federal government, which now runs Khyber Pakhtunkhwa under governor’s rule, would make every effort possible to “bring back” progress to the province.

He made the remarks while chairing a meeting of the apex committee in Peshawar, where he arrived earlier in the day on his first visit to the province since the imposition of governor’s rule and the declaration of emergency on Oct 11.

The meeting, attended by Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir and KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi, reviewed KP’s overall security situation. Federal ministers and newly appointed provincial advisers were also present.

Addressing the committee, PM Shehbaz reiterated that emergency and governor’s rule had to be imposed “under extreme compulsion”.

“I promise that we will leave no stone unturned in bringing back the happiness and era of progress to this province, and in the practical realisation of the wishes, aspirations, and dreams of this province’s people that have been shattered due to the worst actions of recent years,” he said.

The prime minister affirmed that the Centre “will place all possible resources at your feet”.

He added that himself, the Advisory Council led by the governor, the president and the CDF “will ensure that this province, once again, not only matches the other provinces in the race for development, but I would be extremely happy if it moves even further ahead”.

The prime minister regretted that “terrorists were summoned back here” after peace had been established, “washing down all sacrifices down the drain”.

“There can be no greater enmity with the country than not honouring and respecting such sacrifices, not holding them in esteem,” he remarked, highlighting that young soldiers left their homes and families to defend their country.

The premier called for an “all-encompassing analysis as to why this happened”, adding that there was “no worse callousness, criminal negligence, and hostility towards the national interest than this”.

He said: “All issues of the people were pushed aside — whether it is education, healthcare, or protecting the lives and property of the people — and [having] matters with terrorists instead. I believe that no other example can be found of such hostility against the country, in terms of their attitudes, detachment, and callousness.”

PM Shehbaz asserted that 5,000 police vacancies were not filled, Safe City projects were yet to be completed, the capacity of the Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) had not been enhanced significantly, and neither were special measures taken regarding police training.

He recalled that all provinces had agreed at the time of the 2010 National Finance Commission Award that KP, being the front-line region in combatting terrorism, needed ample resources.

“From 2010 to today, more than Rs800 billion in funds have either already been provided or are being provided under this,” he stressed.

“However, not only did it resurface, but the weapons needed to counter terrorism, the required capacity, and the trained officers needed were nowhere to be found.”

While saying he would not go into the details, the prime minister emphasised that he had assured the provincial governments of ex-chief ministers Ali Amin Gandapur and Sohail Afridi of the Centre’s full support in the fight against terrorism.

“But nothing was done regarding this,” he regretted, adding that the government could not remain a “silent spectator” when a “party was stooping to such enmity against the country” and the economy and society were being destroyed.

“Therefore, on this occasion we made this one last effort,” the premier said, referring to the province’s interim handover to the federal government under governor’s rule.

Highlighting the Centre’s efforts to stabilise the economy over the past two and a half years, PM Shehbaz remarked, “It wouldn’t have been possible [without] unprecedented partnership between political and military hierarchy.”

He said the federal government could not remain a silent spectator when “terrorists were roaming around dancing in all areas of KP, and were ruling over some areas in the evening, and collecting extortion” at a time when the stabilisation of Pakistan’s economy was being acknowledged globally.

The prime minister recalled the breakdown of the Oct 3 talks between the Centre and reiterated that his government was “compelled to make this decision” of imposing governor’s rule.

PM Shehbaz remarked that the province was “shattered with wounds due to the circumstances created in the past several years”.

He highlighted the poor law and order situation over the past six years, recalling that security forces and law enforcement agencies had made sacrifices to establish peace in KP.

The premier said there was corruption of Rs100bn in the clean drinking water of the Cities Improvement Project and Rs37bn in the “infamous looting” in the case of the Kohistan District Accounts Office.

He said that “80,000 people were martyred and the [economy] suffered a loss of several hundred billion dollars. Only then, in 2018, was peace completely restored in this country”.

Describing the province as “very beautiful”, the premier expressed his hope that the government “work hard day and night and speedily make it progress towards development and prosperity”.

“This is the province that is the first extremely strong wall of the homeland,” he noted.

Centre announces Rs160bn uplift funds, other measures

PM Shehbaz later also attended a meeting of the Area Representative and Development Council (ARDC) constituted for 12 districts of KP, which face serious security challenges. CDF Munir was also present on the occasion.

The council covers Dera Ismail Khan, Tank, Lakki Marwat, Bannu, Bajaur, Mohmand, Khyber, Kurram, Orakzai, North Waziristan, South Waziristan Upper and South Waziristan Lower. It includes 48 elders and prominent personalities from those districts to ensure local representation.

Addressing the ARDC, the prime minister announced that the federal government would provide KP with Rs160bn for development projects.

Furthermore, to address the wheat shortage in the province, he said the Centre would provide KP “as much wheat as is needed” from the storages of Pakistan Agricultural Storage and Services Corporation (Passco).

“However, there should be no hoarding. And whatever price the Centre provides wheat at, the common man should get wheat at that very price,” the premier emphasised.

He went on to assure the ARDC that the federal government will provide “whatever assistance” in operations and resources is needed to fight terrorism. He also said directives have been issued to bolster the CTD and complete Safe City projects.

PM Shehbaz also asserted that any difficulties in the completion of the federal government’s projects in KP will be resolved, adding that the governor-led administration will address problems in provincial projects.

The prime minister appreciated the tribal elders for always supporting Pakistan unequivocally and said the ARDC now had an “immense responsibility”.

Noting the remarks of ARDC Chairman Shaukatullah Khan, PM Shehbaz said: “He stated that development work is zero, corruption is 100 per cent, and terrorism is at its peak. I completely agree with him.”

The premier referred to weaknesses in the police’s performance, stating that arrests in cases of theft and robbery were not made.

Mentioning examples of corruption, such as the Kohistan scandal, he said: “You will feel great pain and sorrow over how the province’s resources were looted. God willing, this will be fully controlled, and every single penny of your development and prosperity will be delivered to your doorstep.”

Police’s vehicle procurement ban relaxed: Kundi

Separately, in a bid to improve the police’s capabilities amid the current law and order situation in the province, Kundi said he has approved the relaxation of the police’s vehicle procurement ban to ensure personnel have the necessary resources.

In a post on X, Kundi said that in line with the prevailing security landscape in the province, he approved the relaxation of the ban.

“Our [KP police] force stands on the front lines to protect the lives and security of our people,” he wrote.

“In the prevailing law and order situation, ensuring that our officers have the vehicles and resources they need is essential to an effective response to security challenges.”

Kundi added that the restrictions would be loosened “within the approved scope and against funds already allocated in the Police Procurement Plan”.

“This will strengthen operational capacity without placing any additional burden on the provincial exchequer,” he noted.

“Supporting our police is not just a responsibility; it is an investment in the safety of our people and the peace of KP.”

In July this year, the KP government had imposed a ban on the procurement of vehicles except for ambulances; earth-moving machinery; fire trucks; tractors; trucks; buses; passenger vans; prisoner vans; motorcycles; water tankers; rescue and recovery vehicles and boats; and mobile laboratory vehicles, according to an order issued by the KP finance department.

“In case of [an] essential requirement, the chief minister, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, may relax the ban on [a] case-to-case basis,” the order, seen by Dawn, read.

Development of merged districts a ‘special priority’

In his address to the apex committee, the KP governor termed establishing peace and stability in KP a “collective priority”, and stressed that it was in the interests of the entire country.

Referring to the federal government’s decision to impose emergency and governor’s rule in KP, Kundi said that the peaceful transition showed that the people of the province wanted peace and stability.

“I want to pay tribute to my people who showed restraint despite the turmoil,” he said, asserting there had been no untoward incident in the region following the measures.

On Oct 14, three days after emergency was imposed, a protest demonstration by PTI workers in Khyber’s Bara tehsil turned violent as protesters clashed with police. Injuries to party workers and cops were reported in the incident.

Speaking at the meeting, Kundi also paid tribute to those who sacrificed their lives in the war against terrorism, including personnel of the police, army, Frontier Corps, and Federal Constabulary.

“These sacrifices demand a more effective strategy to combat terrorism,” he underscored.

The governor reiterated that the foremost priority of his KP Advisory Council was to restore peace and eliminate terrorism.

Kundi termed the development of the merged districts a “special priority”.

“The people of these regions have paid a heavy price during this fight against terrorism. Now, they deserve better education, health, and economic opportunities,” he declared.

“The federal government’s cooperation in establishing peace and stability in the province is very significant,” the PPP leader highlighted, saying he was keen to play his role in this collective endeavour.

The governor maintained that the people of KP would not have to choose between peace and development. “This is our collective responsibility to provide people with both.”

Kundi declared that the KP Advisory Council would keep playing its role in integrating these merged areas in the circle of national development.

“The public’s trust is the only metric of measuring our success in the war on terror,” he asserted, while reaffirming that the whole network of terrorism would be annihilated, and the facilitators and financiers of terrorists would also be targeted.

“I seek constant support and supervision by the federal government,” he asked, expressing the hope that the Centre would continue its cooperation.

Emergency amid security challenges

The Centre had imposed emergency and governor’s rule in KP on Oct 11, citing the PTI-led provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism. The decisions were also endorsed by the Parliament last week amid protests by the opposition.

Governor Kundi, along with Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, had chaired a meeting of the provincial apex committee a day after governor’s rule was imposed.

In the meeting, the governor — who is now in charge of running the province — assured Naqvi he would enforce all policies of the federal government and work together with the security forces for peace and prosperity of the province.

Kundi asserted that under the new set-up, tackling terrorism would be the priority.

Later that day, Kundi, addressing a press conference, called for greater coordination between the Centre and the province, stressing that policies on counterterrorism will “come from Islamabad [..] not Kabul,” in an apparent jibe at the PTI-led KP government, which has been accused of maintaining a “nexus” with terrorist groups by federal ministers.

The Centre’s move to impose governor’s rule and emergency in KP also followed a mobilisation drive and protest march by the PTI and in opposition at the Centre, to demand the release of its jailed founder, Imran Khan.

Intense negotiations between the two sides a week before the imposition of governor’s rule had failed to yield any results, with counterterrorism policy being one of the main reasons behind the breakdown of their talks.

The PTI said it was being left out of security decisions concerning KP, which the Centre denied . It also called for reviewing the counterterrorism policy, while the latter criticised the KP government’s efforts to combat terrorism in the province and objected to its stance on dialogue with the Afghan Taliban.

Soon after, the Centre also authorised the deployment of Pakistan Army troops and assets in aid of civil power in KP.

Federal ministers have also alleged that the PTI-led government in KP had a “nexus” with terrorist groups, stating that the province’s security situation necessitated the imposition of emergency there.

Additional input by Irfan Raza

World.title: Govt reduces petrol price by Rs1.60 per litre, raises high-speed diesel rate by Rs1.64
World.content:
The government on Thursday decreased the price of petrol by Rs1.60 per litre, but raised that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs1.64.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs377.71 per litre while HSD will cost Rs391.75 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices are applicable for Oct 23 (Friday).

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm and fuel allocations for official vehicles has been cut by 50 per cent for three months.

On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Punjab MPA Hina Parvez Butt defends deleted X post on alleged CCD encounter amid criticism
World.content:
Punjab lawmaker Hina Parvez Butt on Thursday defended herself after a social media post by her regarding an alleged encounter by Punjab’s Crime Control Department prompted outrage and criticism.

On Wednesday, a suspect accused of running over a teenage boy who worked for him with his car in a private housing society in Multan, was killed in an alleged encounter in Bahawalpur. The killing of the teenager, Waseem, had sparked anger among the public, with a police officer saying the he had been “subjected to barbarity”.

“This is [Punjab Chief Minister] Maryam Nawaz sahiba’s government; justice is served immediately,” Butt subsequently wrote on X, sharing screengrabs of a TV report regarding the alleged encounter. She later deleted the post after it was widely panned for “celebrating extrajudicial killings”.

In a video statement posted on X on Thursday, Butt said: “I posted a tweet in which I said, ‘This is Maryam Nawaz Sharif sahiba’s government; justice is served immediately’. This was my personal opinion and creating propaganda on this was uncalled for.”

She said that the post was meant to express the “feelings of an ordinary citizen”. She asserted that she did not “blame” the chief minister, the Punjab government or talk about any institution. She said that criticising her for this was “uncalled for”.

She also took exception to remarks by Punjab Information Minister Azma Bokhari, saying that she “respectfully disagreed”.

On Wednesday night, Bokhari had appeared on Geo News programme ‘Aaj Shahzeb Khanzada Ke Saath’, where she was asked about Butt’s post.

The Punjab minister said that Butt had a habit of saying things without thinking them through, which caused problems for her and become a “source of embarrassment for the government”.

Referring to the remarks, Butt said: “None of my actions or words have ever harmed or embarrassed the Punjab chief minister or the government. If Azma Bokhari sahiba is feeling embarrassed, that is her personal choice.

“I don’t feel that anyone should be embarrassed [at] anything I tweeted on my social media account. Azma Bokhari is the [Punjab] government’s official spokesperson, so obviously she clarified the government’s policy, which is good. But, I think her remarks on me were unnecessary and uncalled for,” she said.

“So I would again, respectfully, disagree with her,” she said.

Referring to recent incidents involving minors and the youth in the country, she said that their parents should be called on shows and asked how those who subjected their offspring to “savagery” should be treated.

“I believe I have stated public sentiment and what is the people’s voice. Those coming forward to defend the culprits do not meet the families whose children’s bodies are recovered in a bad state. I meet such parents,” he said.

“So any person who has even a bit of humanity in their heart, what will they have felt when they heard about Waseem from Multan?” she asked.

The CCD, established last year, has been criticised by human rights advocates and civil society members for a high number of casualties.

The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) alleged earlier this year that the CCD has adopted a “deliberate policy of staged police encounters leading to extrajudicial killings”.

World.title: Pakistan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye to meet European trio in Istanbul
World.content:
Turkiye will host an R-4 and an R-4+E-3 meeting of foreign ministers in Istanbul on October 23, the Turkish foreign ministry said on Thursday.

The R-4 group, which comprises Pakistan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye, emerged in March and has been focusing on regional security and mediation efforts between the United States and Iran.

The E-3 group is a trio of European powers — France, Britain and Germany — that was set up more than 20 years ago to advance diplomatic coordination over Iran’s nuclear programme.

The Foreign Office in Islamabad has yet to comment on the planned meetings and Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar’s participation.

A Turkish diplomatic source told Reuters that the seven countries would meet in the R-4+E-3 format for the first time at Turkiye’s initiative as wars involving Iran, Yemen and Ukraine threaten shipping routes and regional security.

The ministers are expected to discuss the Israeli-Palestinian issue, the latest situation in the Strait of Hormuz, developments related to Yemen, efforts to end the Russia-Ukraine war, and opportunities for closer cooperation between the regional and European countries, the source added.

Fidan is expected to emphasise the need for a diplomatic solution to the war between the United States and Iran, the importance of freedom of navigation in the straits of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab, and reiterate Turkiye’s support for Saudi Arabia’s security against attacks by Yemen’s Houthi rebels under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement signed by Islamabad, Ankara, and Riyadh, they said.

Fidan will also tell counterparts that Turkiye has been working to stop the war in Ukraine from spreading to the Black Sea, pointing to the regional security risks posed by the conflict, the source said.

World.title: England's Brook hits record ODI double ton but Sri Lanka pull off epic chase in Rawalpindi clash
World.content:
England’s Harry Brook smashed the fastest double-century in One-Day International (ODI) history and became the first Englishman to score 200 in the format but Sri Lanka sealed a two-wicket win in their tri-series clash with one ball to spare in Rawalpindi on Thursday.

The 27-year-old captain rewrote the record books by racing to his double hundred in 114 balls, surpassing the previous mark of 117 deliveries set by India’s Shubman Gill.

In the process, Brook also eclipsed England’s highest individual ODI score of 182, held by all-rounder Ben Stokes.

Brook’s scintillating performance ended with the final ball of England’s innings when he was caught by Sahan Arachchige off the bowling of Janith Liyanage.

England’s captain Harry Brook celebrates after scoring a double century (200 runs) during the one-day international (ODI) tri-series cricket match between England and Sri Lanka at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium in Rawalpindi on October 22, 2026. — AFP

He made 202 from 116 deliveries, peppering the Sri Lanka attack with 21 fours and 10 sixes before departing to warm applause from the crowd.

The defeat leaves England bottom of the standings after losing both their matches, with Brook saying they need to win their next two games to reach the final in Lahore.

“Unfortunately, it (the record) doesn’t matter now. I thought we were going to be in a good position but, unfortunately, it doesn’t even count,” Brook said.

“Heart-breaking. I think you’ve hit the nail on the head there. It’s very disappointing that we haven’t been able to defend 430, but that’s life, that’s cricket,” he added.

“You don’t see many teams chase down 430 and hats off to Sri Lanka. They’ve played exceptionally well. We couldn’t execute our skills enough with the ball and, again, they’ve just played an absolute blinder there.

“We’ll have a good chat about it now and over the next couple of days. We’ve got a good opportunity in the next couple of games to really try and get to that final in Lahore.”

Joe Root provided strong support with 69 off 66 balls as England piled up 429-4.

But the total proved insufficient as Sri Lanka completed the second-highest successful run chase in ODI history.

Pavan Rathnayake top-scored with 130 from 106 deliveries, while opener Avishka Fernando and Dasun Shanaka both fell three runs short of centuries.

Sri Lanka’s Pavan Rathnayake in action in the one-day international (ODI) tri-series cricket match between England and Sri Lanka at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium in Rawalpindi on October 22, 2026. — Reuters

Needing six runs from the final two deliveries, Sri Lanka sealed victory when Liyanage launched Josh Tongue over long-off for six, leaving Brook’s record-breaking innings all in vain.

Tongue was England’s most successful bowler with 3-79.

England lost by 87 runs at the same venue in Rawalpindi on Tuesday to Pakistan, who lead the table with two wins from two.

World.title: 4 cops including DSP martyred, 2 terrorists killed during exchange of fire in KP's Karak: police
World.content:
LAKKI MARWAT: Four policemen, including two officials, were martyred and two terrorists were killed during an exchange of fire in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Karak district on Thursday, police said.

A statement by the KP police said law enforcers had initiated a search and strike operation in the Charpara area at noon, where terrorists had set up a blockade on Wednesday night.

Banda Daud Shah and Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) deputy superintendents of police (DSP) led the operation, in which bomb disposal unit (BDU) personnel, a drone team, Rescue 15 personnel and Rapid Response Force personnel also participated, the statement said.

“During the operation, the law enforcers raided the hideout of a terrorist commander, Qaiser Iqbal, where an exchange of fire took place,” the police said, adding that two terrorists were killed in the encounter.

CTD DSP Imranuddin Khan, Latambar Station House Officer (SHO) Sub-Inspector (SI) Afzal Awan, Constable Kazim and Head Constable Amjad from the BDU were martyred in the exchange of fire.

The statement said the operation was ongoing.

It added, “The brave martyred personnel of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Police have set a shining example of dedication to duty, courage, and a commitment to public safety by sacrificing their lives in the fight against terrorism.”

The statement said the sacrifices of the martyred policemen reflected the police force’s “unwavering resolve” to continue making every possible effort to eradicate terrorism and establish lasting peace in the region.

Later, the funeral prayers for the martyred police personnel were offered with full official honours.

According to the KP police, the funeral was attended by KP Inspector General of Police (IG) Zulfiqar Hameed, CTD Additional IG Jawad Qamar, Kohat Regional Police Officer Shakir Hussain Dawar, Kohat Commissioner Parvez Khan Sabt Khel, CTD Senior Superintendent of Police (Operations) Najamul Hasnain, Karak Deputy Commissioner Hamid Iqbal and Karak District Police Officer Niaz Muhammad, among other high-ranking civil and military and police officers, the families of the martyred personnel, and others.

A police contingent presented a final salute to the martyrs, while high-ranking officers paid tribute to them by laying floral wreaths on their coffins.

“The attendees honoured the supreme sacrifices offered by the martyrs, prayed for the elevation of their ranks, and sought patience for the bereaved families,” the police statement added.

Police officers pay tribute to the martyred police personnel during funeral prayers in KP’s Karak on Oct 22. — photo courtesy KP police

KP IGP Hameed paid tributes to the bravery, sense of duty, and professional commitment of the martyrs. He stressed the great courage of the KP police personnel in laying down their lives while confronting terrorists.

“The martyrs’ bravery, unwavering dedication to duty, and unparalleled sacrifices for the protection of the public serve as a guiding light for the entire police force,” he added.

Earlier, KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi condemned the incident and expressed sorrow over the martyrdom of four police personnel.

“The sacrifices of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa police in the fight against terrorism are unforgettable. The blood of our martyrs will not go to waste; our resolve against terrorism will be further strengthened, and the struggle for the establishment of peace will continue,” he said in an X post.

KP has been witnessing terrorist attacks and security challenges for a long time, including attacks on police personnel.

Thursday’s operation comes around 20 days after several terrorist hideouts were destroyed during a joint search and strike operation in Karak.

In September, two terrorists were killed in an intelligence-based operation in Lakki Marwat, and in August, a police constable was martyred and six officials were injured when an improvised explosive device was used to attack a police patrol van.

According to a recent report from the Centre for Research and Security Studies, Pakistan recor­ded a sharp 83 per cent increase in violence-linked fatalities during the third quarter of 2026, re­­versing a declining trend reported in the first and second quarters as terrorism and counter-terrorism deaths surged nationwide.

Balochistan and KP remained the epicentres of violence, jointly accounting for 98pc of all fatalities during the period. Balochistan recorded 829 deaths, nearly 59pc of the national total, while KP reported 556 fatalities, accounting for more than 39pc.

World.title: Direct flights between Pakistan and Maldives on the horizon as PM stresses connectivity
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday announced that he had issued instructions for direct flights between Pakistan and the Maldives.

The premier was addressing the Pakistan-Maldives Business Forum, attended by visiting Maldivian President Dr Mohamed Muizzu, who arrived in Islamabad on Tuesday for a three-day trip at the invitation of PM Shehbaz.

The visit marks the first by a Maldivian president to Pakistan in 11 years, and comes as the two countries celebrate the 60th anniversary of their diplomatic relations, established in 1966.

PM Shehbaz said, “I want to say that connectivity is very important. We don’t have direct flights from Malé to Islamabad or Karachi, so this air link is very important.

“I have already given instructions to our ministry of civil aviation to prepare a quick feasibility [study], be it Pakistan International Airlines, or any other airline in Pakistan, to find the ways and means to take the first flight comprising tourists [and the] business community to Malé,” he announced.

The premier said he had been informed by President Muizzu that he gave instructions “to his airline to work out a quick plan to start flights from [the] Maldives to Pakistan”.

“I have given instructions to our civil aviation department to immediately invite a delegation from [the] Maldives and work out a plan whereby we can start these air flights between the two countries as early as possible,” PM Shehbaz added.

Moreover, the premier highlighted the importance of maritime connectivity, noting that unless there is a reliable direct shipping schedule from Karachi or Gwadar to Malé, “we will not be able to meet our targets efficiently and effectively.”

He added that once Muizzu returned to his country, a delegation of Pakistani government officials and businessmen would be sent to Malé. He said that the delegation would arrive within the next week or so.
